cases.question: Reconstruct the travel story as a sequence of actions, speakers, addressees, misunderstandings and replies. Which participants actually meet? Which speech is imagined, conditional or remembered? Keep story evidence separate from a generic together edge.

findings.claim: The story is told by the anonymous Gemara as a precedent ('like this case') for the rule just stated: people who mislead themselves are not being misled. It is a narrated incident, not a sage's own report or memory.

evidence.exact_quote: והא קמטעי להו אינהו הוא דקמטעו נפשייהו
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: But doesn't this mislead them? It is they who mislead themselves.

evidence.exact_quote: כי הא דמר זוטרא בריה דרב נחמן הוה קאזיל מסיכרא לבי מחוזא
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Like this: Mar Zutra son of Rav Nachman was going from Sikhra to Bei Mechoza

findings.reasoning: The segment opens with כי הא ד, the usual formula for citing an incident as support. No participant introduces it with 'I saw' or 'he told'. So the whole story sits in the narrator's voice; speech inside it is reported speech.
findings.graph_effect: Record one episode (a road encounter) with narrator = anonymous Gemara. Speech edges are reported speech inside a narrated story, not attributed teachings.

findings.claim: Sequence of movement: Mar Zutra was travelling from Sikhra towards Bei Mechoza. Rava and Rav Safra were travelling (as one party) towards Sikhra. The two parties met each other on the way. All three named men are physically present at the meeting.

evidence.exact_quote: הוה קאזיל מסיכרא לבי מחוזא ורבא ורב ספרא הוו קא אתו לסיכרא פגעו אהדדי
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: [Mar Zutra] was going from Sikhra to Bei Mechoza, and Rava and Rav Safra were coming to Sikhra; they met each other.

findings.reasoning: The verb for Rava and Rav Safra is a single plural (הוו קא אתו), so the text itself states that they travel together. The two parties go in opposite directions, and פגעו אהדדי ('they met each other') states the encounter. The ו between the Mar Zutra clause and the Rava clause joins two travel clauses; it does not make Mar Zutra and Rava companions.
findings.graph_effect: Rava + Rav Safra: co-travel (explicit, story evidence). Mar Zutra with Rava and with Rav Safra: road encounter (explicit meeting). These are story-specific relations, not a generic 'together' edge; in particular Mar Zutra and Rava were NOT travelling together.

findings.claim: The misunderstanding is narrated as Mar Zutra's own thought: he supposed they had come out towards him (to greet him). It is not speech and nobody said it to him.

evidence.exact_quote: הוא סבר לאפיה הוא דקאתו
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: He thought: it is towards him that they were coming.

findings.reasoning: סבר ('he thought, supposed') marks a belief. The text never says Rava or Rav Safra told him they came for him. Rashi, Tosafot and the codes all build on this: he misled himself.
findings.graph_effect: Do not create an 'honours / goes out to greet' edge from Rava or Rav Safra to Mar Zutra. At most store Mar Zutra's mistaken belief as a belief attached to the episode.

findings.claim: Speech 1: Mar Zutra speaks to both men together (plural addressee), in polite third person: why did the Rabbis trouble themselves to come so far?

evidence.exact_quote: אמר להו למה להו לרבנן דטרוח ואתו כולי האי
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: He said to them: Why did the Rabbis need to trouble themselves and come all this way?

findings.reasoning: אמר להו is plural 'to them'. לרבנן refers to his addressees respectfully in third person.
findings.graph_effect: Mar Zutra addresses Rava and Rav Safra jointly (one speech act, group addressee). If the graph stores pairwise address, both pairs derive from this single act and must not be counted as two independent observations.

findings.claim: Speech 2: Rav Safra alone answers Mar Zutra. He states a fact (we did not know you were coming) and a counterfactual (had we known, we would have troubled ourselves more). The extra effort is hypothetical: it never happened. Rava says nothing to Mar Zutra in the text.

evidence.exact_quote: אמר ליה רב ספרא אנן לא הוה ידעינן דקאתי מר אי הוה ידעינן טפי הוה טרחינן
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Rav Safra said to him: We did not know that the Master was coming; if we had known, we would have troubled ourselves more.

findings.reasoning: אמר ליה is singular 'to him', naming Rav Safra as speaker. אי הוה ... הוה is a contrary-to-fact conditional. Rashi explains the unstated purpose: they had gone out on their own business to go elsewhere.
findings.graph_effect: Rav Safra addresses Mar Zutra (reply, corrects a misunderstanding). The conditional 'would have honoured more' is imagined behaviour and supports no honour or deference edge. No Rava to Mar Zutra speech edge.

findings.claim: Speeches 3-5 (Chullin 94b:14, the next segment of the same story): Rava rebukes Rav Safra for upsetting Mar Zutra. Rav Safra objects that otherwise they would be misleading him. The closing line, 'he is misleading himself', rebuts that objection. The text does not say whether Mar Zutra heard this exchange.

evidence.exact_quote: אמר ליה רבא מאי טעמא אמרת ליה הכי דאחלישתיה לדעתיה
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Rava said to him: Why did you say that to him? You upset him.

evidence.exact_quote: אמר ליה והא קא מטעינן ליה איהו הוא דקא מטעי נפשיה
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: He said to him: But [otherwise] we would be misleading him! He is misleading himself.

findings.reasoning: The first speaker and addressee are explicit: Rava to Rav Safra. The reply's speaker is unnamed ('he said to him'), but it answers Rava, so it is Rav Safra. Where the speaker changes inside the reply is discussed in F7. Nothing in the text places Mar Zutra inside or outside this conversation.
findings.graph_effect: Rava addresses (rebukes) Rav Safra; Rav Safra replies to Rava; they disagree on conduct. Store as a conduct exchange inside the episode. Keep it separate from the co-travel edge. Mar Zutra is the topic (spoken about), not an addressee.

findings.claim: Who says the last line, 'he is misleading himself'? The William Davidson Aramaic and Wikisource texts have a single 'he said to him' covering both sentences. The Davidson English and Steinsaltz Hebrew (one editorial project) give the last line to Rava. The Rif's text of the story has a second explicit 'he said to him' before it. Petach Einayim also says Rava concludes and Rav Safra accepted.

evidence.exact_quote: Rav Safra said to Rava: But if I would not have said so we would have misled him. Rava responded: Mar Zutra misled himself,
אמר לו רבא לרב ספרא: אין זה נחשב שאנו מטעים אותו, שכן
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Rava said to Rav Safra: this does not count as our misleading him, since... [Steinsaltz Hebrew gloss]

evidence.exact_quote: אמר ליה והא קא מטעינן ליה אמר ליה איהו דקא מטעי אנפשיה
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: He said to him: But we would be misleading him! He said to him: He is misleading himself. [Rif]

evidence.exact_quote: ובסוגיין מסיק רבא שלא לומר ואיהו קמטעי נפשיה
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: In our passage Rava concludes that one should not say it, and 'he is misleading himself'.

evidence.exact_quote: ובסוגיין רב ספרא לא השיב לרבא ונראה שקבל דבריו
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: In our passage Rav Safra did not answer Rava; it seems he accepted his words.

findings.reasoning: The objection-then-answer shape (והא ... ! איהו הוא ...) and the codes that adopt 'he misled himself' as the rule support giving the answer to Rava. The Rif's added אמר ליה makes the change of speaker explicit, but it is one witness to the text and its parenthetical printing is unexplained (see S8 note). The Davidson English and Steinsaltz Hebrew come from the same editorial work and count as one voice, not two. Rashi (S4) and Rabbeinu Gershom (S6) gloss the phrases without naming speakers.
findings.graph_effect: Default: Rava has the last word (Rava to Rav Safra: 'he misleads himself'), as a reading branch, not settled text. Alternative branch: one reply by Rav Safra containing both sentences. No commentator I checked reads it that way, and the logic argues against it. The Rif witness supports the default and should be stored as a text variant, not as commentary.

findings.claim: Patronymic: Mar Zutra is called son of Rav Nachman. That is a father-child relationship shown in the name. Rav Nachman does not appear or speak in the story.

evidence.exact_quote: מר זוטרא בריה דרב נחמן
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Nachman

evidence.exact_quote: מר זוטרא בריה דרב נחמן הוה אזיל
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Mar Zutra son of Rav Nachman was going [Rif]

findings.reasoning: בריה ד is a plain 'son of'. The project rule keeps the kin relation and a local parent placeholder even though the parent never acts. Seder HaDorot (S14) files this story under 'מר זוטרא בר רב נחמן' with other passages. That is a later index, and it does not establish which Rav Nachman is meant or that every listed passage is the same man.
findings.graph_effect: Add local placeholder 'Rav Nachman (father of Mar Zutra, this passage)' and edge child-of: Mar Zutra -> Rav Nachman (literal kinship, from the name). Do not merge the placeholder with any historical Rav Nachman here. Identification is a separate decision.

findings.claim: Place-name variant: the Rif has Mar Zutra going to 'Bei Chozai' (לבי חוזאי), not 'Bei Mechoza'. It also has Rava and Rav Safra coming FROM Bei Chozai to Sikhra, and it lacks the narrated clause 'he thought they were coming towards him'.

evidence.exact_quote: הוה אזיל מסיכרא לבי חוזאי ורבא ורב ספרא הוו אתו מבי חוזאי לסיכרא פגעו אהדדי אמר להן
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: was going from Sikhra to Bei Chozai, and Rava and Rav Safra were coming from Bei Chozai to Sikhra; they met each other. He said to them... [Rif]

findings.reasoning: This is a variant in a secondary witness quoting the Gemara, not an emendation. It changes the geography but not who meets whom. I did not check manuscripts of the Bavli, so I cannot say which reading the manuscripts support.
findings.graph_effect: Store the destination as a text variant (Bei Mechoza / Bei Chozai). Do not derive a residence edge (for example 'Rava of Mechoza') from this story. Participants and encounter are unchanged across both versions.

findings.claim: Commentators agree that Rava and Rav Safra had not set out for Mar Zutra at all. Rashi: they had gone out on their own business. Ritva: they were going their own way, not towards him. Tosafot: here they did not come for him at all. That is how Tosafot tell this case apart from Ulla and Rav Yehuda's barrels on 94a.

evidence.exact_quote: ולעשות עסקינו ולילך למקום אחר יצאנו
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: We went out to do our business and to go elsewhere. [Rashi, explaining Rav Safra's words]

evidence.exact_quote: דרבא ורב ספרא לדרכן הוי הולכין ולא לקראתו
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Rava and Rav Safra were going on their way, and not towards him. [Ritva]

evidence.exact_quote: אבל הכא לא באו כלל בעבורו
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: But here they did not come on his account at all. [Tosafot]

evidence.exact_quote: שאני עולא דחביב ליה לרב יהודה דבלאו הכי נמי פתוחי מפתח ליה
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Ulla is different, since he was dear to Rav Yehuda, who would have opened them for him anyway.

findings.reasoning: The Tosafot question: Rav Safra said they would have made more effort had they known, so perhaps there was no real deception, as with Ulla. Tosafot answer that there the act was done for the guest; here nothing was. That answer depends on the meeting being accidental.
findings.graph_effect: Supports tagging the encounter as accidental or incidental. No planned visit or greeting. The Ulla / Rav Yehuda case belongs to a different episode (94a) and must not be merged into this one.

findings.claim: Commentators differ on why Rav Safra thought silence would mislead, and on what Mar Zutra knew. Ben Yehoyada infers that Rava and Rav Safra turned back and went with Mar Zutra to Mechoza; otherwise silence could not mislead. Rabbeinu Gershom glosses 'he misleads himself' as 'he knows we did not go out to meet him'. Rashi glosses it as 'since we did not tell him we came out to meet you'.

evidence.exact_quote: ועל כן מוכרח לומר דחזרו עמו למחוזא והביאוהו לביתם
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Therefore one must say they returned with him to Mechoza and brought him to their home. [Ben Yehoyada]

evidence.exact_quote: איהו הוא דקא מטעי נפשיה כלומר שהוא יודע דלא נפקינן לקדמותיה
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: He misleads himself: that is, he knows that we did not go out to meet him. [Rabbeinu Gershom]

evidence.exact_quote: אחרי שאנו לא אמרנו לו לקראתך יצאנו
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Since we did not tell him 'we came out towards you'. [Rashi]

findings.reasoning: Ben Yehoyada's accompaniment and hosting is an inference he makes to answer a difficulty. The text does not say it. Gershom's 'he knows' may mean 'he should know'; I cannot settle that from the gloss alone.
findings.graph_effect: Do NOT add 'accompanies' or 'hosts' edges from Ben Yehoyada's inference. Keep it as a commentary alternative attached to the episode.

findings.claim: A different, later-reported story about Rav Safra is related to this one but is not the same event. In it, Rav Safra goes out to stroll, a pious man thinks he has come to greet him, Rav Safra says he came out only to stroll, and his students question him. Petach Einayim cites it from Reshit Chokhmah and Seder HaDorot also reports it. Seder HaDorot thinks it is aimed at this Gemara but in a different form.

evidence.exact_quote: דרב ספרא יצא יום אחד לטייל ובא חסיד א"ל לרב ספרא למה טרח מר א"ל רב ספרא לא יצאתי אלא לטייל נתבייש אותו חסיד
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Rav Safra went out one day to stroll; a pious man came and said to Rav Safra: Why did the Master trouble himself? Rav Safra said: I only came out to stroll. That pious man was ashamed. [Petach Einayim, reporting Reshit Chokhmah]

evidence.exact_quote: וראה השינוי שיש
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: And see the difference there is.

evidence.exact_quote: ולדעתי כוונתו על גמרא זו אבל הוא בענין אחר
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: In my opinion he means this Gemara, but it is in a different form. [Seder HaDorot]

findings.reasoning: The cast differs (an unnamed pious man and students instead of Mar Zutra and Rava). So does the moral (Rav Safra defends his honesty with a verse rather than being corrected). I saw it only through these two later works, not in Reshit Chokhmah itself.
findings.graph_effect: No edges for Mar Zutra or Rava from this retelling. Do not identify the pious man with Mar Zutra or the students with Rava. If stored at all, it is a separate later-tradition episode about Rav Safra with unnamed participants.

findings.claim: The codes adopt the conclusion as an anonymous rule: if someone meets another on the road and the other thinks he came out to honour him, there is no need to tell him. The Prisha names this story as the source.

evidence.exact_quote: כגון שפגע בחבירו בדרך וסבור זה שיצא לקראתו לכבדו אין צריך להודיעו
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: For example, he met his fellow on the road and the other thought he had come out towards him to honour him: he need not inform him. [Shulchan Arukh]

evidence.exact_quote: כגון שפגע בחבירו בדרך כו' שם ע"ב מביא מעשה דמר זוטרא בריה דר"נ הוה קאזיל באורחא וזה נלמד ממנו
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: 'For example he met his fellow on the road...': there (94b) it brings the incident of Mar Zutra son of Rav Nachman going on the road, and this is learned from it. [Prisha]

findings.reasoning: The codified rule matches the closing line of F6/F7. That supports reading it as the Gemara's accepted conclusion, whoever says it. The Mishneh Torah text I fetched (S20) lists other examples of misleading people but not this road case. That is only a finding about that paragraph.
findings.graph_effect: Reception evidence only; creates no person-to-person edges. It may support the branch in F7 in which Rava's line is the conclusion.

findings.claim: Haggahot Ya'avetz proposes a later emendation of Rav Safra's words: 'לא הוה ידעי דקאתי מרב' should be read. I cannot tell from the gloss alone what exact change from the printed text he intends.

evidence.exact_quote: לא הוה ידעי דקאתי מרב
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: We did not know that ... was coming [his proposed wording; meaning of מרב unclear to this dossier]

findings.reasoning: This is a later proposed emendation, a different kind of evidence from a text variant. It concerns the wording of Rav Safra's reply, not who speaks or who meets.
findings.graph_effect: None on persons. Store as a proposed emendation on the wording, unresolved.

findings.claim: Parts of the English translation are editorial additions, not text. 'out to greet', 'Rava responded' and the unbolded 'Rava ... Rav Safra' addressee names do not appear in the Aramaic. The Davidson English and Steinsaltz Hebrew belong to one editorial project and are not independent witnesses.

evidence.exact_quote: Mar Zutra thought they were coming out to greet him.
הוא, מר זוטרא, סבר
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: He, Mar Zutra, thought [Steinsaltz supplies the name]

findings.reasoning: In this edition, bold marks the translated text and plain type marks explanation. Graph extraction from English must not treat the plain additions as source text.
findings.graph_effect: Anchor speaker and addressee decisions on the Aramaic. Where the Aramaic is implicit ('he said to him'), mark the name as resolved by context or by commentary.

corrections.change: Kind 'together' -> road encounter (met) plus Mar Zutra addresses Rava as part of a two-person group addressee. The name span should include the title מר ('מר זוטרא בריה דרב נחמן').
corrections.why: The ו in the pattern joins two opposite-direction travel clauses; Mar Zutra and Rava were not travelling together. Their contact is the explicit meeting (פגעו אהדדי) and the one plural speech (אמר להו). Rava never speaks to Mar Zutra in the story.

corrections.change: Kind 'together' -> co-travel (explicit, single plural verb), stored as story evidence. Add a separate conduct exchange from 94b:14: Rava rebukes Rav Safra, Rav Safra objects, and Rava answers on the default reading (F7).
corrections.why: 'Together' is correct here but loses what the story says. The rebuke and reply are a separate relation from travelling together, and the 94b:14 exchange lies just outside the focal segment.

corrections.change: Add missing pair Mar Zutra - Rav Safra: road encounter; Mar Zutra addresses both (shared act with the Rava pair); Rav Safra replies to Mar Zutra, correcting his mistaken belief.
corrections.why: Rav Safra is the only person who speaks to Mar Zutra, and the first-pass pairs miss this.

corrections.change: Add kin: Mar Zutra child-of local placeholder 'Rav Nachman (this passage)'. Direction: Mar Zutra -> father.
corrections.why: Patronymic בריה דרב נחמן is relationship evidence even though the father is absent from the story (project rule).

corrections.change: Do not add any honour, deference or greeting edge from Rava or Rav Safra to Mar Zutra.
corrections.why: The honour exists only in Mar Zutra's mistaken belief (סבר) and in Rav Safra's counterfactual ('if we had known ...'). Commentators agree they did not come for him.

lessons: Separate 'co-travel' (one party moving together) from 'encounter' (two parties meet). A generic 'together' blurs a story in which people moving in opposite directions meet.

Speech modality: store narrated belief (סבר), actual speech (אמר), counterfactual content (אי הוה ... הוה) and inferred-speaker lines as different modalities. A counterfactual about honouring someone is not an honouring event.
A plural address (אמר להו) is one speech act with a group addressee. Pairwise projections of it are not independent observations.
A person spoken ABOUT (Mar Zutra in 94b:14) is a topic, not an addressee.
Implicit speaker changes ('he said to him' covering two turns) should be saved as a reading branch with who-says-what, plus any textual witness (here the Rif) that makes the change explicit.
Commentary inferences about off-text actions (Ben Yehoyada's return to Mechoza) must not become edges.
Later retellings with a different cast (Reshit Chokhmah's pious man) are separate episodes; do not merge participants by role similarity.
Place variants in a story should not feed residence edges without separate evidence.

review.scope: Checked every graph-relevant finding, episode step and proposed correction against the saved sources (Davidson vocalized and unvocalized Aramaic, Wikisource, Davidson English, Steinsaltz, Rashi, Tosafot, Rabbeinu Gershom, Ritva, Rif, Ben Yehoyada, Petach Einayim, Haggahot Ya'avetz, Seder HaDorot, Prisha, Shulchan Arukh); fetched nothing new and did not check Bavli manuscripts, Reshit Chokhmah or any historical identification.

findings.target: F3 / episode step 4 (Mar Zutra's mistaken belief)
findings.reason: The printed Aramaic does narrate a belief: 'הוא סבר לאפיה הוא דקאתו'. But the Rif's quotation leaves that clause out, and the dossier quotes only part of Rabbeinu Gershom's gloss. In full it reads 'שהוא יודע דלא נפקינן לקדמותיה ואף על פי כן קאמר אמאי איצטער רבנן' ('he knows we did not go out to meet him, and even so he says why did the Rabbis trouble'). That reads as real knowledge, which fits a text without 'he thought'. So any belief attached to Mar Zutra should be tied to the printed reading, with Gershom and the Rif kept as a separate branch. It should not be stored as high-confidence across all witnesses. The 'no honour edge' decision holds on every branch.

findings.target: F6 / episode step 7 (addressee of Rava's rebuke)
findings.reason: F6 says 'The first speaker and addressee are explicit: Rava to Rav Safra.' Only the speaker is named: 'אמר ליה רבא' names no one after 'to him'. The addressee comes from the content. 'מאי טעמא אמרת ליה הכי' ('why did you say this to him') can only be aimed at Rav Safra, who had just spoken to Mar Zutra. The Davidson English adds 'Rav Safra' in plain, unbolded type, which F15 itself counts as an editorial addition. Keep Rava → Rav Safra at high confidence, but record the basis as 'resolved from context', not 'named in the text'.

findings.target: F7 / F9 / reading.md 'Where the sources differ' (status of the Rif)
findings.reason: The dossier calls the Rif both 'the Rif's text' and 'a text variant'. The saved Rif prints the whole story inside parentheses, after a footnote marker whose note reads 'ד"ת מ"ז'. That is a later quotation, and in this edition it may even have been added by an editor. It is not a reading of the Bavli. Its second 'אמר ליה איהו דקא מטעי אנפשיה', its 'לבי חוזאי ... מבי חוזאי' and its missing 'הוא סבר' should be stored as the Rif's quotation, uncertain in status. They should not be stored as a Bavli text variant, or as settling the speaker change.

The dossier assigns 'והא קא מטעינן ליה' to Rav Safra from the flow of the dialogue alone, and says Rashi does not name speakers. Rashi's gloss is in the first person singular: 'אם לא הייתי מגלהו היה מחזיק לנו טובה חנם' ('if I had not revealed it to him'). That fits only the man who told Mar Zutra, Rav Safra. Ben Yehoyada names him outright: 'מאי סלקא דעתיה דרב ספרא שאמר קא מטעינן ליה'. These are commentary, a separate evidence type. They back up the inference but do not replace it, and the Aramaic still leaves the speaker unnamed.

Rav Safra speaks in the plural: 'אנן לא הוה ידעינן דקאתי מר ... טפי הוה טרחינן'. So he makes a claim about what Rava also did and did not know. The graph should keep Rav Safra as the only speaker and Mar Zutra as the only addressee. Rava is covered by the content, but he is not a speaker, and no Rava → Mar Zutra speech edge follows. The dossier's 'No Rava to Mar Zutra speech edge' is right. It just should not say Rava is absent from the reply's content.

findings.target: proposed_corrections 1-3 (together → encounter / co-travel; add Mar Zutra – Rav Safra)
findings.reason: 'ורבא ורב ספרא הוו קא אתו לסיכרא' uses one plural verb for the two men, so they travel together. Mar Zutra goes 'מסיכרא' ('from Sikhra'), so the ו joins two clauses about opposite journeys, not one party. 'פגעו אהדדי' states the meeting. 'אמר להו' is one plural speech to both men, and 'אמר ליה רב ספרא' is the only reply to Mar Zutra. So the three proposed pair changes follow. The shared plural address should be counted once, not as two separate observations.

'מר זוטרא בריה דרב נחמן' in the printed text, the same name in the Rif, and 'בריה דר"נ' in the Prisha all give a patronymic. It is ordinary 'son of' wording, with nothing suggesting a fixed name. Keep a local placeholder 'Rav Nachman (father of Mar Zutra, this passage)' and a child_of claim limited to readings that carry this name. The Seder HaDorot entry lists other passages and names another 'רב הונא בריה דרב נחמן' in it. Nothing from that entry may be merged or imported here.

findings.target: proposed_correction 5 / F10 / F11 / F12 (no honour, accompaniment or retelling edges)
findings.reason: Honour appears only in a belief ('סבר') and in a counterfactual ('אי הוה ידעינן טפי הוה טרחינן'). Rav Safra's 'לא הוה ידעינן' already shows in the text itself that the meeting was not planned. Rashi, Ritva and Tosafot confirm it ('אבל הכא לא באו כלל בעבורו'). But 'commentators agree' should read 'the commentators checked agree'. Ben Yehoyada's 'חזרו עמו למחוזא והביאוהו לביתם' is his own inference. It gives no accompaniment, hosting or residence edge. The Reshit Chokhmah story, with 'חסיד' and 'תלמידיו', is a separate episode and imports no participants.

quote_checks.exact_quote: הוה קאזיל מסיכרא לבי מחוזא ורבא ורב ספרא הוו קא אתו לסיכרא פגעו אהדדי
quote_checks.note: Found in the Davidson unvocalized Aramaic and Wikisource at 94b:13. One plural verb for Rava and Rav Safra, the opposite direction for Mar Zutra, and 'פגעו אהדדי' support co-travel plus an encounter.

quote_checks.exact_quote: אמר ליה רב ספרא אנן לא הוה ידעינן דקאתי מר אי הוה ידעינן טפי הוה טרחינן
quote_checks.note: Davidson Aramaic 94b:13 (Wikisource has א"ל). Rav Safra is named as speaker and 'ליה' is singular. The second clause is contrary to fact. The plural 'אנן' covers Rava in the content only.

quote_checks.exact_quote: אמר ליה רבא מאי טעמא אמרת ליה הכי דאחלישתיה לדעתיה
quote_checks.note: Davidson Aramaic 94b:14, the right occurrence (the first line of 94b:14). The speaker is named. The addressee is unnamed 'ליה' and is resolved as Rav Safra from 'אמרת ליה הכי', not stated as the dossier says.

quote_checks.exact_quote: אמר ליה והא קא מטעינן ליה איהו הוא דקא מטעי נפשיה
quote_checks.note: Davidson Aramaic 94b:14. There is one 'אמר ליה' with no named speaker, covering both sentences. That supports the dossier's two-branch treatment in F7.

quote_checks.exact_quote: איהו הוא דקא מטעי נפשיה כלומר שהוא יודע דלא נפקינן לקדמותיה
quote_checks.note: The words are present, but the quote is cut short. The saved gloss goes on 'ואף על פי כן קאמר אמאי איצטער רבנן', which makes Gershom read Mar Zutra as knowing. That bears on F3/F11 and is not reflected in the dossier's 'may mean he should know'.

quote_checks.exact_quote: אמר ליה והא קא מטעינן ליה אמר ליה איהו דקא מטעי אנפשיה
quote_checks.note: Present in the saved Rif, inside a parenthesis that follows a footnote marker ('ד"ת מ"ז'). It supports a second turn, but only as a later quotation of uncertain status in this edition.

quote_checks.exact_quote: הוה אזיל מסיכרא לבי חוזאי ורבא ורב ספרא הוו אתו מבי חוזאי לסיכרא פגעו אהדדי אמר להן
quote_checks.note: Confirms the Rif's place variant and that it moves straight from 'פגעו אהדדי' to 'אמר להן' with no 'הוא סבר' clause.

quote_checks.exact_quote: אם לא הייתי מגלהו היה מחזיק לנו טובה חנם
quote_checks.note: Rashi on 94b:14. It is not quoted in the dossier, but its first person singular points the objection at Rav Safra, the one who had told Mar Zutra. This is commentary support for step 8.

quote_checks.exact_quote: ועל כן מוכרח לומר דחזרו עמו למחוזא והביאוהו לביתם
quote_checks.note: Ben Yehoyada's own inference, introduced by 'ונראה לי'. The same gloss names Rav Safra as the objector ('דרב ספרא שאמר קא מטעינן ליה'). It supports no accompaniment or hosting edge.

quote_checks.exact_quote: אמר לו רבא לרב ספרא: אין זה נחשב שאנו מטעים אותו, שכן
quote_checks.note: Steinsaltz adds 'Rava' as the speaker of the last line in plain (non-bold) type. It belongs to the same editorial project as the Davidson English, so it is one voice.

quote_checks.exact_quote: אבל הכא לא באו כלל בעבורו
quote_checks.note: Tosafot on 94b:14 (heading 'והא קא מטעינן ליה'). It supports the meeting being unplanned.

cases.question: Reconstruct the visit, blessings, challenge to practice and cited rulings. Separate action target, addressee and cited authority. Research halachic context and whether any later verse changes the participant identity.

findings.claim: The focal segment names two people: Rav Huna bar Yehuda (the visitor) and Rava (the host). The patronymic implies a third, Yehuda, Rav Huna's father, who does not act. Unnamed plural agents bring the light and spices.

evidence.exact_quote: רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רָבָא, אַיְיתוֹ לְקַמַּיְיהוּ מָאוֹר וּבְשָׂמִים.
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: 'Rav Huna bar Yehuda happened to come to the house of Rava; they brought before them light and spices.'

evidence.exact_quote: רב הונא בר יהודה איקלע לבי רבא, אייתו לקמייהו מאור ובשמים.
רב הונא בר יהודה איקלע לבי רבא אייתו לקמייהו מאור ובשמים
evidence.note: Same wording in the unvocalized Wikisource text (shares Vilna base; not an independent witness).

findings.reasoning: 'איקלע לבי X' is a visit formula: the subject arrives at X's household. 'אייתו' is a third-person plural verb with no named subject, so the bringers are unnamed members of the household (servants or family); they are agents but not named persons. 'לקמייהו' (before them, plural) places both men at the table. 'bar Yehuda' is a patronymic, which by project rule supports a father placeholder.
findings.graph_effect: Local persons: P1 Rav Huna bar Yehuda; P2 Rava; P3 Yehuda (father of P1, name-embedded, silent); G1 unnamed household bringers (group, no identity). Edge P3 -father_of-> P1 (source: patronymic; literal kinship is the plain reading, with the variant note in F7).

findings.claim: Action, target, addressee and cited authority are distinct. Action: Rava recites blessings. Objects: spices first, then light (things, not people). Addressee of the challenge: Rava. Speaker of the challenge: Rav Huna bar Yehuda, who is not named at the verb.

evidence.exact_quote: בָּרֵיךְ רָבָא אַבְּשָׂמִים בְּרֵישָׁא וַהֲדַר אַמָּאוֹר. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָא בֵּין בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵין בֵּית הִילֵּל — מָאוֹר בְּרֵישָׁא וַהֲדַר אַבְּשָׂמִים.
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: 'Rava blessed over the spices first and then over the light. He said to him: But [according to] both Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel, light is first and then spices!'

evidence.exact_quote: עָנֵי רָבָא בָּתְרֵיהּ וְאָמַר
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: 'Rava answered after him and said.'

evidence.exact_quote: א"ל - רב הונא לרבא לאחר שגמר הבדלה
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: Rashbam: '"He said to him" - Rav Huna to Rava, after he had finished havdala.'

evidence.exact_quote: אמר ליה רב הונא והא בין ב"ש וב"ה מאור ואחר כך בשמים
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: Rosh's quotation of the passage: 'Rav Huna said to him: But between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel, light and afterwards spices.'

findings.reasoning: 'אמר ליה' has no named subject. The later segment names Rava as the one who answers ('עני רבא בתריה'), so the challenger must be the other man present, Rav Huna. Rashbam states this explicitly, and the Rosh's quotation inserts 'רב הונא' as subject. These are commentary and codifier readings, not a different Talmud text. The spices and light are objects of the blessing, so the 'target' of the action is not a person.
findings.graph_effect: Edge P1 -addresses/challenges-> P2 (direction P1 to P2), resolved from context; mark speaker as 'inferred from later segment, confirmed by Rashbam'. Edge P2 -responds_to-> P1 from 103a:7. The response is part of the same exchange, not a second independent observation of the same relation. No person edge from the blessing itself.

findings.claim: In the Pesachim version the anonymous Gemara, not Rav Huna, supplies the source for his objection (the mishnah of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel). In the Berakhot 52b parallel Rav Huna himself cites the source. The cited authority differs by version in who does the citing.

evidence.exact_quote: וּמַאי הִיא? דִּתְנַן, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נֵר וּמָזוֹן, בְּשָׂמִים וְהַבְדָּלָה. וּבֵית הִילֵּל אוֹמְרִים: נֵר וּבְשָׂמִים, וּמָזוֹן וְהַבְדָּלָה.
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: 'And what is it? As we learned [in a mishnah]: Beit Shammai say: candle and food, spices and havdala. And Beit Hillel say: candle and spices, food and havdala.'

evidence.exact_quote: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִכְּדִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל אַמָּאוֹר לָא פְּלִיגִי, דְּתַנְיָא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נֵר וּמָזוֹן, בְּשָׂמִים וְהַבְדָּלָה.
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: Berakhot 52b: 'He said to him: Since Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel do not disagree about the light, as it is taught: Beit Shammai say: candle and food, spices and havdala.'

evidence.exact_quote: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, נֵר וּמָזוֹן וּבְשָׂמִים וְהַבְדָּלָה. וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, נֵר וּבְשָׂמִים וּמָזוֹן וְהַבְדָּלָה.
evidence.note: Mishnah Berakhot 8:5, the cited source.

findings.reasoning: 'ומאי היא' is the stam editor's question interrupting the story, so in Pesachim the explicit citation belongs to the editor's voice glossing Rav Huna's claim. In Berakhot the citation continues Rav Huna's own sentence. The Berakhot WD text has 'דתניא' (a baraita formula) while the source is a mishnah; Rif Berakhot (S11) reads 'דתנן'.
findings.graph_effect: Record Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel as cited groups (schools), not persons. Attach the citation to P1 only for the Berakhot version; for Pesachim attach it to the anonymous editorial voice with P1's claim as the target. No person-to-person edge between P1 and the schools.

findings.claim: Rava's reply cites two tannaim: he assigns the mishnah's version to Rabbi Meir and quotes Rabbi Yehuda's contrary version, in which Beit Hillel put spices before light. A statement of Rabbi Yohanan follows: people follow Beit Hillel as Rabbi Yehuda reports them.

evidence.exact_quote: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר, אֲבָל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִילֵּל עַל הַמָּזוֹן שֶׁהוּא בַּתְּחִלָּה וְעַל הַבְדָּלָה שֶׁהִיא בַּסּוֹף,
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: 'This is the statement of Rabbi Meir; but Rabbi Yehuda says: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree about food, that it is first, and about havdala, that it is last.'

evidence.exact_quote: וּבֵית הִילֵּל אוֹמְרִים: בְּשָׂמִים וְאַחַר כָּךְ מָאוֹר. וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: נָהֲגוּ הָעָם כְּבֵית הִילֵּל וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: 'And Beit Hillel say: spices and afterwards light. And Rabbi Yohanan said: The people are accustomed [to follow] Beit Hillel according to Rabbi Yehuda.'

evidence.exact_quote: זו דברי ר"מ - דהכי הוו תני לפלוגתייהו דב"ש וב"ה דסתם מתני' ר"מ
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: Rashbam: 'This is the statement of R. Meir - for so he would teach their dispute; an anonymous mishnah is R. Meir.'

findings.reasoning: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda are cited authorities for rival versions of a school dispute. They are not present. Whether 'ואמר רבי יוחנן' is still Rava speaking or the editor adding a ruling is not marked in the text. In Berakhot 52b the WD edition sets it as a separate segment (52b:26). Goldschmidt renders it 'Hierzu sagte R. Joḥanan' ('On this R. Yohanan said'), also without placing it in Rava's mouth. Rabbi Yehuda the tanna here shares a name with Yehuda, father of Rav Huna. A shared name is not an identity.
findings.graph_effect: Edges P2 -cites-> R. Meir (attribution of a version) and P2 -cites-> R. Yehuda (tanna). R. Yohanan: cited authority for the custom, with the citer left uncertain (P2 or the editor). No contact edge between P2 and R. Yohanan. Keep R. Yehuda (tanna) separate from P3 Yehuda.

findings.claim: The later segments do not change who the participants are. 103a:7 names Rava as the answerer, which fixes the addressee of the challenge. 103a:9 starts a separate visit by a different man, Rav Ya'akov bar Abba, to Rava's house. It must not be merged with Rav Huna bar Yehuda's visit.

evidence.exact_quote: עָנֵי רָבָא בָּתְרֵיהּ וְאָמַר: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
רַב יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַבָּא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רָבָא, חַזְיֵהּ דְּבָרֵיךְ ״בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הַגֶּפֶן״ אַכָּסָא קַמָּא
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: 'Rav Ya'akov bar Abba happened to come to Rava's house; he saw that he blessed "who creates the fruit of the vine" over the first cup.'

evidence.exact_quote: רבי יעקב בר אבא איקלע לבי רבא - שבת הוא
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: Rashbam: 'R. Ya'akov bar Abba happened to Rava's house - it was Shabbat.'
evidence.note: Rashbam's lemma reads 'רבי' where the WD Gemara reads 'רב'; a title variant in the next episode, noted only.

findings.reasoning: The same visit formula recurs with a different visitor and a different practice (wine blessings), and Rashbam dates it to Shabbat itself, while he places the Rav Huna visit on an ordinary Saturday night. Nothing in 103a:6-8 introduces a new speaker who could be the challenger. Scope: checked 103a:1-10 in the WD edition and Rashbam/Tosafot on 103a.
findings.graph_effect: No identity change. Keep the Rav Ya'akov bar Abba visit (103a:9) as a separate event with its own local persons. Do not carry the 'challenger' role across episodes.

findings.claim: Commentary adds a setting the Aramaic does not state. Rashbam puts the visit on an ordinary Saturday night, says the challenge came after havdala was finished, and says Rava's order matches his own community's custom. The WD English 'After Shabbat' and 'Rava acted as dictated by this custom' are translator glosses.

evidence.exact_quote: רב הונא בר יהודה איקלע לבי רבא - במוצאי שבת של חול
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: Rashbam: 'on an ordinary (weekday) Saturday night' (i.e., not a festival following Shabbat).

evidence.exact_quote: בריך אבשמים ברישא - כמנהג שלנו
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: Rashbam: 'blessed over spices first - as our custom is.'

evidence.exact_quote: After Shabbat, <b>they brought before them a light and spices.
evidence.note: WD English: 'After Shabbat' is unbolded, i.e., the translator's addition.

evidence.exact_quote: Rava acted as dictated by this custom.
evidence.note: WD English, unbolded gloss at the end of 103a:8.

findings.reasoning: The sugya before (103a:1-4) concerns a festival that follows Shabbat. Rashbam separates this story from that case. The bold/unbold convention in the WD English marks literal translation versus added explanation. The glosses are reasonable, but they are interpretation, not text.
findings.graph_effect: Event attributes (Saturday night, after havdala) are commentary-sourced and should be tagged as such. They do not change persons or edges.

findings.claim: The name has a textual variant. Rif on Pesachim reads 'רב הונא ברבי יהודה'. The Talmud editions checked, the Rif on Berakhot, the Rosh on Pesachim and Halakhot Gedolot read 'בר יהודה'. The variant bears on whether the father is a titled Rav/Rabbi Yehuda. It does not remove the father relation.

evidence.exact_quote: רב הונא ברבי יהודה
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: Rif Pesachim: 'Rav Huna berabbi Yehuda'
evidence.note: In the saved text a Hagahot Chavot Yair marker (label א) stands between this and the next words 'איקלע לבי רבא'; quoted as two pieces.

evidence.exact_quote: רב הונא בר יהודה איקלע לבי רבא חזייה דבריך אבשמים והדר אמאור
evidence.note: Rif Berakhot 39a:4, same event, reads 'בר'.

evidence.note: Rosh on Pesachim 10:9.

evidence.exact_quote: דרב הונא בר יהודה איקלע לבי רבא אייתי לקמייהו מאור ובשמים
evidence.note: Halakhot Gedolot 2:6.

evidence.exact_quote: איקלע לבי רבא ברכות (נ"ב ב') פסחים (ק"ג א')
evidence.note: Seder HaDorot lists both visits under Rav Huna bar Yehuda.

evidence.exact_quote: גם צ"ע שהיה בימי רב יהודה ורבא אם לא שנים היו
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: Seder HaDorot: 'also needs study, that he lived in the days of Rav Yehuda and of Rava, unless there were two.'

findings.reasoning: 'ברבי' can mean 'son of Rabbi/Rav' or be a scribal expansion of an abbreviated 'ב"ר'. The Rosh elsewhere writes 'רב הונא ב"ר יהודה' (S7, 10:8), which shows how the abbreviation can arise. The Rif Pesachim reading is one printed witness against several; manuscripts were not checked. Seder HaDorot's doubt about one or two men of this name is a later historical question, not a text variant.
findings.graph_effect: Keep P1 with name forms ['רב הונא בר יהודה' (majority of checked witnesses), 'רב הונא ברבי יהודה' (Rif Pesachim)]. Keep P3 as the father, marked 'title of father uncertain by variant'. Do not merge P1 with 'Rav Huna son of Rav Yehuda' or with any other Rav Huna globally without an identity pack.

findings.claim: Some witnesses say the items were brought 'before him' (singular, Rava) rather than 'before them'. The Rif and Rosh also add 'פתח רבא' ('Rava began'). Rava's presence is certain either way. Rav Huna's presence at the table rests on the visit plus his speaking, not only on 'before them'.

evidence.exact_quote: אייתו לקמיה מאור ובשמים פתח רבא בריך אבשמים ברישא
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: Rif: 'they brought before him light and spices; Rava began, blessed over spices first.'

evidence.exact_quote: אייתי לקמיה מאור ובשמים פתח רבא בריך
evidence.note: Rosh, singular 'לקמיה'.

evidence.note: Halakhot Gedolot, plural 'לקמייהו', with 'שקל רבא' ('Rava took').

findings.reasoning: A co-presence edge between P1 and P2 should cite the visit formula and the direct speech, which appear in all versions checked, not the plural pronoun alone.
findings.graph_effect: P1-P2 co-present (symmetric, saved once), evidence = 'איקלע לבי' + 'אמר ליה'. Tag 'לקמייהו' as version-dependent.

findings.claim: Halakhic context: the practice Rava followed, spices before light, is the rule adopted by Halakhot Gedolot (which cites this story), the Rambam, the Tur and the Shulchan Arukh. The codes also put wine first. That part does not come from this passage.

evidence.exact_quote: וכד איכא בשמים ומאור בהבדלה מברך על הבשמים ברישא והדר על מאור (פסחים קג.)
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: Halakhot Gedolot: 'And when there are spices and light at havdala, one blesses over the spices first and then over the light (Pesachim 103a).'

evidence.exact_quote: סֵדֶר הַבְדָּלָה בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת. מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיַּיִן וְאַחַר כָּךְ עַל הַבְּשָׂמִים וְאַחַר כָּךְ עַל הַנֵּר.
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: Rambam, Shabbat 29:24: 'The order of havdala on Saturday night: bless over wine, then spices, then the candle.'

evidence.exact_quote: סדר הבדלה
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Translation by this dossier: Tur OC 296: 'Order of havdala:'
evidence.note: A commentator marker (Darkhei Moshe) stands between the two pieces in the saved text.

corrections.change: Replace first-pass 'before' with a visit/co-presence relation (P1 visits P2's house; symmetric co-presence saved once). Keep 'addresses' P1 -> P2, but source it to 'אמר ליה' with the speaker resolved from 103a:7 and Rashbam, not to the visit pattern '[A] איקלע לבי [B]'. Add P2 -responds_to-> P1 (103a:7).
corrections.why: 'איקלע לבי' is a visit formula, not 'sitting before' a master. 'לקמייהו' refers to objects placed before both men and is singular in some witnesses. The addressing is a separate act in the next clause.

corrections.change: Keep 'same-man' (coreference of 'לבי רבא' and 'בריך רבא' to local P2). Drop the first-pass 'before'.
corrections.why: Both mentions are the host. The pattern spans the bringing of objects, and no second person is involved.

corrections.change: Add P3 Yehuda (father of Rav Huna) as a name-embedded placeholder with a father_of edge; add cited authorities R. Meir and R. Yehuda (cited by Rava), R. Yohanan (citer uncertain); Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel as groups.
corrections.why: Project rule: patronymics are kinship evidence. Cited authorities are distinct from addressee and actor.

lessons: The visit formula 'X איקלע לבי Y' should map to visits/co-present, not to 'before' (student sits before master).
An unnamed 'אמר ליה' speaker is resolved from the next named turn ('עני רבא בתריה'). Save the resolution as inferred and cite the commentary that confirms it.
Separate the actor (Rava blesses), the object (spices, light: not persons), the addressee (Rava), the speaker (Rav Huna) and the cited authorities (schools, R. Meir, R. Yehuda, R. Yohanan).
Editorial interjections ('ומאי היא? דתנן') can take over a citation from a character. Who cites a source can differ between parallel tellings.
Parallel tellings (Pesachim 103a / Berakhot 52b) are one event and should not double edge weight.
A tanna named Yehuda in the same passage as a patronymic 'bar Yehuda' is a name collision, not an identity.
Translator glosses (unbolded WD English) are interpretation and must not be stored as text facts.

review.scope: I checked every person, speaker, addressee, citation, name-variant and parallel claim in dossier.json and reading.md against the saved files in sources/ (Pesachim 103a WD, Wikisource and Goldschmidt; Rashbam; Tosafot; Rif and Rosh on Pesachim; Halakhot Gedolot; Berakhot 52b and its link bundle; Rosh on Berakhot 8:2; Seder HaDorot 995), fetched nothing new, did not check manuscripts, and did not judge historical identity or dates.

findings.reason: The dossier's own saved Rosh on Berakhot 8:2 (also inside S11) tells this same visit with a different visitor: "רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע איקלע לבי רבא חזייה דהוה בריך אבשמים". The dossier files that source as "discusses the one-cup case of the mishnah, not the visit" and F7 counts "the Rosh" among the witnesses for "בר יהודה", which is true only of the Rosh on Pesachim. Add this as a third name form for the visitor, typed as a later quotation (not printed Talmud text), with its own name-embedded parent Rav Yehoshua scoped to that reading. Do not pick one form, do not merge, and do not count the Rosh as a vote for either form, since he quotes the story two different ways.

findings.target: F3 (who cites the mishnah in Pesachim)
findings.reason: F3 says that in Pesachim the anonymous Gemara, not Rav Huna, supplies the mishnah, based on "ומאי היא? דתנן" in the WD and Wikisource text. But the three saved quotations of the Pesachim passage have no "ומאי היא": the Rif reads "א"ל והא בין ב"ש ובין ב"ה מאור ואח"כ בשמים דתנן", the Rosh "אמר ליה רב הונא והא בין ב"ש וב"ה מאור ואחר כך בשמים דתנן", and Halakhot Gedolot likewise runs straight into "דתנן". In those the citation reads as part of Rav Huna's own sentence. Keep the editor attribution for the printed text and record the later-quotation wording as a separate reading. Do not say the citer differs only between Pesachim and Berakhot.

findings.target: F2 / proposed_local_edges P2 responds_to P1 / reading.md step 6
findings.reason: Rava's reply is "עָנֵי רָבָא בָּתְרֵיהּ וְאָמַר" with no "ליה". Its addressee is not marked, and Goldschmidt renders it "Da fuhr Raba fort" ("Rava continued"), not "replied to him". Keep a link from Rava's statement to Rav Huna's objection as the target, but leave the addressee empty and give the reply link medium confidence, not high. The challenger's identity is well inferred (the only other man present, with Rava named as the one who answers), but Rashbam's "רב הונא לרבא" and the Rosh's inserted "רב הונא" are commentary and later quotation, not printed text. The unbolded WD English "Rav Huna bar Yehuda said to him" is a translator's gloss and must not be counted.

"רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רָבָא" is one observation. The dossier stores it as a directed 'visits' edge and also as a separate symmetric 'together' edge, both citing F1. Store the visit once, with co-presence implied by it, so it does not count twice. F8 is right that the co-presence should rest on the visit and on 'אמר ליה', not on the version-dependent "לקמייהו".

findings.target: F10 (merge Pesachim 103a and Berakhot 52b as one event)
findings.reason: Counting the two tellings once for edge weight is correct. But the review cannot approve an event merge. Record them as parallel tellings (parallel_of), with the claim that they are the same historical occasion left open. The Berakhot detail "חַזְיֵיהּ לְרָבָא" supports that telling's wording. It must not be imported into Pesachim as "stronger co-presence" for this passage. The parallel's own name variant (Rosh Berakhot's "בריה דרב יהושע") shows why participants should not be carried across tellings automatically.

findings.target: F1 / P3 / proposed edge P3 father_of P1
findings.reason: Keep the name-embedded father Yehuda. "בר יהודה" is kinship evidence even though the father never acts. Scope it to the readings with that name: under the Rif Pesachim reading "רב הונא ברבי יהודה" the father may be a titled Rav or Rabbi Yehuda, or 'berabbi' may be a title or an expanded abbreviation. Under the Rosh Berakhot reading the name-embedded father is Rav Yehoshua. Mark that a patronymic can work as a fixed name. Keep R. Yehuda the tanna separate from P3, as the dossier does.

findings.target: reading.md 'Name variant' and F7 note on Seder HaDorot
findings.reason: reading.md says "Seder HaDorot lists both visits under Rav Huna bar Yehuda", right after discussing the Rav Ya'akov bar Abba visit. The saved entry reads "איקלע לבי רבא ברכות (נ"ב ב') פסחים (ק"ג א')": one visit cited at two places, not the Ya'akov bar Abba visit. The same entry also mixes "ר"ה בריה דר"י" and "ר"ה ברב יהודה" forms before asking "אם לא שנים היו". Its doubt about one man or two stays an open identity question. The Rosh 10:8 line "רב הונא ב"ר יהודה" is a different passage (a Rav Sheshet tradition) and should be used only as a spelling illustration, never as a link to this visitor.

Rashbam's "בריך אבשמים ברישא - כמנהג שלנו" means 'as our custom is', which is Rashbam's own community's practice. The dossier's wording "Rava's order matches his own community's custom" could be read as a claim about Rava's community. Attach nothing to Rava from this gloss. The Saturday-night and after-havdala settings ("במוצאי שבת של חול", "לאחר שגמר הבדלה") are rightly tagged as commentary.

findings.target: F4 / A1 (R. Yohanan) and proposed correction for pair 0-27
findings.reason: The first-pass 'before' label for Rav Huna / Rava is wrong: "איקלע לבי" is a visit, not sitting before a master. 'Same-man' for the two Rava mentions in 103a:5 is right. Rava cites R. Meir ("זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר") and R. Yehuda as authorities, not as people present. "וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן" rightly stays unresolved between Rava and the editor, with no contact edge; Tosafot's "חולק רבי יוחנן אסתם משנה" does not settle who quotes him.

cases.question: Preserve the two versions of the question and their attribution, nested alternatives, and the related repeated passage. Do not attach a quoted opinion to the wrong speaker or count parallel editorial repetitions as independent evidence.

findings.claim: In 20b:9 the exchange is given with two alternative speaker pairs: Rav Pappa asks Abaye, or ('and some say') Rami bar Hama asks Rav Hisda. Both askers put the same question.

findings.translation_by_this_dossier: 'Rav Pappa said to Abaye, and some say it: Rami bar Hama to Rav Hisda: Like whom?'
findings.reasoning: ואמרי לה swaps the whole pair of names, not one name. The question is one question with two transmitted speaker pairs. It is a textual alternative about who asked whom; it does not show that only one of the two exchanges happened, nor that both did.
findings.graph_effect: Record two branch-scoped 'asks' edges: Rav Pappa -> Abaye (branch PAIR-A) and Rami bar Hama -> Rav Hisda (branch PAIR-B). Mark Rav Pappa|Rami bar Hama as alternative askers and Abaye|Rav Hisda as alternative addressees of the same question. These alternative links are role alternatives, not social relations between those people. No Abaye-Rav Hisda or Rav Pappa-Rami bar Hama personal edge.

findings.claim: The whole exchange in 20b:9 is itself an alternative ('some say') to the version in 20b:8, where Rav Yehuda reports in Rav's name that the baraita follows Rabbi Meir. So there are nested alternatives: the form of the tradition (report vs exchange), and inside the exchange, which pair spoke.

findings.translation_by_this_dossier: 20b:8: 'Rav Yehuda said Rav said: Whose is this? It is Rabbi Meir, who said: a person can consecrate something that has not come into the world.' 20b:9 opens: 'There are those who say: Rav Pappa said to Abaye ...'. Steinsaltz: 'some say this matter in a different formulation'.
findings.reasoning: The text marker is איכא דאמרי. Steinsaltz and the Davidson English (same editorial family, not independent) both render it as another version of the same discussion. Whether the second version fully replaces the Rav Yehuda-Rav report, or only its form, is not stated in the text; that is interpretation (see alternative_readings AR1).
findings.graph_effect: Create branch group FORM with FORM-REPORT (Rav Yehuda citing Rav, 20b:8) and FORM-EXCHANGE (20b:9). Branch group PAIR (PAIR-A, PAIR-B) is nested under FORM-EXCHANGE. The Rav Yehuda -> Rav 'reports in name of' edge belongs to FORM-REPORT; the asks edges belong to FORM-EXCHANGE.

findings.claim: The reply 'Rather, like whom?' has no named speaker in the Aramaic. By structure the addressee answers: Abaye in pair A, Rav Hisda in pair B. The Davidson English at 20b:9 inserts 'Abaye' only; the same translation at the repeated passage 21a:4 says 'He said to him', and Steinsaltz at 21a:4 calls the speaker 'the one asked'.

findings.reasoning: The pronoun ליה plus the question-answer frame binds the reply to the addressee of whichever pair is read. The Davidson English choice of 'Abaye' at 20b:9 silently follows pair A only; its own rendering of the identical Aramaic at 21a:4 does not name anyone. Steinsaltz Hebrew and Davidson English come from the same editorial project and are not independent witnesses.
findings.graph_effect: Bind the reply role per branch: respondent = Abaye in PAIR-A, Rav Hisda in PAIR-B. Do not attach the reply to Abaye unconditionally. Keep the English 'Abaye' as a translation rendering, not as Hebrew source evidence.

findings.claim: The question and reply identify which tannaitic position the anonymous baraita follows: Rabbi Meir's view that one can consecrate what does not yet exist. They do not say that Rav Hisda (or Abaye) personally follows or rules like Rabbi Meir.

lessons: Alternatives nest: placement (which baraita) > form (report vs exchange) > speaker pair. A flat 'alternative' kind loses which branch an edge lives in; branch groups need a parent pointer.
An 'and some teach it on this' (ואיכא דמתני לה אהא) repetition is one tradition with two placements. Mentions in the repeated block link to the same tradition id and add no evidence weight.
An unnamed reply (אמר ליה) binds to the addressee per branch. Translation insertions of a name are renderings, and may pick one branch only.
כמאן (like whom?) asks which authority an anonymous teaching follows. It should map to 'attributes position to', never to 'follows' between the discussants and the cited tanna.
A name-form difference between a passage and its repetition needs three fields: printed reading, later emendation (with who proposes it), and manuscript evidence (here: not checked).
Recurring transmission formulas (אמר ליה רב פפא לאביי ואמרי לה ...) do not create juxtaposition or togetherness edges between the alternate names.

findings.target: F4; proposed correction for bavli|Arakhin|20b|9|53|67 (Rav Hisda follows Rabbi Meir)
findings.reason: 'כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, דְּאָמַר: אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם?' asks whose opinion the anonymous baraita follows. It comes right after the objection 'וְהָא אֵין אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם?' in 20b:8. Nothing says that Rav Hisda or Abaye rules like Rabbi Meir, so removing the 'follows' edge is correct. Keep the roles within each version apart: the asker puts forward the attribution as a question, and the addressee confirms it with the rhetorical 'וְאֶלָּא כְּמַאן?'. Rabbi Meir is a cited legal position, not a participant. Steinsaltz on 21a:4 glosses the question as 'כמאן [כמי] אתה מפרש דבר זה?' ('according to whom do you explain this?'). That is a commentary rendering that the Aramaic does not have. It must not be used to make the addressee the author of the attribution.

F8 records only 'Rav Yehuda reports in the name of Rav'. F4 records the Rabbi Meir attribution only for the exchange version. In 20b:8, 'אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא', the one who attributes the baraita to Rabbi Meir is Rav, and Rav Yehuda passes it on. Add an explicit FORM-REPORT content claim: Rav's reported statement attributes the baraita to Rabbi Meir's position. Rav is the speaker, Rav Yehuda the transmitter, and no addressee is marked. This matches the earlier cross-check's 'claims_to_keep', which the dossier endorses but never writes out. The report must not become a student_of link or a meeting.

The Aramaic reply is only 'אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְאֶלָּא כְּמַאן?', and Steinsaltz on 20b:9 also leaves it unnamed ('אמר ליה [לו]: ואלא כמאן'). The Davidson English at 20b:9 adds 'Abaye said to him', which fits only PAIR-A. At 21a:4 the same translation has 'He said to him', and Steinsaltz there has 'הנשאל' ('the one asked'). Assigning the reply to Abaye in PAIR-A and to Rav Hisda in PAIR-B is correct. Treating the English 'Abaye' as a translation choice from the same editorial project, not as a vote, is also correct.

findings.target: F1; F10; proposed corrections for bavli|Arakhin|20b|9|19|27 and bavli|Arakhin|20b|9|27|53
findings.reason: 'אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא' prints two complete asker-addressee pairs. So 'Rav Pappa asks Abaye' (PAIR-A) and 'Rami bar Hama asks Rav Hisda' (PAIR-B) are each tied to their version. Abaye and Rav Hisda (and likewise Rav Pappa and Rami bar Hama) are alternative holders of the same role, with no social link, so 'none' as a person relation is correct. One narrow caution on F1's general wording that the formula 'swaps the whole pair'. In Temurah 33b:6 ('ואמרי לה רבא לרבי יוחנן דמוקים לה') the words after 'לרבי' mean 'according to Rabbi Yohanan', not an addressee, and the Davidson English there changes only the asker. Whether the whole pair changes has to be read from each passage, not assumed from the formula.

findings.target: F5 (placement and repetition); reading.md 'What the text says' item 1
findings.reason: 'וְאִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַהָא' (20b:10) supports treating 21a:4 as the same discussion under a second placement, adding no extra weight. Rashi's gloss 'להא דרב יהודה ואביי ורמי בר חמא' is a commentator's short label for the unit that moves. It names Abaye (who answers in PAIR-A) and Rami bar Hama (who asks in PAIR-B), so it assigns no roles and yields no edges. It is also a note on 20b, so it must not be counted as a witness to the 21a:4 name (see the first finding). Small fix: PLACE-BULL is '20b:6-9' in structure but '20b:7-9' in F5's graph_effect. One range should be chosen.

'אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי' at the start of 20b:9 makes the exchange an alternative to the report in 20b:8. Leaving open whether it replaces the report or only rephrases it is right, because neither the Aramaic nor Steinsaltz's 'דבר זה בלשון אחרת' decides the question. Nested branches (placement > form > pair) are the right structure. All edges stay historical_graph_eligible=false: the words say nothing about meetings, seniority or dates.

cases.question: Preserve two reported transmission routes as separate claims under one teaching. The textual or need not mean only one event historically happened. Investigate source editions and commentators, and define what a graph may infer from each route.

findings.claim: In the printed tradition and its digital texts, one question (how many trumpets may be added) gets one answer (up to 120, from II Chronicles 5:12) under two attribution routes joined by ואמרי לה ('and some say'): Route A 'Rav Huna said'; Route B 'Rav Zavdi said Rav Huna said'. Both routes end in Rav Huna.

evidence.exact_quote: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב זַבְדִּי אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: עַד מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים
evidence.translation_by_researcher: Researcher translation: 'Rav Huna said, and some say: Rav Zavdi said Rav Huna said: up to one hundred and twenty'

evidence.exact_quote: ועד כמה אמר רב הונא ואמרי לה אמר רב זבדי אמר רב הונא עד מאה ועשרים
ועד כמה אמר רב הונא ואמרי לה אמר רב זבדי אמר רב הונא עד מאה ועשרים
כמה אמר רב הונא ואמרי לה אמר רב זבדי אמר רב הונא עד מאה ועשרי׳ שנאמ׳ ועמהם

findings.reasoning: The wording is identical in the Koren texts, the Wikisource text and the 1523 Venice print as read from the page image. These are not independent witnesses: S01 and S02 are one editorial work, and S03 and the Vilna print descend from the printed tradition that the Venice print begins. They show a stable printed text, not independent corroboration of history.
findings.graph_effect: One teaching node T (limit of 120 trumpets) with two attribution branches: branch A {Rav Huna -> credited_with T}; branch B {Rav Zavdi -> reports_in_name_of -> Rav Huna; Rav Huna -> credited_with T}. Rav Huna's credit for T is shared by both branches.

findings.claim: The two routes do not disagree about who is the source of the teaching. They differ only in whether a transmitter is named. The Talmud's phrasing reports two ways the teaching was cited; it does not say which is right, and it does not say only one event happened.

evidence.exact_quote: אמר רב הונא, ואמרי לה [ויש ד'דאומרים] שאמר רב זבדי אמר רב הונא
evidence.translation_by_researcher: Researcher translation: 'Rav Huna said, and some say [there are those who say] that Rav Zavdi said Rav Huna said'

evidence.exact_quote: Rav Huna says, and some say Rav Zavdi says that Rav Huna says: They may play up to 120 trumpets
R. Hona, manche sagen R. Zabdi im Namen R. Honas, erwiderte: Bis hundertundzwanzig
evidence.translation_by_researcher: Researcher translation of the German: 'R. Huna, some say R. Zavdi in the name of R. Huna, answered: up to one hundred and twenty'

findings.reasoning: All three renderings keep both routes and choose neither. S06 and the English of S01 come from the same Koren project, so they count as one editorial reading; the 1929 German is a separate translation. A short attribution (Huna) and a longer chain ending in the same person (Zavdi reporting Huna) can both be true: Rav Huna may have taught it and Rav Zavdi may also have passed it on. The phrase ואמרי לה marks a disagreement in how the report was transmitted, not a statement that the other report is false.
findings.graph_effect: Mark the two branches exclusive only as report forms (a reader follows one wording at a time). Do NOT mark them historically exclusive. Do NOT create a Huna<->Zavdi 'alternative' edge: Zavdi is never offered as an alternative author.

findings.claim: The Mishnah the Gemara is explaining says trumpets may be added without limit; the Gemara's question 'up to how many?' is what the two routes answer.

evidence.exact_quote: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִשְּׁתֵּי חֲצוֹצְרוֹת, וּמוֹסִיפִין עַד לְעוֹלָם
evidence.translation_by_researcher: Researcher translation: 'One does not use fewer than two trumpets, and one may add without limit'

evidence.exact_quote: מִשְּׁתֵּי חֲצוֹצְרוֹת וּמוֹסִיפִין וְכוּ׳. וְעַד כַּמָּה?

findings.reasoning: This fixes the topic of the teaching. Both routes answer the same question, which supports treating them as two reports of one teaching rather than two teachings.
findings.graph_effect: Attach T to Mishnah Arakhin 2:5 as the explained text. Teaching node is shared across both branches.

findings.claim: The printed Vilna page carries, in its marginal column headed שיטה מקובצת, a note keyed to this line that proposes a different wording: the first speaker is 'Rav Huna bar Zavdi', the alternative is 'Rav Zavdi' alone, and the words 'said Rav Huna' (the second occurrence) are deleted.

evidence.exact_quote: הונא ב] ואמרי לה אמר רב זבדי אמר רב הונא עד מאה ועשרים
evidence.note: Main text with note marker ב] after the first רב הונא.

evidence.exact_quote: ב] רב הונא בר זבדי ואמרי לה אמר רב זבדי עד ותיבות אמר רב הונא נמחק:
evidence.translation_by_researcher: Researcher translation: '[note b:] Rav Huna bar Zavdi, and some say Rav Zavdi said, [up to the word] "until"; and the words "said Rav Huna" are deleted.'

findings.reasoning: Read as a correction note, it yields the text: אמר רב הונא בר זבדי ואמרי לה אמר רב זבדי עד מאה ועשרים ('Rav Huna bar Zavdi said, and some say Rav Zavdi said: up to 120'). The letters of the note are clear in the image; turning the note into a full sentence is the researcher's reconstruction of a standard note form. This is a later proposed reading printed beside the text. It is not the main text, and it is not a manuscript reading the case has seen. What the compiler based it on is not stated in the note.
findings.graph_effect: Save as a separate evidence type (proposed emendation / reported variant), branch C. Under C: two alternative SPEAKERS (Rav Huna bar Zavdi; Rav Zavdi) with no transmission edge between them, plus a patronymic child_of edge from Rav Huna bar Zavdi to a local parent placeholder 'Zavdi'. Do not let C overwrite the printed branches A and B.

findings.claim: The 1342 Munich manuscript (Cod. hebr. 95) appears to have the printed structure (Rav Huna; and some say Rav Zavdi ... Rav Huna; up to 120), not the Shitah Mekubetzet wording. The researcher could not read every letter between זבדי and עד at the available image resolution.

evidence.exact_quote: ועד כמ׳ א׳ רב הונא ואמרי לה א׳ רב זבדי [?] רב הונא עד מאה ועשרים
evidence.note: [?] marks one or more letters not read with confidence (probably the abbreviation א׳). No 'בר זבדי' was seen after the first רב הונא. Work crops in work/munich_crop_1830.jpg, work/m_a_big.jpg, work/m_b_big.jpg, work/mz_700_big.jpg.

findings.graph_effect: Tentatively attach S19 as manuscript support for branches A and B. Flag for human verification. Do not use it to reject branch C until checked.

findings.claim: The commentators and codes checked explain or rule on the content (up to 120 trumpets) without deciding between the attribution routes. Tosafot and Kessef Mishneh quote the attribution only as 'Rav Huna said, and some say, etc.' or 'Rav Huna said, etc.'

evidence.translation_by_researcher: Researcher translation: 'And one may add without limit; up to how many? Rav Huna said, and some say, etc.'

evidence.exact_quote: אמר רב הונא עד ק"כ דהא אשכחן בקרא (דברי הימים ב ה) שחפשו אחרי ק"כ כהנים לתקוע בחצוצרות ולא יותר
evidence.translation_by_researcher: Researcher translation: 'Rav Huna said up to 120, because we find in Scripture that they sought 120 priests to blow trumpets and no more'

evidence.exact_quote: ובגמרא ועד כמה אמר רב הונא וכו' עד מאה ועשרים
evidence.translation_by_researcher: Researcher translation: 'and in the Gemara: up to how many? Rav Huna said, etc.: up to 120'

evidence.exact_quote: וְאֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִשְּׁתֵי חֲצוֹצְרוֹת וְלֹא מוֹסִיפִין עַל עֶשְׂרִים וּמֵאָה
evidence.translation_by_researcher: Researcher translation: 'one does not use fewer than two trumpets and does not add beyond 120'

findings.reasoning: When Tosafot restate the view they name only Rav Huna. This fits the fact that Rav Huna is the source in both routes. It is not a vote against Rav Zavdi's route: Tosafot abbreviate with כו' ('etc.'). The Rambam, Bartenura, Tosafot Yom Tov, Melekhet Shelomoh and Sefer HaChinukh give the rule without naming anyone. Rashi and Rabbeinu Gershom (Vilna texts on Sefaria) have no comment on this line in the segments checked.
findings.graph_effect: No commentator evidence supports choosing one route. Short-form citations of 'Rav Huna' by later works do not create new person relations or new witnesses.

findings.claim: A modern commentary (Mishnat Eretz Yisrael) quotes both routes and describes the teaching as a scriptural derivation from a one-time biblical event, not a received tradition or a practical ruling.

evidence.exact_quote: ברור שזו הגדרה כללית, והבבלי מצמצמה
evidence.translation_by_researcher: Researcher translation: 'It is clear this is a general statement, and the Bavli narrows it'

evidence.translation_by_researcher: Researcher translation: 'This is not a tradition, nor even a halakha, but a derasha based on a chance event in the past'

findings.reasoning: This is one modern scholarly reading of the content. It does not address the attribution question. It is useful for the episode type: the teaching is exegesis, not a report of Temple practice seen by the speaker.
findings.graph_effect: Episode kind: exegetical derivation of a halakhic limit. Do not infer that Rav Huna or Rav Zavdi witnessed Temple practice.

findings.claim: Seder HaDorot (19th-century chronicle) uses the printed chain 'Rav Zavdi said Rav Huna said' to date Rav Zavdi, and proposes that an earlier chronicle (Yuchasin) placing him 'in the time of Rav' has a copying error for 'in the time of Rav Huna'.

evidence.exact_quote: רב זבדי בעירכין בזמן רב עיי"ש (י"ג ב') אמר רב זבדי אמר רב הונא, ואולי ביוחסין ט"ס וצ"ל בזמן רב הונא:
evidence.translation_by_researcher: Researcher translation: 'Rav Zavdi, in Arakhin, [Yuchasin says] in the time of Rav. See there (13b): Rav Zavdi said Rav Huna said. Perhaps in Yuchasin it is a scribal error and it should read: in the time of Rav Huna.'

findings.reasoning: This is a historical inference built on one branch (B) of this very passage, plus a proposed emendation of a different book (Yuchasin), not of the Talmud. It is not an independent witness to Rav Zavdi's dates. Yuchasin itself was not fetched.
findings.graph_effect: Store as a later chronological proposal that depends on branch B. It must not be counted as extra evidence for branch B, and it gives no calendar date.

corrections.why: The earlier review said the textual branches were clear and sought no parallel. The Vilna margin shows a later proposed wording with different people (Rav Huna bar Zavdi / Rav Zavdi).

lessons: ואמרי לה between a short attribution and a longer chain ending in the same person is an 'attribution length' alternative. Store branches on the teaching, not as a person-person 'alternative' edge.
Each branch gets its own inference licence. A chain branch licenses reports_in_name_of only; it does not license teacher, met, heard-directly, before or generation.
Report-form exclusivity and historical exclusivity are separate fields. Default historical exclusivity to not_established when one branch is an expansion of the other.

Printed marginal emendations (Shitah Mekubetzet, Bach, Gra etc.) are a distinct evidence type from main-text readings and from manuscripts. A proposed wording can change which people exist in the passage (here: a new 'Rav Huna bar Zavdi' and a patronymic parent placeholder).
Later chronicles that date a sage from a citation chain (Seder HaDorot) depend on one branch of the same passage and are not independent evidence for it.

Digital editions from one publisher (vocalized, unvocalized, Hebrew commentary, English) count as one editorial witness. Page images of early prints and manuscripts are separate witnesses, but a researcher's visual reading must be marked as such.

review.scope: I checked every graph-relevant finding, edge and proposed correction against the saved text files, and read the three saved page images myself (Munich 95 line at about y 1848-1898 px, x 460-1110 px; Bomberg 1523; the Vilna main text, Shitah Mekubetzet column and Hagahot HaBach column); I did not fetch new sources, collate other manuscripts, or see Yuchasin or the Shitah Mekubetzet book itself.

findings.target: F04 / branch C / may_infer 'two different people are offered as the speaker'
findings.reason: The Vilna margin note, which I read myself, gives two NAMES for the speaker: 'רב הונא בר זבדי' and, after 'ואמרי לה', 'אמר רב זבדי'. The note does not say these are two different men; a name is not a person, and 'X, and some say Y' does not prove only one of them said it. Keep P4 and P6 as two alternative speaker names under branch C, with 'distinct persons: plausible, not stated', and add an open P4-P6 relation next to the open P5-P6 one.

The parent placeholder must stay: 'רב הונא בר זבדי' embeds a father Zavdi, and that holds even though the father never acts. But this edge, unlike the two other branch C edges, carries no evidence_type, and it is marked 'literal per patronymic בר' with no caveat. Tag it evidence_type = proposed_emendation (S21 margin only, not main text, not a manuscript seen), and mark that 'bar Zavdi' may be a fixed name rather than literal kinship.

findings.target: F09 claim 'Other Bavli hits for זבדי are patronymics of other named men'
findings.reason: Zevachim 28b:5 (S33, and the same hit in S28) reads 'תָּנֵי זַבְדִּי בַּר לֵוִי'. There Zavdi is the man's own name, not his father's. The other hits (Kiddushin 33b 'רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר זַבְדִּי', Kiddushin 73b and Yevamot 83b 'רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר זַבְדִּי') are patronymics. The conclusion 'no cross-passage merge' still holds, but the claim should say 'patronymics, plus one man named Zavdi (Zavdi bar Levi)'. That man is another bearer of the name to keep apart from Rav Zavdi here and from the father in branch C.

I read the Munich line myself and agree with the first reader. After 'ועד כמ׳ א׳ ר[ב] הונא' the next dark main-hand word is 'ואמרי לה'. There is a gap with faint brown strokes, which I read as ink showing through from the other side of the page, and I cannot rule out an erasure. No 'בר זבדי' is written. After 'זבדי' a second 'רב הונא' stands before 'עד מאה ועשרים', though I cannot read the small mark before it. So Munich, as read, does not show either change that branch C proposes (adding 'bar Zavdi' and deleting the second 'Rav Huna'). Keep confidence low until a published collation is checked; do not use it to reject branch C.

In the printed line 'אמר רב הונא ואמרי לה אמר רב זבדי אמר רב הונא', Rav Zavdi is a transmitter inside branch B, never another author. A Huna/Zavdi 'alternative' person pair is wrong for branches A and B. Replace it with two branch records on teaching T, exclusive only as report forms. Do not move the 'alternative' label onto P4/P6 except inside branch C with its evidence type, and then only as alternative names (see the first finding).

Offsets 61 and 73 are 'רב זבדי' and the second 'רב הונא', and the words between them are 'אמר רב זבדי אמר רב הונא'. So this is Zavdi reporting in Huna's name, inside branch B only. Store the direction once, as reports_in_name_of Zavdi -> Huna, with direct_hearing = not_stated. Add no teacher, meeting, before/after or generation edge.

The saved text reads 'רב זבדי בעירכין בזמן רב עיי"ש (י"ג ב') אמר רב זבדי אמר רב הונא, ואולי ביוחסין ט"ס וצ"ל בזמן רב הונא'. The bracket '[Yuchasin says]' in the dossier's translation is an inference, reasonable because the next clause blames Yuchasin, not words in the text. Besides being non-independent (the dossier already says so), the proposed 'in the time of Rav Huna' does not follow from branch B: 'in the name of' does not make the two men contemporaries. Keep Yuchasin's unseen reading 'in the time of Rav' and Seder HaDorot's proposed correction as two separate items. Neither becomes a time edge.

findings.target: F04 evidence 0 and 1, F01 evidence 3 (page-image readings)
findings.reason: I confirmed the Bomberg reading letter for letter: 'כמה אמר רב הונא ואמרי לה אמר רב זבדי / אמר רב הונא עד מאה ועשרי׳ שנאמ׳ ועמהם'. I also confirmed the Vilna main text with its marker right after the first 'הונא', and the note in the column headed 'שיטה מקובצת': 'ב] רב הונא בר זבדי ואמרי לה אמר רב זבדי עד ותיבות אמר רב הונא נמחק:'. The note's lemma ends 'אמר רב זבדי עד', so the deleted 'אמר רב הונא' is the second one, as the dossier says. The Hagahot HaBach column on the same page has no note on this line, which settles one item the dossier left open.

The question 'וְעַד כַּמָּה?' belongs to the anonymous voice of the Gemara, asked about the Mishnah's 'וּמוֹסִיפִין עַד לְעוֹלָם'. It is not addressed to Rav Huna or Rav Zavdi. Record speaker = anonymous discussion for the question, and addressee = not marked for both routes. The 120 priests of the verse are biblical figures inside a proof text, not people in the passage.
