findings.claim: The rule against asking demons on Sabbath is anonymous. It is not a continuation of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's clause. Rif quotes it as a baraita on its own without him. Yad Ramah calls its author the first tanna against Rabbi Yosi.

evidence.exact_quote: ת"ר אין שואלין דבר מן השד בשבת רבי יוסי אומר אף בחול אסור
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: The rabbis taught: one does not ask a thing of a demon on Sabbath. R. Yosi says: even on a weekday it is forbidden.

evidence.exact_quote: ולת"ק דר' יוסי הוא דאצטריך
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: It was needed for R. Yosi's first tanna.

findings.reasoning: This supports c3 (the sages hold the Sabbath rule). The Talmud text alone does not rule out reading the clause as Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's continuation, but these two sources treat it as anonymous.
findings.graph_effect: Keep c3 with subject 'sages'. Cite Rif and Yad Ramah in its notes. No Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel edge to the demon rule.

findings.claim: The William Davidson Aramaic and English, and the Tosefta, write 'רשב"ג' out as Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. That name contains a father named Gamliel, and the first reading gave that father no placeholder.

evidence.exact_quote: אמר רבן שמעון בן גמליאל במה דברים אמורים בכלי הניטל
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: in what case are these words said? With a movable vessel.

evidence.exact_quote: מעין בשבת. רבן שמעון בן
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: ...[over the] eye on Sabbath. Rabban Shimon ben — (the saved text continues 'גמליאל' after an apparatus marker).

findings.reasoning: Under project rules, a relationship embedded in a name is evidence. The abbreviation רשב"ג itself encodes 'ben Gamliel', and the other editions spell it out. Whether 'ben Gamliel' is literal kinship is the usual reading of a patronymic. Which Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is meant is a separate historical decision, and the text gives no clue.
findings.graph_effect: Add a local placeholder 'Gamliel, father in the name of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel' and a child_of claim with basis 'name', evidenced by the expanded spellings in S1 and S15 and by the abbreviation in S0. Relabel 'rsbg' as Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel (expansion attested in other editions). No historical identity.

findings.claim: Seder HaDorot files this story under a 'רב יצחק בר יוסף' entry that also holds unrelated passages, such as the traveller who reports what happened before Rabbi Yohanan. It also quotes Yuchasin's guess that Rav Dimi bar Yosef was his brother. Both are identity hypotheses built on a shared name.

evidence.exact_quote: כי אתא אמר עובדא הוה קמי' דר' יוחנן
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: (under the bold heading רב יצחק בר יוסף:) when he came he said: a case came before R. Yohanan...

evidence.exact_quote: וכתב ואולי רב דימי בר יוסף אחיו
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: and he wrote: perhaps Rav Dimi bar Yosef was his brother.

findings.reasoning: A shared name does not establish identity. Seder HaDorot's compiler marks the brother idea as 'perhaps'. Nothing in Sanhedrin 101a ties this Rav Yitzhak to Rabbi Yohanan or to a brother.
findings.graph_effect: No edges to Rabbi Yohanan, Abaye or Rav Dimi bar Yosef from this passage. At most, record Seder HaDorot's grouping as a historical-identity candidate in a separate layer, unaccepted.

findings.claim: Rashi on the baraita explains the practice (people who lose something ask by demon-craft) and says Rabbi Yosi's weekday ban is 'because of danger, as is explained below'. He does not say who gives that explanation.

evidence.exact_quote: שכן עושין כשאובדין שום דבר שואלין במעשה שדים והם מגידים להם
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: for this is what they do: when they lose something they ask by demon-craft, and the demons tell them.

evidence.exact_quote: אף בחול אסור - לשאול בשדים כדמפרש לקמן משום סכנה
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: 'Even on a weekday it is forbidden': to ask of demons, as is explained below, because of danger.

findings.reasoning: This settles what 'asking' means, as Rashi reads it, but not who speaks the danger clause (F4).
findings.graph_effect: Can serve as the gloss on the 'sabbath' and 'weekday' statement nodes (commentary layer). No person edges.

lessons: Textual evidence needs separate types: direct witness, medieval quotation, quotation within a quotation, a report about other books, a later emendation, and a modern translation. They should not be pooled into one count.
One work can carry internal variants: the Vilna Rosh has Ulla, while Radbaz's quotation of the Rosh has Rav Huna. A witness is a particular copy, not the work.
A trailing unmarked clause after a named ruling needs a speaker branch rather than a silent 'narrator' default.
Event labels like 'miracle' should not fix their referent when commentators disagree. Keep a referent-open node and put the readings in branches.
Agents that only commentary supplies (here a demon) belong in a commentary layer, attributed to the commentator, and are not persons.
An abbreviated name (רשב"ג) can still encode a patronymic. Expand it only when another edition spells it out, and keep the parent as a local placeholder.
Parallel sources with the same attribution and different wording are parallel evidence, not independent repeat observations.

review.scope: Checked every dossier quotation against the saved files in sources/ (all 60 quotes found verbatim) and read the surroundings for F1-F11, the alternative readings and the proposed corrections; no manuscripts, no Gra gloss and no new network sources were consulted, and no page images were involved.

findings.reason: The Yad Ramah quote 'ולת"ק דר' יוסי הוא דאצטריך' comes from his comment on the NEXT baraita (שידי שמן ושדים הבאים על ידי ביצים ... מותרים לשאול בהם בשבת), not from the Sabbath rule in 101a:5. It says only that there is a first tanna against Rabbi Yosi, which is true whether that first tanna is the anonymous baraita or Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. So Yad Ramah is neutral on this point and should be removed as support.

The claim 'It is not a continuation of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's clause' overreaches. The Talmud text runs 'אבל בכלי שאינו ניטל אסור ואין שואלין בדבר שדים בשבת' with only a 'ו' between them, and Soncino punctuates it as part of his sentence ('are forbidden; nor may demons be consulted on the Sabbath'). The Tosefta also puts the demon clause right after his words with no new speaker. Only the Rif's layout supports a separate teaching: it inserts 'תניא אידך' and then opens a new 'ת"ר אין שואלין דבר מן השד בשבת'. That is the Rif's editorial arrangement. Keep c3 with subject 'sages' and basis interpretation, add a low-confidence note that the clause can be read as Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel continuing, and approve no Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel edge in either direction.

Radbaz is not a second copy of the Rosh's wording. After 'הביא הרא"ש ז"ל ראיה' he quotes the Gemara in his own form: 'א"ר הונא (אין) ... ואיתעביד ליה ניסא ופקע ארזא ופלטי''. That is fuller than the Rosh, which stops at 'אבלע בארזא' and reads 'רבי יצחק ברבי יוסף'. Beit Yosef's quotation of the same Rosh passage leaves out the ruling line altogether ('אף בחול אסור ואף ר"י לא אמר אלא מפני סכנה'), and Be'er Sheva only reports loosely that 'הרא"ש' reads 'אמר רב הונא'. The Ulla reading therefore rests on the one Vilna print. It is still a weak speaker branch, but the saved sources do not show 'an internal variant inside the Rosh', so the ontology lesson should not cite Radbaz as that example.

The dossier cuts the Rif quotation off at 'ואף רבי יוסי'. The printed Rif continues 'לא אמר' אלא בשעת הסכנה' ('only at a time of danger'). Hagahot HaBach corrects this to 'אלא מפני הסכנה כצ"ל'. 'At a time of danger' turns Rabbi Yosi's weekday ban into a conditional one, which is a legal condition. Record it as a printed-Rif wording variant on c5, with Bach's correction stored as a separate emendation layer that does not erase the printed Rif reading.

Support splitting 'rescue' into swallowing, a miracle whose referent is left open, and 'פקע ארזא ופלטיה'. But the Steinsaltz Hebrew cites Rashash for this very gloss ('דאיבלע בארזא [שנבלע בתוך הארז] (רש"ש)'), and the William Davidson English belongs to the same project. So 'Rashash, Steinsaltz and the William Davidson English' is one line of reading, not three. Also, Rashash's last note, 'רש"י ד"ה כי הא דרי"צ. ובלעו הארז. כצ"ל', emends Rashi's own words. The saved 'ובלעו הארז' may already be corrected text, so Rashi's branch should note that its key word carries an emendation. Do not use this to settle Yad Ramah's 'בארץ'.

findings.target: c9, c10, c11 (story nodes) and proposed correction 'rescue'
findings.reason: The story comes in as 'כי הא' ('as in this case') inside a legal argument. It is an illustration of the danger, not a free-standing narrated event. The scene claims should carry that role, and their voice should follow the F4 speaker branch (anonymous voice or Rav Huna continuing) instead of a default 'narrator'. Citing Rav Yitzhak bar Yosef's case establishes no meeting, no teaching link and no chronology between him and Rav Huna.

A1 files 'Radbaz and the Wikisource/Koren Hebrew print it in parentheses' under the with-אין reading. That contradicts F1, which rightly says the parentheses leave 'read or delete' unstated. Parenthesized witnesses should support neither branch. A1 also lists Be'er Sheva's reported 'הרי"ף והרא"ש והרמב"ן ורוב הפוסקים' beside the Rif, Rosh and Ramban themselves, so the report must not be counted on top of them.

The Aramaic has no speech marker before 'ואף רבי יוסי לא אמרה אלא משום סכנה'. 'The Gemara notes' / 'ומעירים' is one editorial project's choice. Beit Yosef's quotation of the Rosh even attaches the danger clause straight to Rabbi Yosi's baraita with no Rav Huna line, which shows the clause travels on its own. Keep the two-way speaker branch, and note that no saved source asserts the 'Rav Huna continuing' reading; it is only left open by run-on quotation.

Support adding a local Gamliel placeholder and a child_of claim with basis 'name', scoped to readings that carry the name. Mark it as a name that may be a fixed dynastic form rather than a proof of literal kinship. Note that the expansion in the William Davidson text is editorial, while the Tosefta Vienna spelling ('רבן שמעון בן גמליאל') is a parallel that supports only the wording. Add the Rif's title variant 'אמר רבי שמעון בן גמליאל' ('Rabbi', not 'Rabban') as a name variant, not an identity signal.

Each checks out against the saved text. The Rosh has 'כי הא דרבי יצחק ברבי יוסף אבלע בארזא', so keep Yosef and c8. The demon and the asking are supplied only by commentary ('היה שואל במעשה שדים ובקש השד להזיקו', 'שבא לשאול בשדים'). The Tosefta reads 'אף בחול אין לוחשין בדבר שדים', a parallel and not a second observation. Seder HaDorot's 'ואולי רב דימי בר יוסף אחיו' is marked 'perhaps' and yields no edge. Lieberman calls the Chelek commentary 'המיוחס לרש"י' (attributed to Rashi), a small caution on how the Rashi branch is labelled.

cases.question: Who acts, speaks and is cited in Bava Batra 24a:14 (with its continuation at 24b:1)? Which graph claims are explicit, which rest on interpretation, and which alternatives must stay open, when checked against the wider discussion (23b-24b), translations, commentaries and codes?

findings.claim: Rava is the only person named as acting in 24a:14. The text narrates that he permitted the wine skins; it does not quote his words or give his reason.

evidence.exact_quote: הנהו זיקי דחמרא דאשתכחן בי קופאי שרנהו רבא
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: those skins of wine that were found at/among 'bei kofa'ei' - Rava permitted them.

findings.reasoning: שרנהו רבא is a third-person report of a decision in a case. No אמר or quoted statement follows. Everything after לימא is the anonymous discussion.
findings.graph_effect: Keep Rava as a local person with a case-ruling claim (voice: narrator). Better predicate: rules_on or permits (case decision), not holds_view with an attached rationale.

findings.claim: Both the question and the answer are unattributed. The majority-of-pourers reason is the anonymous discussion's explanation of Rava's ruling. The text does not say that Rava gave this reason.

evidence.exact_quote: לימא לא סבר לה לדרבי חנינא שאני התם דרובא
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: shall we say he does not hold Rabbi Hanina's [rule]? It is different there, for the majority...

evidence.exact_quote: דשפוכאי ישראל נינהו
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: ...of the pourers are Jews.

evidence.exact_quote: שרא ליה רבא אע"ג דרובא דעלמא עובדי כוכבים נינהו רובא  דשפוכאי ישראל נינהו
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: Rava permitted it, although most of the world are gentiles, [since] most pourers are Jews.

findings.reasoning: The question-and-answer form (לימא ... שאני התם) is the Talmud's anonymous editorial voice. The Rosh drops the question and presents the majority reason as the ground of Rava's ruling. That is a later presentation, not a quotation of Rava. The graph should keep 'the anonymous discussion explains Rava's ruling by X' separate from 'Rava held X'.
findings.graph_effect: Earlier claim c4 should have voice anonymous_discussion (not narrator) and discourse_status: answer to the question in c3. Any link 'Rava holds majority-of-pourers reasoning' must be marked interpretation, sourced to the anonymous answer or to the Rosh.

findings.claim: The answer crosses the page break. 'Majority' (רובא) ends 24a:14 and 'of the pourers are Jews' begins 24b:1. The earlier evidence for 'most local wine pourers are Israelites' quotes only the 24b words, which do not contain the word for majority.

evidence.exact_quote: שאני התם דרובא
דשפוכאי ישראל נינהו

findings.reasoning: Read alone, the 24b words say 'the pourers are Jews'. Only with 24a's רובא do they say that most of them are Jews. The distinction matters because the whole argument depends on majority.
findings.graph_effect: The evidence for the 'majority' statement and for claim c4 should cite both pieces: 24a:14 'שאני התם דרובא' plus 24b:1 'דשפוכאי ישראל נינהו'.

findings.claim: Rabbi Hanina's rule, which the first reading called 'not stated in this excerpt', appears at the start of the same discussion (23b). Where majority and proximity conflict, one follows the majority.

evidence.exact_quote: אמר רבי חנינא רוב וקרוב הולכין אחר הרוב
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: Rabbi Hanina said: majority and proximity - one follows the majority.

findings.reasoning: 24a:10, 24a:12 and 24a:14 all say 'דרבי חנינא', referring back to this statement. Rashi on 24a:14 also glosses the question as 'to follow the majority'.
findings.graph_effect: Fill hanina_rule with this content and evidence from 23b:2. Change coverage from needs_context to resolved for this point. Rabbi Hanina is a speaker at 23b:2; at 24a:14 he is only cited.

findings.claim: In the same discussion, a person named Rava had already derived the majority-over-proximity rule (24a:5). He then withdrew an earlier objection of his that seemed to point the other way (24a:3, 24a:8). Tosafot and Rashba use this to read the 24a:14 question as a contradiction inside Rava's own position, not a neutral question.

evidence.exact_quote: ואמר רבא ש"מ מדרבי חייא תלת שמע מינה רוב וקרוב הלך אחר הרוב
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: And Rava said: learn three things from Rabbi Hiyya's [baraita]; learn from it that with majority and proximity one follows the majority.

evidence.exact_quote: והא רבא הוא דקאמר רוב ומצוי ליכא למ"ד הדר ביה רבא מההיא
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: But it was Rava who said 'majority plus frequent [presence] - nobody disputes'? Rava retracted that one.

evidence.exact_quote: לימא רבא לית ליה דר' חנינא. פי' והא רבא אית ליה לעיל דר' חנינא
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: 'Shall we say Rava does not hold Rabbi Hanina's [rule]' - meaning: but Rava holds Rabbi Hanina's [rule] above.

evidence.exact_quote: ולאו דחויי קא מדחי ליה, דודאי רבא כרבי חנינא סבירא ליה
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: and it is not a mere deflection, for Rava certainly holds like Rabbi Hanina.

findings.reasoning: The textual facts are Rava's statement at 24a:5 and the retraction note at 24a:8. Linking them to 24a:14 depends on reading the three Ravas in one discussion as the same literary character. That is the natural reading within the discussion, but it is an editorial co-reference, not a historical identification. The weight of the question (a contradiction versus a neutral question) is Tosafot's and Rashba's interpretation. The Piekarski English note on Tosafot also refers readers to Ritva, which I did not fetch.
findings.graph_effect: Add a separate claim: Rava (24a:5) holds majority over proximity, with evidence from 24a:5 and voice Rava (quoted). Add a local coreference candidate: rava@24a:5 = rava@24a:14, basis same-discussion literary continuity. Keep it provisional and separate from any global identity. Do NOT turn c3 into a disagreement.

findings.claim: The two לימא questions next to each other mirror each other, and both are rejected. At 24a:12 the question is whether Ravina agrees with Rabbi Hanina; at 24a:14 it is whether Rava disagrees. Neither case settles either person's position on the rule.

evidence.exact_quote: ההוא חצבא דחמרא דאישתכח בפרדיסא דערלה שריא רבינא לימא משום דסבר לה דרבי חנינא
שאני התם דאי מיגניב מינה אצנועי בגויה לא מצנעי

findings.reasoning: In both cases שאני התם supplies a case-specific reason, so the ruling is neutral about Rabbi Hanina's rule. This is a check against adding either 'Ravina agrees with Hanina' or 'Rava opposes Hanina' as asserted.
findings.graph_effect: Earlier c3 (rava opposes hanina_rule, question/rejected) is correct and must not be promoted. If Ravina's case is graphed, its 'agrees' claim must likewise be question/rejected.

findings.claim: Commentators disagree on בי קופאי. It may be a common noun for the vines (the wine was hidden among vines, per Rashi, belonging to a Jew). Or it may be a place name (the Arukh as reported by Tosafot, and Rambam as read by Kessef Mishneh). The Arukh itself gives both.

evidence.translation_mine: My translation: hidden among vines in a vineyard, and it [the vineyard] is a Jew's.

evidence.exact_quote: בי קופאי. בין הגפנים:

findings.reasoning: Rashi's reading makes the case a 'proximity' case: a Jew's vineyard is nearby, set against a gentile majority. Tosafot then has to explain how a bare place name could give proof-bearing proximity ('ובכהאי גוונא היה דהוה קורבא דמוכח'). Maharsha says that under Rashi, finding the wine among vines is itself proof-bearing proximity. The William Davidson English and Steinsaltz follow Rashi ('of a Jew', 'במקום של ישראל'). Those two are one editorial project and should not be counted as two witnesses. Soncino's footnote also records the place-name alternative with a historical-geography identification from Obermeyer, which I have not checked.
findings.graph_effect: Earlier entity 'site' (kind place) should become an ambiguous locator with two branches: (a) common noun 'among the vines' (Rashi, Gershom, Arukh second view, Jastrow, Dictionary of the Talmud, Soncino main text); (b) toponym 'Bei Kofa'ei/Kifa'ei' (Arukh first view via Tosafot; Rambam per Kessef Mishneh; Soncino footnote). No gazetteer identification should be accepted from this passage.

lessons: An anonymous answer that explains a named sage's ruling should be stored as the anonymous discussion explaining the ruling. It should not be stored as the sage's own view. Later codifiers such as the Rosh may fold the reason into the ruling; that is a separate, later presentation.
When a statement crosses a page or segment boundary, its evidence needs every piece. Here the word carrying the argument (רובא) sits on the earlier side of the break.
'Rejected לימא' claims come in mirrored pairs on this page (Ravina agrees? / Rava disagrees?). The contract should treat both as question/rejected, with no residual stance.
Implied contrast groups (here gentiles) are commentary inferences with competing scopes. They need a basis field and branches, not a textual mention.
A word that may be a toponym or a common noun (בי קופאי) needs a locator entity with branches. It should not be a place node.

Commentary lemmas and citations (Tosafot, Arukh, Rosh), dictionary-reported manuscript readings (Jastrow) and one's own image reading are three distinct evidence types. Do not merge them into a 'variant' flag.
Names in a commentary's cross-reference (Rav Mordechai, Rav Shimi bar Ashi) belong to the cited passage. They must not leak into the focal graph.
The William Davidson English and Steinsaltz Hebrew are one editorial project. Their agreement is not two witnesses.

findings.target: F05 (and alternative_readings 'force of the לימא question', reading.md 'Force of the question')
findings.reason: Tosafot does turn the question into a challenge ('פי' והא רבא אית ליה לעיל דר' חנינא'). Rashba says something different: his words 'ולאו דחויי קא מדחי ליה, דודאי רבא כרבי חנינא סבירא ליה' are about the answer (it is not a mere deflection) and assert that Rava holds Rabbi Hanina's rule. They do not describe the question as a contradiction. Rabbeinu Gershom belongs in the same camp ('שאני התם. לעולם רבא סבר לה כר' חנינא') and is missing. Record the Rashba and Gershom positions as commentary interpretation that Rava holds the rule, kept apart from Tosafot's reading of the question's force.

findings.target: F05 claim wording 'He then withdrew an earlier objection' and proposed context claim
findings.reason: At 24a:8 the retraction comes from the anonymous discussion answering its own difficulty: 'והא רבא הוא דקאמר ... הדר ביה רבא מההיא'. Rashba also reports it as the Talmud's answer ('ואקשינן ... ואמרינן הדר ביה רבא מההיא'). The text does not narrate an act of retraction by Rava, and it gives no order of events. If graphed, 'Rava retracted his 24a:3 view' takes the anonymous_discussion voice and is marked as a harmonising answer. The claim 'Rava holds majority over proximity' (24a:5, Rava's own quoted voice) stays as proposed.

findings.target: F06 and ontology_lessons ('Rejected לימא claims ... with no residual stance')
findings.reason: The two rejected questions do not mirror each other in what they leave behind. Ravina's answer at 24a:13 ('דאי מיגניב מינה אצנועי בגויה לא מצנעי') has nothing to do with majority, so his stance stays open. Rava's answer re-grounds his ruling in a majority ('שאני התם דרובא | דשפוכאי ישראל נינהו'), which fits Rabbi Hanina's rule rather than being neutral about it. Also, at 24a:11 a rejected לימא ends with an asserted stance in the anonymous voice: 'לא דכולי עלמא אית להו דר' חנינא' (Rav and Shmuel both hold it). So c3 stays question/rejected and no 'Rava agrees with Hanina' edge comes from 24a:14's text. But the general lesson 'no residual stance' is too broad and should be dropped or limited to cases like Ravina's.

findings.target: F13 (Munich 95 visual reading) and entity winepourers (m4)
findings.reason: I re-read the image. I confirm the case and the question, roughly '…זיקי דחמר׳ דאשתכחו בי קופ[אי] שרינהו רב[א] לימ׳ דלא סבר לה לר׳ חנינ׳ שאני הת׳'. The name looks more like רבא than רבה, but I cannot settle it. Where the dossier wrote 'דרוב[א] … ישר׳ נינהו' with an ellipsis, I read 'דרוב ישר׳ נינהו והנ"מ … אבל', and there is no visible room for 'דשפוכאי' before the next line's 'זוטרי אימור מעוברי דרכ׳ נפול'. My reading is low confidence and proves nothing. Still, it means the 'wine pourers' group should be scoped to the printed text and to the commentaries quoting it (Rashi, Rashba, Rosh, Kessef Mishneh lemma), with a flag that one manuscript may read only 'the majority are Jews'. That flag stays until a proper transcription is checked. Do not delete the group.

findings.target: F05 proposed context claims from 24a:3-5 (missing addressee and citations)
findings.reason: If the 24a:3-8 exchange enters the graph as context, 24a:3 opens 'א"ל רבא', so the addressee is marked. 'Him' points back to Abaye, who spoke just before in 24a:2 ('אמר אביי'). The dossier mentions Abaye only as a wider-context name. At 24a:4-5 Rava also cites two earlier teachings: Rabbi Hiyya's baraita ('דתני ר' חייא') and Rabbi Zeira ('וש"מ איתא לדר' זירא'). The dossier's added claim names only Rabbi Hiyya. These are citation claims only, never student_of or a meeting, and they stay scoped to 24a:3-5, not to the focal case.

findings.target: F02, F03 and proposed corrections c4 / c1
findings.reason: The answer does cross the page break: 24a:14 ends 'שאני התם דרובא' and 24b:1 begins 'דשפוכאי ישראל נינהו'. The question and answer carry no speaker. 'שרנהו רבא' is a narrated ruling that gives no words or reason. The Rosh's 'שרא ליה רבא אע"ג דרובא דעלמא עובדי כוכבים נינהו רובא דשפוכאי ישראל נינהו' is a later retelling that folds the reason into the ruling, and it should stay a separate evidence type. The William Davidson English also supplies words the Aramaic lacks: 'Rava' as the subject of לימא, 'of a Jew', and 'unconcerned ... gentile'. Treat those as translation, not text.

I support turning the locator into a two-branch entity with no place node. Two points are narrower than the dossier puts them. Rambam's own words ('מקום שהיו רוב מוכרי היין בו ישראלים') never name Bei Kofa'ei, and Kessef Mishneh hedges ('ונראה שרבינו מפרש בי קופאי שם מקום'), so Rambam belongs in the toponym branch only as Kessef Mishneh's guess. Tosafot reports the Arukh's view and fits it to the argument ('ובכהאי גוונא היה דהוה קורבא דמוכח') without adopting it. The Arukh's extra variant 'ס"א עד בי כיפי פי' גשר' belongs to the cited escort story, not to this passage.

The quotes 'Ms. F.' and 'Ms. M.' do appear in Jastrow, but on their own they carry none of the reported readings. The evidence should quote 'B. Bath. 24ᵃ בי ק׳ (Ms. F. קַפָּאֵי)' and 'B. Bath. 24ᵇ אימור באברוו׳ הוו מנחי Ms. M. (ed. באברו׳)'. Rashba's heading adds a further commentary wording, 'לא שאני התם'. None of this changes people or speakers, and all of it stays reported-reading or commentary-citation evidence, not manuscript text.

Checked and supported. Rabbi Hanina's rule sits at 23b:2 ('אמר רבי חנינא רוב וקרוב הולכין אחר הרוב'). The label should rest on those words only, because the next clause ('ואע"ג דרובא דאורייתא ... רובא עדיף') may be the anonymous discussion. Gershom's first explanation forbids the small skins ('אסירי') and his alternative permits them ('ל"מ ... אפי' דזוטרי מותרין ... והכי עיקר'). Kessef Mishneh does weigh a vessels-only reading and then reject it. The Sotah 46b people stay out of this graph. There are still no patronymic names in the focal segments.

cases.question: In Bava Batra 152b:7 (with 152b:4-8 and 152a-153a context), which people, speech turns, concessions and school versions are explicit, which rest on interpretation, and what did the first reading and the earlier review miss?

findings.claim: Both 'concessions' in 152b:7 are the anonymous Gemara's hypothetical reasoning ('one might say'), and the closing צריכא rejects them. Neither Rav nor Shmuel is reported as conceding anything.

evidence.exact_quote: צריכא דאי איתמר בהא בהא קאמר רב משום דקנו מיניה אבל בהא דלא קנו מיניה אימא מודה ליה לשמואל
אבל בהך אימא מודה ליה לרב צריכא
one might say that he concedes to Shmuel.
על כן צריכא [צריך] שייאמרו שתי המחלוקות.

findings.reasoning: אימא ('say', i.e. one might suppose) marks a supposition by the Gemara's own voice. The sentence explains why both disputes had to be recorded; the conclusion is that each concession would have been a mistaken inference. The Davidson English and the Steinsaltz Hebrew are one editorial work, so they count as one reading here.
findings.graph_effect: Keep c6 and c7 as hypothetical and rejected. Their voice is the anonymous Gemara, not a report of what Rav or Shmuel said. No actual agreement or retraction edge between Rav and Shmuel.
findings.translation (this dossier): It is necessary: had it been stated in that case, [one would say] Rav says so there because they performed an act of acquisition with him, but in this case where they did not, say he concedes to Shmuel ... but in that one, say he concedes to Rav. It is necessary.

findings.claim: In the first half of the צריכא, the first בהא is the earlier case (a gift with an act of acquisition, 152a). 'בהא דלא קנו מיניה' is the present case (wrote and conferred, no act of acquisition). Every commentary and translation checked here that addresses the point reads it this way (Rashbam, Tosafot, Rabbeinu Gershom, Soncino, Davidson/Steinsaltz). One printed note to Rabbeinu Gershom proposes an emendation that makes this explicit.

evidence.exact_quote: אבל בהך - בתרייתא דלא קנו מיניה
בההיא דלעיל קאמר רב ארכבוה אתרי ריכשי. משום דקנו מיניה וכתבו לו קנין אבל בהא דכתב וזיכה לו דלא קנו מיניה
נראה דצ"ל דאי איתמר בהא. בההוא דלעיל בהא קאמר רב וכו'.
Since there was no symbolic acquisition.
Where symbolic acquisition did take place.

findings.reasoning: The printed text uses בהא for both cases in the first half. Only the clauses משום דקנו מיניה and דלא קנו מיניה tell them apart. Rashbam's lemma reads בהך where the Wikisource text has בהא דלא קנו מיניה. That is a small lemma difference, recorded as a text-witness detail only. The Gershom footnote is a later proposed emendation ('נראה דצ"ל', 'it seems one should read'), not a manuscript reading.
findings.graph_effect: c6 content = the present zikkui case (the pilot's secondwins); c7 content = the earlier 152a case (the pilot's prior). Both assignments match the pilot. The emendation should be stored as a proposed emendation, separate from source variants.

findings.claim: The earlier dispute that 152b:6-7 refers to (152a:1-3) does not set Rav's plain ruling against an opposite plain ruling by Shmuel. In the Wikisource/Davidson text, Rav's side is reported by 'בי רב' in Rav's name, and Shmuel's side is doubt: 'I do not know what I should rule'. Witnesses differ on the chain: Rif and the Shita Mekubetzet lemma quote Rav directly, and Rashbam's lemma has 'בי רב אמרי' without 'in Rav's name'.

evidence.exact_quote: איתמר מתנת שכיב מרע שכתוב בה קנין בי רב משמיה דרב אמרי ארכביה אתרי ריכשי ושמואל אמר לא ידענא מאי אדון בה
In the study hall of Rav they say in the name of Rav:
רב אומר ארכבה אתרי ריכשי
איתמר מתנת שכיב מרע שכתוב בה קנין רב אמר ארכבה אתרי רכשי שמואל אמר לא ידענא מה אידון בה
מתנת שכיב מרע שכתוב בה קנין בי רב אמרי ארכביה כו'
והא איפליגו בה חדא זימנא - לעיל במתנת שכיב מרע שכתוב בה קנין דרב אמר ארכבה אתרי ריכשי

findings.reasoning: When 152b:6-7 says simply 'Rav' about the earlier case, it compresses a report that the Wikisource text gives through the school of Rav. The Rif and the Shita Mekubetzet are later works quoting the Gemara. Their wording is a different evidence type (a citation or lemma witness) from the Wikisource/Vilna printed text. Shmuel's stance there is uncertainty ('לא ידענא מאי אדון בה'), which his dispute with Rav in 152b:5 does not reproduce.
findings.graph_effect: The pilot's prior statement should carry its transmission: בי רב → in the name of Rav (Wikisource), with separate variant branches (Rav directly; בי רב without 'in Rav's name'). Record Shmuel's view in the prior case as doubt, not as 'second acquires'. This recovers the earlier rule the pilot marked as missing.
findings.translation (this dossier): It was said: a dying man's gift in which an act of acquisition is written. The school of Rav say in Rav's name: he mounted him on two steeds. And Shmuel said: I do not know how to rule on it.

findings.claim: Tosafot hold that the Shmuel half of the צריכא is not really needed, because Shmuel's two rulings do not run parallel and the objection targets Rav only. Rashba repeats the difficulty, calls Tosafot's answer strained, and leaves it open ('ועדיין צריכא עיון').

evidence.exact_quote: ומיהו משמואל לא קשיא מידי
למילתא דשמואל אין צריך כאן שום צריכותא
ובתוספות דוחקין דאדרב בלחוד קא מקשה
אבל קושטא דמלתא לשמואל הפוכין הן בדיניהן. ועדיין צריכא עיון.

findings.reasoning: The Gemara's balanced form (Rav half, Shmuel half) does not prove that Shmuel's positions in the two cases are parallel. Two major commentators question that half, and one leaves the question unresolved.
findings.graph_effect: Do not derive any Shmuel-Rav similarity or consistency edge from the Shmuel half of 152b:7. Save it as a rhetorical hypothetical whose necessity is disputed (Tosafot; Rashba unresolved).
findings.translation (this dossier): Tosafot: 'But from Shmuel there is no difficulty at all' / 'for Shmuel's matter no necessity-argument is needed here'. Rashba: 'but in truth, for Shmuel his rulings are reversed; and it still needs study'.

findings.claim: The meaning of זיכה ('conferred') in the Rav-Shmuel case is disputed, and the commentators name different people for the explanations. Rashbam: he handed over the deed. Rabbeinu Yitzhak bar Meir (in Tosafot) objects. Tosafot: he conferred the property through another person, recorded in the deed. Ramban credits 'the Sages of Spain' with 'go, take hold of the property and acquire', while Rashba credits the same explanation to 'the Geonim'. Raavad (via Shita Mekubetzet): conferring the property itself. Rabbeinu Gershom: 'go and take possession before me'.

evidence.exact_quote: כתב וזיכה לזה - כתב כל נכסיו לראובן ומסר לו את השטר לראיית זכותו
פירש רבינו שמואל זיכה שמסר לו את השטר וקשה לרבינו יצחק בר מאיר
אלא זיכה היינו שזיכה בו את הנכסים וכתב לו בשטר שזיכה לו ע"י אחר
ורבני ספרד ז"ל פירשו בדאמר ליה לך חזק בנכסים וקני
והגאונים ז"ל פרשו בדאמר ליה לך חזק בנכסים וקני
פירוש זיכה הנכסים כמי זכו בשדה זו לפלוני
כתב וזיכה לזה. שא"ל לך וזכה בה לפני
wrote [a deed of the gift] and handed
conferred possession of the same property

findings.reasoning: The legal mechanism does not change who holds which ruling. It does change what the pilot's statement labels say. The Soncino rendering 'handed' follows the Rashbam line; the Davidson 'conferred possession' leaves the mechanism general.
findings.graph_effect: Keep firstwins/secondwins labelled as 'wrote and conferred (זיכה)' with the mechanism open. When commentators are cited as sources of a reading, keep Ramban's attribution ('Sages of Spain') and Rashba's ('Geonim') separate. Do not merge them.

findings.claim: In 152b:5 the reasons ('it is like a healthy person's gift' / 'like a dying man's gift') come in the Gemara's restatement of the two rulings. The Davidson edition and Steinsaltz present them as the Gemara's explanation. The text does not show whether Rav and Shmuel themselves stated these reasons.

evidence.exact_quote: רב אמר ראשון קנה הרי היא כמתנת בריא ושמואל אמר שני קנה הרי היא כמתנת שכיב מרע
The Gemara explains: Rav says
ומסבירים את טעמיהם

findings.reasoning: The rulings ('first acquires' / 'second acquires') are attributed outright in 152b:4. Segment 5 repeats each ruling with a reason attached. That is a common way the Gemara explains a view, and it is ambiguous between quoting and explaining. The two editorial notes come from one editorial work.
findings.graph_effect: Split c3/c4 into (a) the ruling, attributed to Rav or Shmuel (explicit), and (b) the reason, attributed in the Gemara's explanation (voice uncertain).

findings.claim: Rav Dimi explicitly said 'a later testament cancels an earlier testament' when he came. The text does not say where he came from or went to. It is the anonymous Gemara that identifies the 'wrote to this one and wrote to that one' case with his teaching. The same statement by Rav Dimi appears at Bava Batra 135b in another context. The Jerusalem Talmud has the same wording as a baraita in the name of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

evidence.exact_quote: פשיטא כתב לזה וכתב לזה היינו דכי אתא רב דימי אמר דייתיקי מבטלת דייתיקי
As when Rav Dimi came from Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia
רב דימי מארץ ישראל לבבל
R. Dimi enunciated when he came
מאי תיבדק כי אתא רב דימי אמר דייתיקי מבטלת דייתיקי
תני רבן שמעון בן גמלי' אומר דייתיקי מבטלת דייתיקי

findings.reasoning: 'From Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia' is an editorial supplement in the Davidson/Steinsaltz work. Soncino says only 'when he came'. At 135b the statement answers 'what is תיבדק' in Rabbi Yohanan's ruling. That context might suggest Rav Dimi was reporting a Palestinian tradition, but neither 135b nor 152b says he received it from anyone. The Jerusalem Talmud baraita comes from another corpus. It is a parallel attribution, not a variant of this Bavli sentence, and it does not show that Rav Dimi was quoting Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
findings.graph_effect: Keep c1 (Rav Dimi says the dictum) and c2 (the arrival) as explicit, with no origin or destination. Add a separate claim that the anonymous Gemara applies the dictum to the 'wrote to this one, wrote to that one' case. Add no transmission edge from Rabbi Yohanan or Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel to Rav Dimi.
findings.translation (this dossier): It is obvious: wrote to this one and wrote to that one - that is [the case of] what Rav Dimi said when he came: a testament cancels a testament.

findings.claim: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba is the named reporter ('אמר') of the Pumbedita version. The pilot uses him only as a claim 'voice' and records no speech or transmission claim with him as subject. Witnesses give his name differently: 'רב ירמיה בר אבא' (Wikisource), 'ר' ירמי' בר אבא' (Tosafot Rid lemma), 'א"ר ירמיה בר אבא' (Rif), and 'רב ירמיה' without patronymic (Rosh as quoted in Shita Mekubetzet). On the next page (153a:8), Rav Nahman sends a case to 'ר' ירמיה בר אבא' in Shum Tamya.

evidence.exact_quote: בפומבדיתא מתנו הכי אמר רב ירמיה בר אבא שלחו ליה מבי רב לשמואל
אמר ר' ירמי' בר אבא שלחו מבי רב לשמואל
א"ר ירמיה בר אבא שלחו ליה מבי רב לשמואל
מדאמר רב ירמיה בסמוך שלחו מבי רב לשמואל
שדריה לקמיה דר' ירמיה בר אבא לשום טמיא
אמר הכא אתרא דשמואל היכי נעביד כוותיה דרב

findings.reasoning: The reporter is explicit. 'בר אבא' gives a father named Abba, so the pilot's child_of claim (c8) and the parent placeholder stay, under the project rule. The man at 153a:8 has the same name and is placed in the same sugya. Rav Nahman sends him a case so that a ruling following Rav can be given there, which fits someone tied to Rav's rulings. But a shared name does not establish identity, and 153a:8 does not state any teacher-student link.
findings.graph_effect: Add a claim: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba says / reports the correspondence (speech/transmission family, branch pumb_report). Keep c8 child_of Abba, with Abba as a local placeholder. Add the 153a:8 person as a coreference candidate only, not a merge. Record the title and patronymic variants as name-form evidence.
findings.translation (this dossier): In Pumbedita they taught it thus: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said: they sent to Shmuel from the house of Rav ...

findings.claim: 'Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said: they sent to Shmuel from the house of Rav, let our teacher teach us' is a recurring formula. The same opening appears at Gittin 66b, Gittin 89b and Shevuot 46a. At Sanhedrin 24b the same Sura/Pumbedita layout gives a different reporter (Rav Hanina bar Shelemya) and the same answer formula 'אין לאחר קניין כלום'.

evidence.exact_quote: אמר רב ירמיה בר אבא שלחו ליה מבי רב לשמואל ילמדנו רבינו יצא עליה קול מראשון
א"ר ירמיה בר אבא שלחו ליה מבי רב לשמואל ילמדנו רבינו אמר לשנים כתבו ותנו גט לאשתי
א"ר ירמיה בר אבא שלחו ליה מבי רב לשמואל ילמדנו רבינו אומן אומר
בסורא מתני הכי בפומבדיתא מתני הכי א"ר חנינא בר שלמיה שלחו ליה מבי רב לשמואל ילמדנו רבינו לפני גמר דין וקנו מידו מאי שלח להו אין לאחר קניין כלום

findings.reasoning: The Gittin and Shevuot hits come from the Sefaria search-index snapshot (S21). Their full pages were not fetched for this case. The Sanhedrin page was fetched (S24). A repeated formula is a literary pattern of transmission. It is not evidence that these questions formed one historical exchange, and the same answer wording in two tractates does not make two passages one event.
findings.graph_effect: Do not merge the Bava Batra and Sanhedrin correspondences, or their reporters, into one event. Rav Yirmeya bar Abba's link to this sending formula recurs across tractates, which is useful for later identity work only as a pattern. It is not an identity or relationship proof.

findings.claim: 'מבי רב' is a group whose name contains Rav ('the house of Rav'). Translators render it 'the academy' (Soncino), 'the study hall of Rav' (Davidson), or 'Rav's study house' (Steinsaltz). Davidson and Steinsaltz add 'after the death of Rav', and Soncino adds a bracketed alternative 'after Rab's death in 247'. The Hebrew text says nothing about Rav's death, and none of the traditional commentaries checked here says so at this place.

evidence.exact_quote: שלחו ליה מבי רב לשמואל ילמדנו רבינו
After the death of Rav, the following question <b>was sent from the study hall of Rav to Shmuel:
לאחר מותו של רב
was sent from the academy
[Or, 'from the school of Rab', after Rab's death in 247.]

findings.reasoning: The 'after Rav's death' reading, and its date, are historical inference from translators and editors. Davidson and Steinsaltz are one editorial work. Soncino marks the idea as an alternative in brackets. The commentaries checked on this line were Rashbam, Tosafot, Rabbeinu Gershom, Yad Ramah, Ri Migash, Tosafot Rid, Ramban, Rashba and Shita Mekubetzet. None states it here. That finding covers only those files. 'רבינו' ('our teacher') is how the senders address Shmuel. On its own it does not establish a student relationship.
findings.graph_effect: Add the group→Rav link as a name-embedded affiliation (literal 'house of Rav'; academy vs household vs disciples left open). Add no student_of edge from the senders to Shmuel or Rav, no time scope 'after Rav's death', and no date.

findings.claim: Tosafot report Rabbeinu Tam's view, which Rashi shares, that 'אמרי בי רב' means Rav Huna unless Rav Hamnuna is evident. This concerns the phrase 'בי רב ... אמרי' (as at 152a:1). It is not about the senders 'שלחו ליה מבי רב' at 152b:8.

evidence.exact_quote: ועוד דאמרי בי רב הכא ואמרי בי רב היינו רב הונא כמו שמפרש ר"ת
וגם רש"י סובר כן דהיינו רב הונא היכא דלא מוכח שהוא רב המנונא

findings.reasoning: This is an interpretive convention reported by one school of commentators, used here in an argument about the halakhah. It is not an explicit statement in the Gemara.
findings.graph_effect: Record it as a commentary-sourced identity candidate (בי רב at 152a:1 → Rav Huna), kept separate from text evidence and not applied to the 152b:8 senders.

findings.claim: How far back does 'בסורא מתנו הכי' ('in Sura they taught thus') reach? Rashbam reports that some explain it as reaching the first dispute (152a). He rejects that view and says, with Rabbeinu Chananel, that it refers to the immediately preceding Rav-Shmuel dispute about 'wrote and conferred'. Tosafot Rid reads the Sura and Pumbedita versions as disagreeing. Rabbeinu Gershom glosses only 'as said above'.

evidence.exact_quote: בסורא מתנו הכי - אית דמפרשי אדלעיל קאי אפלוגתא קמייתא דמתנת שכיב מרע שכתוב בה קנין
אלא אהך דסליק מיניה קאי דפליגי רב ושמואל בכתב וזיכה לזה וכתב וזיכה לזה וכן פר"ח
משמע דפליגי סוריא ופומבדיתא
בסורא מתנו הכי כדאמר לעיל
At Sura they taught as above

findings.reasoning: The pilot rightly left the backward reach uncertain. The commentaries give it two named options: 'some explain' (152a) versus Rashbam and Rabbeinu Chananel (152b:4-7). Rav Dimi's line is not in dispute either way.
findings.graph_effect: The sura_report branch covers at least the 'wrote and conferred' dispute and its צריכא (152b:4 second half through 152b:7). Keep an alternative in which it also covers the 152a dispute. Rav Dimi stays shared.

findings.claim: The witnesses word the Pumbedita question differently. Wikisource: a dying man wrote all his property to others and they performed an act of acquisition with him. Rif: he wrote and conferred, and they performed an act of acquisition, with a footnote giving the Gemara's other wording. Tosafot Rid: 'some books' read 'and conferred on the first and they performed an act of acquisition'. Rashbam's paraphrase, following Rabbeinu Chananel, is 'wrote and conferred on the first'. Rabbeinu Gershom: an act of acquisition without writing, then given to another. The answer also varies: 'אין אחר קנין' (Wikisource) versus 'אין לאחר קנין' (Rif, Rambam).

evidence.exact_quote: ילמדנו רבינו שכיב מרע שכתב כל נכסיו לאחרים וקנו מידו מהו שלח להו אין אחר קנין כלום
וזיכה וקנו מידו מהו שלח להו אין לאחר קנין כלום
בגמ' איתא ש"מ שכתב כל נכסיו לאחרים וקנו מידו מהו כו' (ג"א)
יש ספרים שכתב בהן וזיכה לראשון וקנו מידו דאיכא תרתי זיכוי וקנין
בפומבדיתא מתנו שלחו מבי רב לשמואל ילמדנו רבינו כתב וזיכה לראשון וקנו מידו מאי
קנו מידו בלא כתיבה וחזר ונתנו לאחר מהו
אֲבָל שְׁכִיב מֵרַע שֶׁכָּתַב וְזִכָּה וְקָנוּ מִיָּדוֹ אֵין לְאַחַר קִנְיָן כְּלוּם
[but was not entered in the deed]

findings.reasoning: These are different evidence types. The Wikisource line is a printed text. The Rif line is a medieval digest's text with a later printed note. 'יש ספרים' in Tosafot Rid reports manuscripts he saw. Rashbam and Rabbeinu Gershom paraphrase. Rambam codifies. Soncino's bracket follows Rabbeinu Gershom. None of these changes who asks or answers. They change what Shmuel is said to rule on in the Pumbedita branch.
findings.graph_effect: The pilot's question statement should record the Wikisource wording as the text and link the other wordings as variant or interpretive branches of the question's content. The sender (בי רב), addressee (Shmuel) and reporter (Rav Yirmeya bar Abba) stay the same across them.

findings.claim: Under the readings checked, Shmuel's Pumbedita answer means the gift cannot be withdrawn once the act of acquisition is done: the first recipient keeps it. That outcome matches Rav's 'first acquires' in the Sura version, but it may concern a different set of facts (with an act of acquisition, or with conferring plus acquisition).

evidence.exact_quote: וראשון קנה שני לא קנה
the first donee acquires the legal ownership of the gift
קנה ואין יכול לחזור במתנתו וכ"ש להקנותו לאחר
שלח ליה אין אחר הקנין כלום ואין יכול לחזור בו
רב אמר ראשון קנה

findings.reasoning: A shared outcome is not stated agreement. The text never says Shmuel agreed with Rav or changed his mind. It gives two school versions.
findings.graph_effect: Keep Shmuel's Sura-branch view (second acquires) and his Pumbedita-branch answer (nothing after acquisition) as separately branched claims. Add no 'Shmuel agrees with Rav' or 'Shmuel retracted' edge.

findings.claim: The Pumbedita report continues onto 153a:1. Unnamed people 'understood from it' that the rule applies only to giving to another. Rav Hisda said to them that when Rav Huna came from Kufri he explained it applies both to oneself and to others. The pilot job ends at 152b:8, so it lacks these people. Davidson identifies the unnamed group as 'Rav's disciples', which the Hebrew does not say. A later quotation (Bach) reads 'מבי כופר' for 'מכופרי'.

evidence.exact_quote: סבור מיניה הני מילי לאחר אבל לעצמו לא אמר להו רב חסדא כי אתא רב הונא מכופרי פירשה בין לעצמו בין לאחרים
Rav’s disciples understood from this
סבור מיניה הני מילי - דאין לאחר קנין כלום
אמר להו רב חסדא כי אתא רב הונא פירש' בין לעצמו בין לאחר
כי אתא רב הונא מבי כופר

findings.reasoning: Rashbam's lemma ties 'סבור מיניה' to Shmuel's answer 'אין לאחר קנין כלום', which exists only in the Pumbedita version. So this continuation depends on the Pumbedita branch. That dependency is an interpretation, but a well-grounded one. The subject of סבור מיניה is unnamed. Treating it as the בי רב senders is an editorial inference.
findings.graph_effect: Add, scoped to pumb_report: Rav Hisda speaks to an unnamed group (explicit). Rav Hisda reports that Rav Huna, arriving from Kufri, explained Shmuel's ruling (explicit report). Record the unnamed group as an unresolved coreference candidate with בי רב, not a merge.
findings.translation (this dossier): They understood from it: this applies [only] to another, but not to himself. Rav Hisda said to them: when Rav Huna came from Kufri he explained it: both to himself and to others.

findings.claim: The Gemara itself links the disputants of 152a and 152b ('they already disagreed about this once'). That is textual support for treating 'Rav' and 'Shmuel' as the same local persons across this sugya. The earlier contradiction at 152a:4 also names Rav's other statement through a sending chain: Ravin, in the name of Rabbi Abbahu, reports that Rabbi Elazar sent a ruling 'in the name of our teacher'. The Gemara counts that ruling as Rav's ('דרב אדרב').

evidence.exact_quote: והא אפליגו בה חדא זימנא במתנת שכיב מרע שכתוב בה קנין
ורמי דרב אדרב ודשמואל אדשמואל דשלח רבין משמיה דרבי אבהו הוו ידעי ששלח ר' אלעזר לגולה משום רבינו
in the name of our teacher, Rav

findings.reasoning: The link inside the sugya is the Gemara's own claim. It supports local coreference only, not a historical biography. The 152a:4 chain lies outside the pilot window. The identification of 'רבינו' as Rav rests on the Gemara's framing ('דרב אדרב') and on the Davidson gloss.
findings.graph_effect: Local coreference of Rav and Shmuel between 152a and 152b is supported by the text. Chains from wider context (Ravin ← Rabbi Abbahu ← Rabbi Elazar ← 'our teacher' = Rav) belong to 152a's job, marked as context and not added to this passage's claims.

findings.claim: Context persons just before the pilot window, 152b:1-3 (with 152a:7): Rav Nahman bar Yitzhak questions Rava. Rava answers ('where he enhances his power'). Rav Hisda defines the formula. Rav Yehuda reports Shmuel's ruling. The one who gestured ('ואחוי ליה בידיה') is unnamed in 152b:1. The Davidson edition supplies Rav Nahman.

lessons: 'בסורא מתנו הכי / בפומבדיתא מתנו הכי' introduces school-version alternatives. The places are where a version was taught, not where the people in it lived.

Formulas recur ('אמר רב ירמיה בר אבא שלחו ליה מבי רב לשמואל ילמדנו רבינו', 'אין לאחר קנין כלום'). The same formula in different tractates is a literary pattern, not one event and not evidence for identity.
The hypotheticals in a צריכא ('אימא מודה ליה') are the anonymous Gemara's rejected suppositions. They need a voice field distinct from the named sages and must never become agreement edges.
A group label that embeds a person ('בי רב') carries a name-based affiliation. Student relations and timing (such as 'after Rav's death') are not derivable from the label.
When a later line refers back to an earlier dispute with a bare name ('Rav'), keep the earlier transmission chain ('בי רב משמיה דרב') on the referenced statement.

Keep evidence types distinct: printed text; a commentator's lemma or citation; 'some books' reports; later 'צ"ל' emendation proposals; translators' glosses. The Davidson English and Steinsaltz Hebrew are one editorial work.
A reporter named with 'אמר' needs his own speech/transmission claim. Using him only as the 'voice' of the reported claims loses the speech turn.
Balanced rhetorical structure (a Rav half and a Shmuel half) is not evidence that both sages' positions are parallel. Commentators can dispute one half.

review.scope: I checked every dossier quote against its saved file in sources/ (all are present), and reread the graph-relevant findings and corrections against Bava Batra 152a-153a, Rashbam, Tosafot, Tosafot Rid, Ri Migash, Yad Ramah, Rif, Shita Mekubetzet, Rabbeinu Gershom and the Soncino HTML, plus the pilot output. I fetched nothing new, checked no manuscripts, and did not look at the Gittin, Shevuot or Sanhedrin pages beyond what the dossier saved.

findings.target: pilot entities giver, first, second, sick, others (not addressed in dossier or reading.md)
findings.reason: The pilot lists the donor and recipients of 'כתב לזה וכתב לזה', 'ראשון' / 'שני', and the 'שכיב מרע שכתב כל נכסיו לאחרים' of the question sent to Shmuel as kind 'person' or 'group'. These are roles in hypothetical legal cases: the anonymous Gemara's 'פשיטא' case, Rav and Shmuel's ruling, and a question framed as 'ילמדנו רבינו ... מהו'. They are not historical people. The dossier, and the previous review, left them as person nodes. They should be requalified as legal roles attached to their statements, with no person node and no edge to any sage.

findings.target: F13 / A3 (wording of the Pumbedita question)
findings.reason: The dossier misses the largest witness group, which has the short question 'קנו מידו מהו' with no 'שכיב מרע שכתב כל נכסיו לאחרים'. That group is Tosafot Rid's own text ('ילמדנו רבי' קנו מידו מהו'), Ri Migash, Yad Ramah and the Rosh as quoted in Shita Mekubetzet. Yad Ramah reads it as continuing the 'wrote and conferred' case ('כלומר קנו מידו לראשון, שכתב וזיכה לו'). The dossier also does not say that Tosafot Rid rejects his 'יש ספרים' reading. He rejects it because Sura and Pumbedita must disagree ('משמע דפליגי סוריא ופומבדיתא ואלו כן לא פליגי'). So A2 cannot count that remark as independent support for disagreement; a text choice made to keep the disagreement cannot then prove it. The pilot's 'sick' and 'others' roles belong only to the printed wording.

findings.target: F10 and the correction adding a בי רב -> Rav affiliation
findings.reason: Keeping the name-embedded link is right under project rules, and so is refusing any 'after Rav's death' scope, date or student_of edge. I found no traditional commentary in the saved files that mentions Rav's death here. But the dossier does not mark that 'בי רב' may be a fixed word for 'the academy' rather than the house of the person Rav. Soncino's main text renders it '[The following enquiry] was sent from the academy' and gives 'from the school of Rab' only as a bracketed alternative. The affiliation claim should carry a 'possibly generic term, not literal kinship or membership' flag.

findings.target: F8 and the correction adding a speech claim for Rav Yirmeya bar Abba
findings.reason: Support adding his own 'אמר' speech/transmission claim. It should be nested: the anonymous Gemara says 'בפומבדיתא מתנו הכי', and inside that teaching Rav Yirmeya bar Abba reports the exchange. Keep c8 child_of Abba, scoped to readings that carry 'בר אבא', and mark that the patronymic may be a fixed name. The Rosh as quoted in the Shita has only 'רב ירמיה', and the Rabbeinu Chananel version in Rashbam ('בפומבדיתא מתנו שלחו מבי רב לשמואל') has no reporter at all; both should be recorded as name-form evidence, not as a reading that deletes him. Drop the dossier's remark that 153a:8 'fits someone tied to Rav's rulings'. There the speaker of 'אמר הכא אתרא דשמואל' is unnamed in the Hebrew (Davidson supplies Rav Nahman), and the line says nothing about what the man in Shum Tamya holds or who he is tied to.

findings.target: F3 / A6 and the correction adding the 152a transmission chain
findings.reason: The Wikisource text at 152a:1 does read 'בי רב משמיה דרב אמרי ארכביה אתרי ריכשי ושמואל אמר לא ידענא מאי אדון בה'. Recording Shmuel's earlier position as doubt, not 'second acquires', is correct, and so is keeping Rif's and the Shita's 'רב אמר' as citation witnesses. But Rashbam's lemma 'בי רב אמרי ארכביה כו'' is abbreviated with כו'. Its lack of 'משמיה דרב' is weak evidence and should not become a branch that drops Rav as the source. This chain belongs to the 152a claim; it is referenced from 152b, not added to it.

findings.target: F15 and the correction extending pumb_report to 153a:1
findings.reason: Explicit: Rav Hisda speaks ('אמר להו רב חסדא'). His addressee is marked by 'להו' and is the unnamed subject of 'סבור מיניה'. Also explicit: Rav Huna came from Kufri and explained 'it'. Interpretation: that 'it' ('פירשה') is Shmuel's Pumbedita answer. That rests on Rashbam's gloss 'סבור מיניה הני מילי - דאין לאחר קנין כלום', so the dossier's 'explicit report' label should apply to the speech, not to the object. Store the Rav Huna -> Rav Hisda report once. Note that Ri Migash's quotation lacks 'מכופרי', and that 153a:2 ('ההוא דקנו מיניה אתא לקמיה דרב הונא') is a separate precedent story with an unnamed litigant.

findings.target: F1 / F2 and the corrections to c6, c7
findings.reason: The words 'אימא מודה ליה לשמואל' and 'אימא מודה ליה לרב', framed by 'צריכא', are the anonymous Gemara's rejected suppositions. Keeping them hypothetical and rejected, with no agreement edge, is right. The voice change is mostly a relabel of the pilot's 'narrator'. Rashbam's lemma 'אבל בהך - בתרייתא דלא קנו מיניה ... ואימא מודה לשמואל' does belong to the first half, so the dossier's lemma-variant note points at the right occurrence. Tosafot's own quotation reads 'אי איתמר בההיא בההיא קאמר רב'. That is a citation witness that differs from Rabbeinu Gershom's 'נראה דצ"ל' emendation, and the two should be stored as different evidence types.

c5 ('Rav opposes secondwins') restates the one dispute 'רב אמר ראשון קנה ושמואל אמר שני קנה' and is not a second observation. The same logic applies to pilot c11 ('Shmuel holds_view answer'). It rests on the same words 'שלח להו אין אחר קנין כלום' as c10, so it should be marked as derived from c10 rather than counted separately.

findings.target: F11 (Tosafot: אמרי בי רב = Rav Huna)
findings.reason: Tosafot's 'ועוד דאמרי בי רב הכא ואמרי בי רב היינו רב הונא' belongs to their argument about whether Rav Huna followed his teacher Rav. So 'הכא' points at the 152a:1 'בי רב משמיה דרב אמרי', not the 152b:8 senders. The dossier scopes it correctly as a commentary-sourced candidate. The same Tosafot passage quotes 'והא רב הונא תלמידיה דרב הוה' from Shabbat. That is a quotation of another passage and must not enter this passage's graph as a student_of edge.

The text says only 'כי אתא רב דימי אמר דייתיקי מבטלת דייתיקי'. 'From Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia' is Davidson's addition. At 135b the line answers 'מאי תיבדק' after 'ור' יוחנן אמר תיבדק' without saying Rav Dimi got it from Rabbi Yohanan. The Jerusalem Talmud's 'תני רבן שמעון בן גמליאל אומר דייתיקי מבטלת דייתיקי' is a parallel attribution in another corpus. No origin, destination or transmission edge follows from any of these.

cases.question: In Bava Batra 170b:4, who challenges Rav Huna's report of Rav's ruling, who answers, and whose teaching is the baraita? Which graph claims are explicit, which rest on interpretation, and which alternatives must stay open? The first reading is checked against 170a-171a, the Yerushalmi parallel, translations, commentaries and codes.

findings.claim: The Bavli gives the challenger as two reported alternatives: Rav Nahman, or ("and some say") Rav Yirmiyah bar Abba. Both speak to Rav Huna. The first reading keeps these as two branches of one reading group. That is correct.

evidence.exact_quote: אמר ליה רב נחמן לרב הונא ואמרי לה רב ירמיה בר אבא לרב הונא
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: Rav Nahman said to Rav Huna, and some say [it was] Rav Yirmiyah bar Abba to Rav Huna.

evidence.exact_quote: Said R. Nahman to R. Huna, and others say [that] R. Jeremiah b. Abba said to R. Huna

findings.reasoning: ואמרי לה is the editors' formula for a second transmission of the same exchange. The text does not choose between them. It does not say both men spoke, or that only one did historically.
findings.graph_effect: Keep reading group 'challenger' with branches nachman_version and yirmiya_version. Do not merge Rav Nahman and Rav Yirmiyah bar Abba. Do not treat the two branches as two historical challenges.

findings.claim: The Aramaic does not name the person who replies 'he heard it and did not retract' (170b:5). It says only 'he said to him'. Rav Huna as the speaker comes from the local exchange. The William Davidson English and Steinsaltz Hebrew add 'Rav Huna' as the editors' explanation, in plain text. Soncino leaves the speaker unnamed.

evidence.exact_quote: אמר ליה שמיע ליה ולא הדר ביה
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: He said to him: He [Rav] heard it and did not retract.

evidence.exact_quote: Rav Huna said to him: Rav heard the baraita, and nevertheless he did not retract his statement.
evidence.location: Bava Batra 170b:5, William Davidson English; 'Rav Huna' is plain (editor's) text

evidence.exact_quote: אמר ליה [לו] רב הונא:
evidence.location: Steinsaltz on Bava Batra 170b:5; רב הונא is outside the bold text

evidence.exact_quote: He said unto him: He heard it and he did not withdraw.

findings.reasoning: The challenge is addressed to Rav Huna. He transmits Rav's ruling, and the reply defends Rav. So Rav Huna is the natural speaker. That rests on reading the conversation, not on a name. The William Davidson English and the Steinsaltz Hebrew belong to one editorial project. They are not two independent witnesses. Rashbam (170b:5) and Rabbeinu Gershom (170b:11) explain the reply without naming who gives it.
findings.graph_effect: Keep c7/c10 with basis local_coreference. Add a note that the speaker's name is not in the Aramaic. Its addressee is whichever challenger the branch selects.

findings.claim: The baraita quoted at 170b:4 is identified by the Gemara itself at 171a:5 ('What is the baraita?'). There it is attributed to Rabbi Yehuda, and Rabbi Yosi gives the opposing view. The first reading stored the baraita with no attribution.

evidence.exact_quote: מאי ברייתא דתניא הרי שהיו נושין בו אלף זוז ופרע מהן חמש מאות זוז עדים מקרעין את השטר וכותבין לו שטר אחר מזמן ראשון דברי רבי יהודה רבי יוסי אומר שטר זה יהא מונח במקומו ויכתבו שובר
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: What is the baraita? As it is taught: If a thousand zuz were owed by him and he repaid five hundred of them, witnesses tear up the document and write him another document from the first date - the words of Rabbi Yehuda. Rabbi Yosi says: this document shall stay in its place and they write a receipt.

evidence.exact_quote: לקמן בשמעתין במילתיה דר' יהודה בפורע חצי חובו שמקרעין עדים
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: below in our discussion, in the statement of Rabbi Yehuda about one who repays half his debt, that witnesses tear up...

findings.reasoning: The focal segment quotes only the first line, without an attribution. The fuller text on the next amud names the Tannaitic speaker. The William Davidson English at 170b:4 adds 'according to Rabbi Yehuda' in plain text. That is supported by 171a:5 but is not in the 170b:4 Aramaic.
findings.graph_effect: Add attributed_to(baraita statement -> Rabbi Yehuda, within the baraita, evidence 171a:5). Add Rabbi Yosi's baraita view (receipt) as a separate statement. Link the 170b:4 excerpt to the 171a:5 baraita as the same quoted source (explicit cross-reference). This makes the hearing event in c11 an event about a teaching attributed to Rabbi Yehuda. It does not make Rav meet Rabbi Yehuda.

findings.claim: The context the first reading said was missing is on the same amud. The Mishnah at 170b:2 gives Rabbi Yehuda's rule ('he should exchange') and Rabbi Yosi's rule ('he should write a receipt'). It also contains a speech exchange: Rabbi Yehuda objects, and Rabbi Yosi answers him.

evidence.exact_quote: מי שפרע מקצת חובו ר' יהודה אומר יחליף רבי יוסי אומר יכתוב שובר אמר רבי יהודה נמצא זה צריך להיות שומר שוברו מן העכברים אמר לו רבי יוסי כך יפה לו ולא ירע כחו של זה
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: One who repaid part of his debt - Rabbi Yehuda says: he should exchange [the note]; Rabbi Yosi says: he should write a receipt. Rabbi Yehuda said: then this one must guard his receipt from mice! Rabbi Yosi said to him: this is good for him, and the other's power will not be weakened.

findings.reasoning: The pilot job began at the Gemara (170b:3), so the Mishnah was not supplied. The pronoun in אמר לו ('said to him') has Rabbi Yehuda as its antecedent. This is a Mishnaic literary dispute. It records a reply in the text. It does not show that the two met in person.
findings.graph_effect: Fill y_rule with 'the debtor exchanges the note' and yosi_rule with 'write a receipt' (evidence 170b:2). Add a Mishnah-level speech pair: Rabbi Yehuda objects to Rabbi Yosi's view, and Rabbi Yosi answers Rabbi Yehuda. Label it as a literary dispute, not a meeting. Close episode.needed_context.

findings.claim: Commentators disagree on what Rav rejects in Rabbi Yehuda's view, and so on why the challenge had force. Rashbam: Rabbi Yehuda lets witnesses re-issue the note from the first date, and Rav requires a court. Rashbam calls Rav a Tanna who may dispute a baraita. Tosafot (the Ri) and Tosfot HaRosh (quoted in Shita Mekubetzet) object. They say Rav understood Rabbi Yehuda to mean the second date.

evidence.exact_quote: שאמר יחליף ואפילו לכתוב לו מזמן ראשון על ידי עדים בלא בית דין
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: who said 'he should exchange', even to write it for him from the first date by witnesses without a court.

evidence.exact_quote: ורב תנא הוא ופליג
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: and Rav is a Tanna and disputes.

evidence.exact_quote: דברייתא תני עדים מקרעין ואיהו אמר ב"ד דוקא ולא עדים
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: for the baraita teaches 'witnesses tear up', and he said specifically a court, not witnesses.

evidence.exact_quote: ונראה לר"י דרב נחמן סבר לה למילתיה דרב הכי אין הלכה כרבי יהודה דאמר יחליף וכותבין ליה מזמן שני
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: The Ri thinks that Rav Nahman understood Rav's statement thus: the halakha is not like Rabbi Yehuda, who said he exchanges and they write it from the second date.

evidence.exact_quote: ונראה לפרש אין הלכה כרבי יהודה דאמר יחליף מזמן שני
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: It seems right to explain: the halakha is not like Rabbi Yehuda, who said he exchanges from the second date.

findings.reasoning: Both readings accept the Gemara's words. They differ on the content of Rabbi Yehuda's view as Rav or the challenger understood it. Tosfot HaRosh is quoted inside Shita Mekubetzet and argues like Tosafot. Tosafot and Tosfot HaRosh are one line of reasoning, not two independent witnesses.
findings.graph_effect: c3 ('Rav does not rule like Rabbi Yehuda') stays explicit. Its content role (y_rule) should be the Mishnah's words 'he should exchange'. Neither commentator's gloss should be stored as the rule. Store the Rashbam and Tosafot readings as commentary-level interpretations of Rav's objection. Do not store either as part of the Talmud's own claim.

findings.claim: The only later commentators found here to name the challenger (Tosafot, Tosfot HaRosh) name Rav Nahman. They do not mention the alternative. Rashbam, Rabbeinu Gershom and the Ramban name no challenger.

evidence.exact_quote: אבל רב נחמן לא היה סובר מילתיה דרב הכי דא"כ מאי הא דקאמר לרב הונא אי שמיע ליה כו'
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: but Rav Nahman did not understand Rav's statement so, for if so, what is this that he said to Rav Huna, 'if he had heard...'.

evidence.exact_quote: מאי קאמר ליה רב נחמן אי שמיע ליה לרב הא דתניא
אי שמיעא ליה לרב הא דתניא. דבקריעת עדים סגי
אי שמיט ליה הא דתניא עדים מקרעין הוה הדר ביה

findings.reasoning: Commentators often use the first-named alternative as a label. That is not a ruling that the 'some say' version is wrong. The Ramban's lemma prints שמיט where the Talmud reads שמיע. That looks like a typographical or transmission error in this edition. I record it and draw nothing from it.
findings.graph_effect: Do not use Tosafot or Tosfot HaRosh to prefer nachman_version. Keep historical_compatibility 'unknown'.

findings.claim: The Yerushalmi has a parallel remark with only one challenger: 'Rabbi Yirmiyah said: had Rav heard the teaching, he would not have said this.' Rav's ruling there is 'they make him a court confirmation', and the opposing teaching is taught by Rabbi Hiyya. The parallel has no Rav Nahman, no Rav Huna as addressee, and no reply that Rav heard and held firm.

evidence.exact_quote: רב אמר עושין לו קיום בית דין תני ר' חייה אין עושין לו קיום ב"ד. א"ר ירמיה אילו שמע רב מתנייה לא הוה מימר הדא מילתא.
evidence.location: Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 10:6:2, Mechon-Mamre text
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: Rav said: they make a court confirmation for him. Rabbi Hiyya taught: they do not make a court confirmation for him. Rabbi Yirmiyah said: had Rav heard the teaching, he would not have said this thing.

evidence.exact_quote: אמר רבי ירמיה אילו שמע רב מתנייה לא הוה מימר הדא מילתא
evidence.location: Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 10:6:2, Venice edition text

findings.reasoning: This is a separate literary witness, not a manuscript variant of the Bavli. The name there is plain 'רבי ירמיה', with no patronymic. The rulings are close but worded differently. So the parallel shows that one tradition put a Yirmiyah in this role. It does not settle the Bavli's ואמרי לה. It does not show that Rav Nahman did not speak, or that the two Talmuds report the same event.
findings.graph_effect: Add a cross-text parallel link from the Bavli yirmiya_version branch to JT Bava Batra 10:6:2. Mark it parallel_tradition, not identity or corroboration. Keep 'רבי ירמיה' (JT) as a separate local person until the identity decision is made. Do not add Rabbi Hiyya to the Bavli focal graph. findings.claim: Two Yerushalmi commentaries identify the Yerushalmi's Rabbi Yirmiyah with a Babylonian Rav Yirmiyah. Sha'arei Torat Eretz Yisrael says he is Rabbi Yirmiyah bar Abba and points to Bavli 170b. The Guggenheimer English note says he is 'Rav Jeremiah, Babylonian of the first generation'. These are identifications made by commentators.

evidence.exact_quote: ור' ירמיה זה הוא ר' ירמיה בר אבא וכ"ה בבבלי ק"ע ב'
evidence.location: Sha'arei Torat Eretz Yisrael on JT Bava Batra 10:6:2:2
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: and this Rabbi Yirmiyah is Rabbi Yirmiyah bar Abba, and so it is in the Bavli 170b.

evidence.exact_quote: He is Rav Jeremiah, Babylonian of the first generation.
evidence.location: Guggenheimer English, JT Bava Batra 10:6:2, footnote 84

findings.reasoning: The identification rests on the shared name, the shared role (commenting on Rav's ruling) and the Bavli's ואמרי לה. Those are real reasons. But a shared name does not establish identity, and the commentators do not report a manuscript with the patronymic in the Yerushalmi. The same Sha'arei Torat Eretz Yisrael comment also proposes an emendation: צ"ל ... מתניתא. That is a later proposed correction, not a source variant.
findings.graph_effect: Record a provisional identity candidate (JT רבי ירמיה = Bavli רב ירמיה בר אבא), sourced to these two commentators, in the identity layer only. Do not merge the nodes in the passage graph.

findings.claim: Yerushalmi commentators disagree about which teaching Rabbi Yirmiyah means, and so about how close the parallel is. Penei Moshe: the teaching Rabbi Hiyya taught, that a court is not needed. Mareh HaPanim: the same as the Bavli's baraita at 170b. Noam Yerushalmi ties Rav's statement to a different case (a blotted note, citing the Bei Levi Ketubot baraita). The Guggenheimer notes say the Halakhah refers to 'Mishnah 9'.

evidence.exact_quote: אלו שמע רב להא מתנייה דתני ר' חייא דאין צריך ב"ד לא הוה מימר הדא מילתא דדוקא בב"ד והוי חזר ביה
evidence.location: Penei Moshe on JT Bava Batra 10:6:2:3
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: had Rav heard this teaching that Rabbi Hiyya taught, that a court is not needed, he would not have said this - that it is specifically by a court - and he would have retracted.

evidence.exact_quote: והכי אמר התם בדף ק"ע ע"ב אי שמיעא ליה לרב הא ברייתא דתניא עדים מקרעין את השטר
evidence.location: Mareh HaPanim on JT Bava Batra 10:6:2:1
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: and so it says there, on 170b: 'if Rav had heard this baraita, as taught: witnesses tear up the document'.

evidence.exact_quote: אלו הוה שמע רב הברייתא דלעיל הא הני בכתובות דבי לוי שמי שנמחק שט"ח מעמיד עליו עדים ובא לב"ד
evidence.translation_mine: My translation (tentative; the sentence is compressed): had Rav heard the baraita above, taught in the Ketubot of Bei Levi, that one whose note was blotted brings witnesses and comes to court...

evidence.exact_quote: This refers to Mishnah 9.
evidence.location: Guggenheimer English, JT Bava Batra 10:6:2, footnote 83

findings.claim: The reason for Rav's requirement follows at 171a:1: a court can reassign property, but witnesses who have done their task cannot do it again. The Aramaic does not say who speaks. The first reading's range ends at 170b:5, so it is unclear whether this is Rav Huna's continued answer or the anonymous Gemara.

evidence.exact_quote: בשלמא בי דינא אלימי לאפקועי ממונא אלא עדים שעשו שליחותן חוזרין ועושין שליחותן
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: Granted, a court is empowered to expropriate money; but witnesses who performed their agency - can they go back and perform their agency again?

evidence.exact_quote: While Rabbi Yehuda says in the baraita that the witnesses write a new promissory note, Rav maintains that this must be done specifically by a court. Why is this?

findings.reasoning: The William Davidson editors add 'Why is this?' in plain text. That frames 171a:1 as the reason, without naming a speaker. Rashbam explains its content, also without naming one. The next line, 171a:2 (ולא והא), is a new anonymous challenge. Assigning 171a:1 to Rav Huna would add a speech claim the text does not make.
findings.graph_effect: Store 171a:1 as an anonymous (stam) explanation of Rav's view. Do not store it as Rav Huna's speech, and not as Rav's own words. Leave the question open.
