lessons: A baraita excerpt quoted without attribution may be given in full, with its Tannaitic attribution, a few lines later ('מאי ברייתא'). The statement node should be linked to that fuller quotation, and the attribution recorded from there. It should not be left unattributed or taken from a translator's plain-text addition.

A parallel in the other Talmud is a separate literary witness. It should be stored as parallel_tradition linked to a branch. It should not be stored as a variant or as corroboration. It does not decide a Bavli ואמרי לה.
When a reply is introduced only by אמר ליה, the replier should be stored as an inferred speaker. Where the evidence for the name is an editor's plain text, the record should say so.
A Mishnah's 'X said ... Y said to him' is a literary speech pair. It should be recorded as a speech claim with a literary-dispute label, not as a scene or meeting.
A commentator who names only the first alternative (for example, Tosafot's 'רב נחמן') is using a label. That should not count as preferring one branch.

review.scope: I checked every person, speaker, addressee, attribution, parallel and identity claim in dossier.json and reading.md (F01-F15 and the nine proposed corrections) against the saved sources in sources/ (Bavli 170b-171a in Wikisource, William Davidson and Soncino, Rashbam, Tosafot, Shita Mekubetzet, Ramban, Rabbeinu Gershom, Steinsaltz, the Yerushalmi and its commentators, the codes) and against the first reading's entities; I fetched nothing new and did not check manuscripts or variant apparatus.

findings.target: pilot entity 'recipient' (m10, the pronoun לו) and the Mishnah's זה / של זה in F04
findings.reason: The first reading typed 'Recipient of the replacement document' (from וכותבין לו in Rav's ruling) as kind person, and the dossier's review_assessment passes over it. It is a legal role in a legal rule, not a person. The same applies to the Mishnah's נמצא זה צריך and ולא ירע כחו של זה that F04 brings in, and to the witnesses and the court in the baraita. These should be stored as legal roles (debtor, creditor, witnesses, court) with no person node and no place in the people graph.

The graph_effect sources the candidate 'JT רבי ירמיה = Bavli רב ירמיה בר אבא' to 'these two commentators', but only Sha'arei Torat Eretz Yisrael says 'ר' ירמיה בר אבא'. Guggenheimer's note 84 says only 'He is Rav Jeremiah, Babylonian of the first generation', with no patronymic. Sha'arei's own basis is the Bavli ('וכ"ה בבבלי ק"ע ב''), in a comment that also emends the line (צ"ל ... מתניתא) and declares the intervening text superfluous ('ומה שבינתיים מיותר'). So the identification cannot later be counted as support for the Bavli yirmiya_version branch, because that would be circular. The child_of(Abba) claim (c13) stays with the Bavli branch and must not be copied onto the Yerushalmi's רבי ירמיה, who has no patronymic in any of the three saved texts.

findings.target: F03 / proposed correction 'baraita (entity)' / reading.md 'The baraita is Rabbi Yehuda's'
findings.reason: The occurrence is right. The words at 170b:4 (עדים מקרעין את השטר וכותבין לו שטר אחר מזמן ראשון) are the first view of the baraita the Gemara quotes in full at 171a:5, and not the Mishnah at 170b:2. But 171a:5 attributes that view ('דברי רבי יהודה') and gives a second view to Rabbi Yosi inside the same baraita. So attributed_to should hang on the quoted excerpt (the 'baraita' statement node), not on the whole baraita, and reading.md's 'The baraita is Rabbi Yehuda's' should be narrowed to match. The 'according to Rabbi Yehuda' in the William Davidson English and 'בשיטתו של ר' יהודה' in Steinsaltz at 170b:4 are unbolded editorial words from one project. They are not a second witness.

Only the second speech marks an addressee: 'אמר לו רבי יוסי' ('Rabbi Yosi said to him'), whose לו points back to Rabbi Yehuda. Rabbi Yehuda's 'אמר רבי יהודה נמצא זה צריך להיות שומר שוברו מן העכברים' has no addressee in the text. Store it with Rabbi Yosi's rule as its target and leave the addressee empty. The literary-dispute label, and the rule that this is not a meeting, stay as the dossier has them.

The dossier proposes the label 'the debtor exchanges the note', but the Mishnah says only 'יחליף' ('he should exchange') and does not name who does it. The saved translations disagree: the William Davidson English has 'The creditor should exchange', and Soncino has 'HE SHALL EXCHANGE [HIS BOND FOR ANOTHER]'. The dossier's own F05 says to store the Mishnah's word rather than a gloss. Label y_rule 'יחליף: he should exchange [the note], subject unstated' and yosi_rule 'יכתוב שובר: he should write a receipt', both with evidence 170b:2.

Tosafot does not simply oppose Rashbam. It says Rashbam's reading fits the Gemara's conclusion ('וכן הוא לפי המסקנא דשמיע ליה ברייתא ולא הדר'). The Ri's second-date reading is offered as how the challenger, under the label 'רב נחמן', understood Rav ('ונראה לר"י דרב נחמן סבר לה למילתיה דרב הכי'). The Ramban 170b:2 takes the same line ('משום שהיה סבור מזמן שני קאמר'), and Tosfot HaRosh openly depends on Tosafot ('ככתוב בתוספות'). So this is one line of reasoning, not three votes. If it is stored, it is a commentary-level claim about what the challenger and the replier each took Rav to mean. It is not a Talmud claim, and it is not a view held by Rav.

The baraita continues at 171a:6: 'ומפני שני דברים אמרו כותבין שובר' ('for two reasons they said one writes a receipt'). The dossier stops at Rabbi Yosi's receipt line. The William Davidson English opens this line with 'Rabbi Yosei continues', but in plain (editorial) type. The Aramaic has only an unnamed 'אמרו' ('they said'). Add it as a statement inside the baraita. Its voice is open, either Rabbi Yosi continuing or the unnamed Sages he cites, with low confidence, and it is not attributed to Rabbi Yosi on the editors' word alone.

The Wikisource and vocalized Aramaic read only 'אמר ליה שמיע ליה ולא הדר ביה', and Soncino has 'He said unto him'. 'Rav Huna' appears only unbolded in the William Davidson English and after the bold 'אמר ליה' in Steinsaltz, which is one editorial project. Keeping c7/c10 with basis local_coreference, and adding a note that the name is not in the Aramaic, is correct. The addressee (ליה) is marked, and it is whichever challenger the branch selects.

'בשלמא בי דינא אלימי לאפקועי ממונא אלא עדים שעשו שליחותן חוזרין ועושין שליחותן' names no speaker. The William Davidson 'Why is this?' is editorial plain text. Mareh HaPanim runs the reply and the reason together ('דשמיע ליה ולא הדר ביה דעדים שעשו שליחותן אין חוזרין'), but that is a paraphrase explaining Rav's view, not evidence that Rav Huna spoke it. Storing it as the anonymous Gemara, and leaving the question open, is the narrow choice.

findings.target: F01, F06, F07 (challenger branches and the Yerushalmi parallel)
findings.reason: 170b:4 reads 'אמר ליה רב נחמן לרב הונא ואמרי לה רב ירמיה בר אבא לרב הונא', so two reported alternatives both addressed to Rav Huna. Tosafot's and Shita's use of 'רב נחמן' is a label, not a choice between the branches. The Yerushalmi line 'א"ר ירמיה אילו שמע רב מתנייה לא הוה מימר הדא מילתא' has no Rav Nahman, no Rav Huna and no reply. Storing it as a parallel tradition with disputed closeness, and keeping Rabbi Hiyya ('תני ר' חייה') out of the Bavli graph, is correct.

quote_checks.exact_quote: מאי ברייתא דתניא הרי שהיו נושין בו אלף זוז ופרע מהן חמש מאות זוז עדים מקרעין את השטר וכותבין לו שטר אחר מזמן ראשון דברי רבי יהודה רבי יוסי אומר שטר זה יהא מונח במקומו ויכתבו שובר
quote_checks.note: 171a:5. The correct occurrence for the 170b:4 excerpt. The attribution covers the witnesses view; Rabbi Yosi holds a second view in the same baraita.

quote_checks.exact_quote: ומפני שני דברים אמרו כותבין שובר אחת כדי שיכוף לפורעו ואחת כדי שיגבה מזמן ראשון
quote_checks.note: 171a:6. Not covered by the dossier. The speaker is an unnamed 'אמרו'; 'Rabbi Yosei continues' appears only as William Davidson editorial text.

quote_checks.exact_quote: מי שפרע מקצת חובו ר' יהודה אומר יחליף רבי יוסי אומר יכתוב שובר אמר רבי יהודה נמצא זה צריך להיות שומר שוברו מן העכברים אמר לו רבי יוסי כך יפה לו ולא ירע כחו של זה
quote_checks.note: 170b:2 Mishnah. Supports the filled rules and the speech pair. Only Rabbi Yosi's reply marks an addressee (לו). The subject of יחליף is unstated, so the dossier's 'the debtor exchanges' label is not in the words.

quote_checks.exact_quote: Rabbi Yehuda says: The creditor should exchange the promissory note
quote_checks.note: The William Davidson English makes the creditor the subject, which contradicts the dossier's proposed y_rule label 'the debtor exchanges the note'. Soncino has 'HE SHALL EXCHANGE [HIS BOND FOR ANOTHER]'.

quote_checks.exact_quote: רב אמר עושין לו קיום בית דין תני ר' חייה אין עושין לו קיום ב"ד. א"ר ירמיה אילו שמע רב מתנייה לא הוה מימר הדא מילתא.
quote_checks.note: Mechon-Mamre text. The Venice and Guggenheimer texts agree on 'רבי ירמיה' with no patronymic. No Rav Nahman, no Rav Huna, no reply.

quote_checks.exact_quote: He is Rav Jeremiah, Babylonian of the first generation.
quote_checks.note: Guggenheimer note 84. It supports F08's claim text ('a Babylonian Rav Yirmiyah') but not the graph_effect, which cites both commentators for identity with Rav Yirmiyah bar Abba. No patronymic is given here.

quote_checks.note: This is the only source for the bar Abba identification, and its stated basis is the Bavli itself. The same comment emends (צ"ל ... מתניתא) and cuts intervening text ('ומה שבינתיים מיותר').

quote_checks.exact_quote: וכן הוא לפי המסקנא דשמיע ליה ברייתא ולא הדר דאיהו מכשר בעדים ואיהו מצריך ב"ד
quote_checks.note: The dossier leaves this out. Tosafot accepts Rashbam's reading for the conclusion and gives the Ri's second-date reading as the challenger's ('רב נחמן') understanding. F05's 'Tosafot objects' is too broad.

quote_checks.exact_quote: וְכוֹתְבִין לוֹ בֵּית דִּין שְׁטָר אַחֵר בִּשְׁאָר הַחוֹב מִזְּמַן רִאשׁוֹן אֲבָל לֹא עֵדֵי הַשְּׁטָר
quote_checks.note: Present in the saved text: it matches after Unicode NFC normalization (the vowel marks are stored in a different order). This is a reception note only, with no people.

cases.question: In Menachot 62a:12, who answers the objection to Rabbi's side-by-side waving, and in which direction? Who owns the baraita citation that follows? Which people and relations in 62a:11-13 are explicit, which rest on interpretation, and which alternatives must stay open?

findings.claim: The answer to the objection is reported in two directions: Rav Hisda to Rav Hamnuna, and 'some say' Rav Hamnuna to Rav Hisda. Only the direction differs; the content of the answer is the same in both.

evidence.exact_quote: והא בעינן על א"ל רב חסדא לרב המנונא ואמרי לה רב המנונא לרב חסדא רבי לטעמיה דאמר על בסמוך
evidence.note: Wikisource Talmud Bavli, 62a:12

evidence.exact_quote: In response, Rav Ḥisda says to Rav Hamnuna, and some say that Rav Hamnuna says to Rav Ḥisda:
evidence.note: William Davidson English 62a:12; bold = Aramaic, plain = editor

evidence.exact_quote: R. Hisda said to R. Hamnuna (others say, R. Hamnuna said to R. Hisda), Rabbi
evidence.note: Soncino 62a

findings.reasoning: Translation (mine): 'Rav Hisda said to Rav Hamnuna, and some say Rav Hamnuna to Rav Hisda: Rabbi follows his own reasoning, for he said al means next to.' Every Hebrew/Aramaic witness checked in the Bavli and both English translations keep both directions. The Davidson and Soncino English are separate translations, but both translate the same printed Bavli text, so they confirm the reading of that text, not an independent tradition.
findings.graph_effect: Keep one reading group with two branches (speaker and addressee swap). Both branches share one fact: the report pairs these two sages in one said-to exchange about Rabbi's view. That pairing can be one branch-invariant, undirected co-mention edge. Directed 'speaks to' and 'explains' edges stay branch-scoped. Neither branch is evidence that the two historically met.

findings.claim: The same reversible attribution formula recurs: again on this page at 62a:19 (on the dispute between Rabbi and the Sages about waving after slaughter), at Menachot 98a:19 (word for word the same answer and baraita, on a different law), and at Shabbat 97a:17. The exact-phrase search returned these four Bavli segments.

evidence.exact_quote: במאי קא מיפלגי אמר ליה רב חסדא לרב המנונא ואמרי לה רב המנונא לרב חסדא
evidence.note: Wikisource 62a:19

evidence.exact_quote: אמר ליה רב חסדא לרב המנונא ואמרי לה רב המנונא לרב חסדא רבי לטעמיה דאמר על בסמוך דתניא רבי אומר
evidence.note: Wikisource 98a:19

evidence.exact_quote: רבי אומר רואין את העליונה כאילו אינה והא בעינן (ויקרא כד, ז) ונתת על
evidence.note: Wikisource 98a:18, the different ruling that the same answer defends there

evidence.exact_quote: אמר ליה רב חסדא לרב המנונא ואמרי לה רב המנונא לרב חסדא מנא הא מילתא
evidence.note: Wikisource Shabbat 97a:17

evidence.exact_quote: Shabbat 97a:17
Menachot 98a:19
Menachot 62a:19
Menachot 62a:12

findings.reasoning: The four Bavli segments (Menachot 62a:12, 62a:19, 98a:19; Shabbat 97a:17) are the Bavli hits in the saved search. The other hits are Steinsaltz, Tosafot and modern commentary. The search is exact-phrase only, so it does not prove there are no other occurrences with different spelling. 62a:12 and 98a:19 share the answer and the baraita word for word, in support of two different rulings of Rabbi. That suggests one transmitted answer used in two places (a historical-literary inference, not stated by the text).
findings.graph_effect: Link 62a:12 and 98a:19 as parallel passages carrying one answer. Do not count them as two independent observations of a Hisda-Hamnuna exchange. 62a:19 and Shabbat 97a:17 have different content and can count as separate attestations of the pair, but they carry the same unresolved direction.

findings.claim: It is not fixed whether the baraita citation that follows (דתניא 'as it is taught') belongs to the speech of Rav Hisda/Rav Hamnuna or is the anonymous Talmud's supporting citation.

evidence.exact_quote: דתניא (ויקרא כד, ז) ונתת על המערכת לבונה זכה רבי אומר על בסמוך
evidence.note: Wikisource 62a:13

evidence.exact_quote: This is as it is taught in a baraita:
evidence.note: Davidson English 62a:13: a new sentence and a separate segment; 'This is' is plain editor's text

evidence.exact_quote: follows his general view that ‘al means ‘near to’; as it was taught:
evidence.note: Soncino continues the same sentence with a semicolon; no quotation marks close the speech

evidence.exact_quote: דתניא [שכן שנויה ברייתא]
evidence.note: Steinsaltz: 'for a baraita teaches', no speaker named

evidence.exact_quote: כדתניא (ויקרא כד, ז) ונתת על המערכת לבונה זכה רבי אומר על בסמוך
evidence.note: Sotah 37a:10: the same baraita cited with no amora present

evidence.exact_quote: This is as it is taught in a baraita that Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:
evidence.note: Davidson English 98a:19

findings.reasoning: The Aramaic has no marker that closes the amora's words. The Davidson English separates the citation into a new sentence. Soncino runs it on. Steinsaltz, Rashi and Rabbeinu Gershom explain the proof but do not say who cites it. In Sotah 37a the same baraita is used by the anonymous voice with no amora, so the citation can function without an amoraic speaker. That shows it is possible, not that it happens here. None of the commentaries checked addresses the boundary.
findings.graph_effect: Add a reading group 'citation_boundary' with branches 'amora_cites' (the citation belongs to whichever speaker the direction group chose) and 'anonymous_cites' (editorial voice). Claim c7 should not be voiced 'narrator' without that note. Rabbi's own baraita teaching (c6) is shared across both branches.

findings.claim: The objection 'But we require al' is anonymous. The text does not say that the addressee (Hamnuna or Hisda) raised it.

evidence.exact_quote: The Gemara raises an objection to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi: But we require
evidence.note: Davidson English; the attribution to 'the Gemara' is plain editor's text

evidence.exact_quote: ומקשים על שיטת רבי: והא בעינן
evidence.note: Steinsaltz: 'they object to Rabbi's view', impersonal

evidence.exact_quote: וְהָא בָּעִינַן "עַל", רַבִּי לְטַעְמֵהּ, דְּאָמַר "עַל" בְּסָמוּךְ, דְּתַנְיָא
evidence.note: Yalkut: question and answer both anonymous

findings.reasoning: Translation (mine): 'But we require al!' The question comes before 'X said to Y' with no speaker. Reading it as the addressee's question is possible under the 'said to' formula but is not stated. Compare Shabbat 97a:17, where the pair's exchange itself contains the question.
findings.graph_effect: Keep the questioner as an anonymous editorial voice, not a person or a group of people. Do not add 'asks' edges from Hamnuna or Hisda.

findings.claim: Rabbi appears three times in the focal unit (the waving baraita, the answer, and the frankincense baraita). The Talmud itself links the second to the first two with 'Rabbi follows his own reasoning'. No Hebrew/Aramaic witness checked expands the name. 'Yehuda HaNasi' appears only in the editor's plain text of the Davidson English and in Steinsaltz's modern framing.

evidence.exact_quote: רבי לטעמיה דאמר על בסמוך
evidence.note: Wikisource 62a:12

evidence.exact_quote: רבי אומר על בסמוך אתה אומר על בסמוך
evidence.note: Wikisource 62a:13

evidence.exact_quote: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says, in objection to this opinion:
evidence.note: Davidson English 62a:11; 'Yehuda HaNasi' is not bold

findings.reasoning: 'לטעמיה' (to his own reasoning) is an explicit claim by the Talmud that the Rabbi of the waving baraita and the Rabbi of the frankincense baraita hold one consistent view. That makes the local coreference textual. Identifying this Rabbi as Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi is a separate identification, by convention and by editors. The first reading anchors a mention for רבי only in s1, although its claims c6 and c8-c11 depend on the occurrences in s2 and s3.
findings.graph_effect: Add mentions for רבי in s2 and s3, both linked to the local entity 'rabbi' with basis 'explicit (לטעמיה)'. Keep the historical identification as a separate, provisional step. The consistency claim says nothing about when or where Rabbi taught each view.

findings.claim: Rabbi's 'one does not do so' rejects Hanina ben Hakhinai's method of putting the bread between the thighs. It is a disagreement between views inside a baraita, not a conversation between the two.

evidence.exact_quote: אמר רבי לפני מלך בשר ודם אין עושין כן
evidence.note: Wikisource 62a:11; 'said Rabbi', not 'said to him'

evidence.exact_quote: אין עושין כן - לתת לחם בין ירכים:
evidence.note: Rashi

evidence.exact_quote: אמר ר' לפני מלך ב"ו אין עושין דבר מגונה כזה
evidence.note: Rabbeinu Gershom

evidence.exact_quote: (15) It is most undignified to present the bread in this manner.
evidence.note: Soncino footnote

findings.reasoning: Translation (mine) of Rashi: 'one does not do so: place bread between thighs'. The text uses 'אמר רבי' with no addressee. The target is fixed by context and by the commentaries, which is why this is an interpretation, though a secure one.
findings.graph_effect: Keep c3 as Rabbi objecting to the statement 'between'. Do not add a person-to-person speech edge from Rabbi to Hanina, and do not infer that they met.

findings.claim: Rabbi's side-by-side ruling offers a different arrangement from every earlier view in the same baraita (the anonymous first view, bread on top; Rabbi Yosi ben HaMeshullam, lambs on top; Hanina, between the thighs). The supplied input began at Hanina's view and left out those earlier participants, and Rav Papa's interjection.

evidence.exact_quote: מה מצינו בכל מקום לחם למעלה אף כאן לחם למעלה היכא אמר רב פפא במילואים
evidence.note: Wikisource 62a:9

evidence.exact_quote: רבי יוסי בן המשולם אומר כבשים למעלה
evidence.note: Wikisource 62a:10

evidence.exact_quote: ודעת התנא קמא שנלמד מתנופת המלואים
evidence.note: Malbim

evidence.exact_quote: ודעת ר' שפירש "על" בסמוך
evidence.note: Malbim

evidence.exact_quote: עד כאן לא פליגי רבי ורבנן בסוף כל המנחות [באות מצה] (לעיל מנחות דף סב.) אלא אי בעינן על בסמוך או על ממש
evidence.note: Tosafot Menachot 78b

findings.reasoning: Translations (mine): Malbim, 'the first tanna's view, learned from the waving at the inauguration ... Rabbi's view, who explained al as next to'. Tosafot, 'Rabbi and the Rabbis disagree only on whether we require al as next to or as literally on'. Malbim sets out four views. Tosafot presents the dispute as Rabbi against 'the Rabbis' (unnamed). Neither says which named tanna the Rabbis are. Rav Papa's 'where? at the inauguration' is an amoraic comment inside the cited baraita. The Davidson English says 'The Gemara interrupts its citation'.
findings.graph_effect: The focal unit's needed_context should include 62a:7-10. Rabbi's view can carry 'differs in view from' edges to the anonymous first view, to Yosi ben HaMeshullam and to Hanina. The Hanina edge is explicit (F6). The others rest on interpretation, from juxtaposition and commentary. Tosafot's 'Rabbanan' should stay an unnamed collective and should not be resolved to specific sages.

findings.claim: Hanina's name has three forms in the witnesses checked: 'חנינא בן חכינאי' (Bavli editions), 'חנינא בן עכינאי' (Sifra Venice 1545, also in Malbim) and 'חנניה בן חכינאי' (Yalkut Shimoni, Torat Emet). All three give the same teaching in the same baraita.

evidence.exact_quote: חנינא בן חכינאי אומר מניח שתי הלחם בין ירכותיהן של כבשים ומניף
evidence.note: Wikisource 62a:11

evidence.exact_quote: חנינא בן עכינאי אומר מניח שתי הלחם בן ירכותיהם של כבשים ומניף
evidence.note: Sifra Emor 13:8, Venice 1545

evidence.exact_quote: ודעת חנינא בן עכינאי שיניח הלחם בין ירכות הכבשים
evidence.note: Malbim

evidence.exact_quote: חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן חֲכִינַאי אוֹמֵר
evidence.note: Yalkut Shimoni 644

findings.reasoning: These are source variants of one name in parallel versions of one teaching. They are not separate persons. Each form includes the patronymic 'בן'. So the father relation holds in every witness, though the father's name is spelled חכינאי or עכינאי. Whether 'ben X' is a literal father's name or a family or place name is not decided by this passage. The ordinary reading is a patronymic.
findings.graph_effect: Keep the child_of edge (c1) and the parent placeholder. Record the placeholder's name as a variant set {חכינאי, עכינאי} with witness labels. Record Hanina's own name variants {חנינא, חנניה}. Do not create extra nodes. Do not merge with a same-named sage elsewhere on the strength of the name alone.

findings.claim: Not every witness to this sugya carries the Hisda/Hamnuna attribution. In the Yalkut Shimoni the answer is anonymous (and so is the parallel at 62a:19). The Sifra, a tannaitic work, has the baraita without any later answer. The Yalkut and the Sifra also word Rabbi's rhetorical line differently.

evidence.exact_quote: וְהָא בָּעִינַן "עַל", רַבִּי לְטַעְמֵהּ, דְּאָמַר "עַל" בְּסָמוּךְ
evidence.note: Yalkut: no Hisda/Hamnuna

evidence.exact_quote: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה
evidence.note: Yalkut: 'how much more so', in place of the Bavli's rhetorical 'one does so?'

evidence.exact_quote: אמר רבי, לפני מלך בשר ודם אין עושים כן, לפני מלך מלכי המלכים עושין כן?!
evidence.note: Sifra: no 'the Holy One, blessed be He'

evidence.exact_quote: לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשִׂין כֵּן?!
evidence.note: Davidson vocalized, punctuated as a rhetorical question

findings.reasoning: The Yalkut is an anthology that often shortens what it quotes. Its silence is evidence about the anthology's text, not a Bavli manuscript variant, and it does not show that the attribution is late. No Bavli manuscripts were checked. Every wording supports reading Rabbi's line as a rhetorical argument from the lesser case to the greater (the first reading's note on c3 is right).
findings.graph_effect: Store the Yalkut's anonymous answer as evidence of type 'anthology witness'. Do not treat it as a reading branch that removes Hisda and Hamnuna. Keep the Hisda/Hamnuna attribution as the Bavli editions' reading.

findings.claim: Commentators connect Rabbi's 'al means next to' to other sages. Ra'avad explains the Sifra's Rabbi by the Bavli's reasoning. Tosafot on Sotah links it to Abba Shaul's view on the frankincense and infers that Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda read al literally there. These links belong to the commentaries, not to Menachot 62a.

evidence.exact_quote: מניחן זה בצד זה ומניף פי' קסבר ר' על בסמוך
evidence.note: Ra'avad on Sifra

evidence.exact_quote: אבא שאול אומר שם היו נותנין בזיכי לבונה של לחם הפנים
evidence.note: Tosafot Sotah 37a, quoting the Mishnah

evidence.exact_quote: ונראה אפי' רבי מאיר ור' יהודה דפליגי התם אאבא שאול ואמרי על ממש
evidence.note: Tosafot's own inference ('it appears')

evidence.exact_quote: דס"ל על פירושו בסמוך וכמו ועליו מטה מנשה
evidence.note: Torah Temimah footnote

findings.reasoning: Translation (mine) of Tosafot: 'it appears that even Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda, who disagree there with Abba Shaul, say al means literally'. This is a commentator's inference about another mishnah.
findings.graph_effect: Do not add edges from 62a to Abba Shaul, Rabbi Meir or Rabbi Yehuda. At most, store a commentary-layer 'aligned view' note with Tosafot as its voice.

findings.claim: The 'king of flesh and blood' is a hypothetical comparison figure and the Holy One is the referent of the comparison. Neither is a participant. The 'officiant' is the unnamed subject of 'he places'. The word 'priest' is only in the editor's plain text and the commentaries.

evidence.exact_quote: there is a different answer: The priest places the two loaves between the thighs of
evidence.note: Davidson English: 'The priest' is plain text

evidence.exact_quote: וּמַנִּיחָן בְּצַד שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם
evidence.note: Rambam's ruling follows 'side by side'

findings.reasoning: The first reading types the king as a person and the questioner as a group. For a graph of people and relationships, these are a hypothetical figure, a generic role, and the editorial voice.
findings.graph_effect: Retype 'king' as a hypothetical figure and 'officiant' as a generic role. Keep 'god' as a divine referent (or unknown, if the contract has no such kind). Retype 'questioner' as the editorial voice. None of them should enter the people network.

The addressee of the answer raised it (possible under the 'said to' formula, not stated)

readings: A rejection of Hanina's method only
A fourth view against all earlier views (Malbim), or Rabbi against 'the Rabbis' on al (Tosafot 78b)

Whether the baraita citation (62a:13) is spoken by the amora or added by the anonymous Talmud.

Bavli manuscript readings of 62a:12 (for example, whether any manuscript names only one direction or leaves out the pair) were not checked. The Hachi Garsinan images and Dikdukei Soferim were not consulted.
The father's name form (חכינאי or עכינאי) and the son's (חנינא or חנניה) differ across witnesses. No reading is established as original.
The historical identities of Rabbi, Rav Hisda, Rav Hamnuna (there are several sages with this name) and Hanina ben Hakhinai are not settled by this passage.

The Tosefta was not searched with different wording. The exact-phrase searches found this baraita only in the Bavli, the Sifra and the Yalkut. That is a limit of the search, not proof that no other parallel exists.

lessons: A reversible attribution ('X said to Y, and some say Y said to X') is one reading group with two branches. The pairing of X and Y holds in both branches and can be stored once, undirected. Speaker, addressee and content ownership are branch-scoped.
The same reversal formula, repeated word for word in a parallel passage (62a:12 and 98a:19), is one transmitted unit. Link the parallels and count them once.
Quotation boundaries ('דתניא' after an amoraic answer) need their own reading group. They are neither the narrator's voice by default nor the speaker's.
'לטעמיה' (to his own reasoning) is an explicit textual coreference between two sources for one named figure. It is not evidence of one occasion or of a historical identity.
Name-form variants across witnesses (חכינאי/עכינאי, חנינא/חנניה) attach to one local person as labelled variants. A patronymic keeps its parent placeholder whatever the spelling.
Anthology witnesses (Yalkut) that drop an attribution are a separate evidence type from manuscripts and must not delete a speaker.
Parable figures (king of flesh and blood), generic ritual roles (the one who waves) and the editorial voice are not people-network nodes.

review.scope: I checked every finding and proposed correction in dossier.json and reading.md against the saved files in sources/ (Menachot 62a, 98a, Sotah 37a, Shabbat 97a:17, Sifra, Yalkut, Malbim, Tosafot, Rashi, Rabbeinu Gershom, Steinsaltz, the Soncino text layer and the exact-phrase search); I fetched nothing new and did not check Bavli manuscripts or the Tosefta.

findings.reason: The proof in 62a:13 ('אתה אומר על בסמוך או אינו אלא על ממש כשהוא אומר וסכות על הארון את הפרוכת הוי אומר על בסמוך') comes after 'רבי אומר' and is inside the cited baraita. It is not spoken by the amora or by the anonymous Talmud: the Davidson English says 'The baraita asks' and 'The baraita explains', and Soncino closes Rabbi's words at 'Rabbi says, ‘Al means near to’.' The open citation_boundary group (amora or anonymous Talmud) is right, but it belongs on a separate act, 'cites this baraita in support of רבי לטעמיה', not on c7. c7's voice should be the baraita. A second question stays open: are the 'you say ... when it says' lines Rabbi's own derivation or the baraita's unnamed voice? The earlier review mixed these layers in the same way.

findings.target: F8 (name variants of Hanina ben Hakhinai)
findings.reason: Tosafot on Sotah 37a quotes our baraita with 'וכו' ר' חכינאי אומר מניח הלחם בין שתי יריכותיהם של כבשים ומניף'. That wording names the speaker by the father's name alone, with a title. The dossier quotes this same file (S18) for F10 but leaves this form out of the variant set. Record it as a later-quotation variant, a separate evidence type from the printed Bavli, the Sifra and the Yalkut. It must not make Hakhinai the speaker in the Bavli reading, merge the father into the son, or weaken the child_of claim c1, which is scoped to the readings that have 'בן'.

The dossier widens the context to 62a:7-10 and proposes edges to 'Yosi ben HaMeshullam', but it records no name-internal relation for him. 'רבי יוסי בן המשולם אומר כבשים למעלה' (62a:10) carries a patronymic, so a parent placeholder and a child_of claim are needed, scoped to that reading. Flag it as possibly a fixed name: it has the article ה, and the Sifra reads 'ר' יוסי בן משולם' without it. Rav Papa ('היכא אמר רב פפא במילואים', 62a:9) enters as an amoraic speaker with no addressee, interjected into the baraita. The 'anonymous first view' is the baraita's unattributed voice, not a person node.

findings.target: F6 vs F7 graph_effect and AR4
findings.reason: F6 calls Rabbi's target an interpretation: 'The target is fixed by context and by the commentaries'. F7 and AR4 call the same Hanina target 'explicit'. The text says only 'אמר רבי לפני מלך בשר ודם אין עושין כן', with no name, and 'כן' points back to the view just stated. Use one basis in all three places: close context (the view immediately before), high confidence, backed by Rashi's 'אין עושין כן - לתת לחם בין ירכים'. The 'differs in view' edges to the unnamed first view and to Yosi ben HaMeshullam rest on the content of the arrangements, not on any word aimed at them. Keep them as interpretation, as F7 already says.

findings.target: F5 and reading.md 'One Rabbi' ('the Talmud itself joins them')
findings.reason: Adding רבי mentions in s2 and s3 is right, and I support it. But 'רבי לטעמיה דאמר על בסמוך' comes after 'א"ל רב חסדא לרב המנונא ...'. The link is therefore made by whichever sage answers, not by the anonymous Talmud. The content is the same in both branches, so the link holds whichever way the answer ran. The tie to the particular Rabbi of the frankincense baraita is made by 'דתניא', and who says that word is itself open (AR2). The coreference basis should read 'stated by the answering sage, in both branches; the baraita is joined by a citation whose speaker is open', not 'the Talmud's own voice'.

The conclusion holds: an anthology witness must not delete Rav Hisda and Rav Hamnuna from the Bavli reading. But 'it often shortens what it quotes' undersells what the saved text shows. In this same section the Yalkut keeps 'אָמַר רַב פַּפָּא: בְּמִלּוּאִים', R. Hiyya bar Abba, R. Yohanan, Rava, Rav Papa and Ravina. It lacks the pair at both of its points, 62a:12 ('וְהָא בָּעִינַן "עַל", רַבִּי לְטַעְמֵהּ') and the 62a:19 material ('רַבָּנָן סָבְרִי'). Record it as an anthology reading without the pair at both reversal points. Keep it open whether this is editing or a different source text, and do not use it to date or remove the attribution.

findings.target: F1 (two directions) and reading.md 'Every witness in the Bavli editions checked keeps both'
findings.reason: Wikisource and both Davidson Aramaic forms read 'רב חסדא לרב המנונא ואמרי לה רב המנונא לרב חסדא', and I support the graph effect: one undirected pairing shared by both branches, directed said-to edges kept inside their branch, and no meeting. But these Hebrew/Aramaic 'witnesses' are all the one printed text, just as the two English translations are. Tosafot Sotah 37a gives a separate, later quotation that also keeps both directions ('אמר רב חסדא לרב המנונא ואמרי לה רב המנונא לרב חסדא רבי לטעמיה דתניא וכו''). That quotation skips 'דאמר על בסמוך'. Label it a later quotation, not a vote.

The search hits check out: four Bavli segments (62a:12, 62a:19, 98a:19, Shabbat 97a:17), each in three versions. The answer line at 98a:19 is word for word the same. The baraita is not: the order of its words differs ('דתניא רבי אומר ונתת על המערכת לבונה זכה על בסמוך' against 62a's 'דתניא ונתת על המערכת לבונה זכה רבי אומר על בסמוך'). Counting 62a:12 and 98a:19 once is sound, and the dossier rightly calls the 'one transmitted answer' an inference. The occurrences at 62a:19 and Shabbat 97a:17 belong to other passages. They should not be added to this passage's graph, and any counting of how often the pair appears together belongs to a separate cross-passage step.

'והא בעינן על' stands before 'א"ל' with no speaker. Steinsaltz's impersonal 'ומקשים על שיטת רבי' and the same pattern at 98a:18 ('והא בעינן ... ונתת על') agree. Adding no 'asks' edge from either sage is correct. The same text sets the addressee only through 'לרב המנונא' / 'לרב חסדא', and only inside each branch.

Retyping is right: the 'מלך בשר ודם' is a figure in a comparison, the unnamed subject of 'מניח' is a generic ritual role, and 'והא בעינן על' is the editorial voice. The Mishneh Torah quote ('וּמַנִּיחָן בְּצַד שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם') shows only that Rambam rules like Rabbi. It says nothing about who these figures are, so it should not serve as evidence for this retyping.

cases.question: In Menachot 73b:16 the Talmud offers two ways to name the tanna of an anonymous baraita (Rabbi Yosei HaGelili with 'wine' deleted, or Rabbi Akiva with 'a burnt offering and all its accompaniments'). Which person, view and attribution claims are explicit, which depend on interpretation, and what did the first reading and its review miss?

findings.claim: The 'wine' that 73b:16 proposes to delete is the word in the earlier baraita at 73b:8, whose inclusive list 73b:9 closes as 'the statement of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili'. Rashi and Rabbeinu Gershom both say the corrected baraita should read 'birds and frankincense' without wine.

evidence.translation_mine: My translation: From where [do we learn] to include birds, and wine, and frankincense, and wood?

evidence.exact_quote: פְּרָט לִנְזִירוּת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: excluding naziriteship; [these are] the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

evidence.exact_quote: איבעית אימא ר' יוסי הגלילי סמי מההיא יין
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: If you like, say [it is] Rabbi Yosei HaGelili: delete 'wine' from that one.

evidence.exact_quote: סמי מכאן נסכי יין - ואמר מנין לרבות העופות והלבונה ולא תיתני היין
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: Delete from here the wine libations, and say 'from where to include birds and frankincense', and do not teach 'wine'.

evidence.exact_quote: סמי מההיא יין. אלא מנין לרבות העופות והלבונה
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: Delete wine from that one: rather, 'from where to include birds and frankincense'.

findings.reasoning: מההיא ('from that one') needs an antecedent. The only earlier text with wine in a Yosei HaGelili teaching is the list at 73b:8, and 73b:15 cites exactly that ('he says even wine'). Two commentaries name the corrected wording. The pilot window (73b:12-16) did not include 73b:8-9, so the first reading anchored Yosei's wine view only to the Gemara's paraphrase at 73b:15.
findings.graph_effect: Anchor Yosei's inclusive view (entity 'wine', claim c3) to the baraita at 73b:8-9 as the primary evidence; keep 73b:15 as the Gemara's paraphrase. The target of 'delete' is a clause in a baraita attributed to Yosei, not a statement by Yosei.

findings.claim: 'Delete wine' is an emendation proposed by the anonymous Talmud voice, offered as only one of two answers. It is a later proposed correction of a tannaitic text, not a reported manuscript reading and not a report that Yosei changed his mind.

evidence.exact_quote: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי – סְמִי מֵהַהִיא ״יַיִן״
evidence.translation_mine: My translation: If you like, say Rabbi Yosei HaGelili: delete 'wine' from that one.

evidence.translation_mine: My translation: from the words of R. Yosei, the word [wine]

findings.reasoning: סמי is an imperative addressed to whoever recites the baraita. It is framed by איבעית אימא, a formula for alternative answers. Nothing in the segment says any witness lacked the word. Steinsaltz reads the result as a statement about Yosei's opinion ('even in his view'), which is commentary, not the Talmud's words.
findings.graph_effect: Save the deletion as evidence_type 'proposed_emendation' on the transmission of the 73b:8 baraita, inside branch yosi_solution. Claim c8 (Yosei holds_view wine, negative) should become a dependent inference from that emendation, not a free-standing view claim.

findings.claim: The Yosei view that includes wine (c3) is shared by the objection and the Akiva answer, but the Yosei answer withdraws it. The first reading saved c3 with an empty branch list, which by the pilot's rules means 'true in every reading'.

All the commentaries checked explain it as the libations that come with the burnt offering.

findings.reasoning: The saved vocalized text marks one word as replaced, but the saved API response does not name who made the replacement. The meaning agreed by these commentaries is the same for both words. No person is affected.
findings.graph_effect: Label entity 'associated' as 'libations that accompany a burnt offering (commentary reading); libations by themselves excluded'. Save the wording difference as a source variant, not as a separate claim.

findings.claim: Tosafot considers and rejects a third way out: reading Yosei's 'wine' as wine that comes with an offering, which would make the baraita fit Yosei without deleting anything. Tosafot also reports a reading difference in the parallel at Temurah 3a.

evidence.translation_mine: My translation: And one cannot say that the wine Rabbi Yosei HaGelili also mentioned is [wine] that comes with the offering.

evidence.translation_mine: My translation: and further, since he counts it together with birds and meal offerings, which come by themselves.

findings.reasoning: This is a commentator's argument, not the Talmud's. It supports keeping only two branches for 73b:16 and records a considered and rejected alternative. Tosafot's 'birds and meal offerings' does not match the Bavli list at 73b:8, which has no meal offerings; the Sifra list does (F07). That suggests Tosafot is not quoting the Bavli list exactly, but this was not checked further.
findings.graph_effect: Record 'Yosei's wine = wine with an offering' as an alternative rejected by Tosafot. Do not add it as a third branch of the Talmud's answer.

findings.claim: Other witnesses to the tannaitic dispute swap the two names. In the saved Sifra (Venice 1545) the inclusive list is Rabbi Akiva's and Rabbi Yosei HaGelili answers 'only a burnt offering'. Lieberman reports the same swap in the Erfurt and London manuscripts of the Tosefta. The Bavli's order matches the Tosefta's Vienna manuscript and first printing. Ra'avad's own Sifra text follows the Menachot order, and he notes that other Sifra versions have the swap.

findings.claim: The parallels also differ in content. The Tosefta (Vienna) list of offerings accepted from gentiles has no wine; it has meal offerings and salt, and its Akiva allows 'a burnt offering and peace offerings only'. The Sifra list includes meal offerings and wine. The Bavli list at 73b:8 has wine but no meal offerings, and its Akiva allows 'a burnt offering only'.

lessons: A proposed deletion ('סמי') changes the transmitted text of a teaching. Model it as a transmission event on the source, not as a change in the sage's view.
A claim whose premise is withdrawn in one branch cannot keep an empty branch list. Premises of an objection need their own branch scope.

'Whose view does this follow?' (כמאן, לימא) is agreement between a teaching and a sage. 'Who is the tanna?' (מאן תנא) is closer to attribution. Neither is authorship when the teaching already has a named speaker.
Put parallel-work variants (Sifra, Tosefta manuscripts), a Talmud-internal proposed emendation, and a commentator's rejected reading into three separate evidence types.
An addressed-speech frame ('said to him') can exist in one witness and not another. Its direction can flip too. It is literary evidence of a debate, not of a meeting.
A translation made from the same text (Silverstein on the Venice Sifra) is not independent support for that text's reading.

review.scope: I checked every dossier quote against its saved file in sources/ (all 57 occur verbatim), reread Menachot 73a:13-73b:20, Mishnah Shekalim 7:4-7, Temurah 2b:6-11 and 3a:7-12, the Menachot commentaries, the Sifra and Tosefta witnesses and the pilot input and output; I fetched nothing new and did not check Bavli manuscripts, Dikdukei Soferim or any page image.

Otherwise the emendation erases the printed reading.

findings.target: pilot entity 'gentile'; claims c2, c11, c12 (not covered by the dossier's proposed_corrections)
findings.reason: The dossier fixes 'citizen' (אזרח) but leaves the pilot's 'gentile' entity as kind 'person'. The 'עובד כוכבים ששלח עולתו ממדינת הים' in 73b:12 is a legal case inside an ordinance, so it is a legal role, not a historical person or event. F13 says 'רבנן' in 'דתנו רבנן' is a citation formula, but no proposed correction changes c2 ('teachers holds_view baraita'). The first reading also keeps c11 and c12 ('מני? לא ר' יוסי הגלילי ולא רבי עקיבא') as negative attributions with no branch, although 73b:16 answers 'איבעית אימא ר' יוסי הגלילי ואיבעית אימא רבי עקיבא'. They need to be marked as the question's premise, overturned in both branches, so they never become 'not Yosei' or 'not Akiva' edges.

Temurah 2b:9 prints 'וְאֵין מְבִיאִין עֲלֵיהֶם נְסָכִים' with 'on them', and 3a:10 prints it in parentheses as '(עֲלֵיהֶן)'. Tosafot says that with 'עליהם' Temurah 'משמע ... מיירי בבאין עם הזבח' (seems to speak of libations that come with the offering) and that 'ברוב ספרים לא גרסי' עליהם'. So calling it 'the same rule' depends on the reading. The dossier also omits that the Temurah baraita has a named dissent right after 'דברי רבי שמעון': 'אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: בְּכוּלָּן אֲנִי רוֹאֶה לְהַחְמִיר' (2b:10; 3a:11). A5 should therefore say 'attributed to R. Shimon in a disputed baraita, reading-dependent'. This Rabbi Yosei is a separate local person and must not be merged with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

I support saving the swap as a textual alternative. The Sifra reads 'דברי ר' עקיבא ... אמר לו ר' יוסי הגלילי ... אין כאן אלא עולה בלבד', and Kifshutah reports 'בכי"ע ובכי"ל: דברי ר' עקיבא'. But the witnesses for the Bavli order are not independent of the Bavli. Ra'avad justifies his text by it ('מיהו האי נסחא דכתיבנא איתא במנחות'). The Sifra's bracketed '[גירס' הגמרא ...]' notes are cross-references to the Bavli, and Chafetz Chaim only reports the Bavli ('ובמנחות הגירסא להיפך'). Only Tosefta Vienna and the printed edition count as separate witnesses for the Bavli order. The rest must not be counted as votes.

findings.target: F07 / proposed correction 'new (reading_groups)' (Tosefta list without wine)
findings.reason: The Vienna list 'עולות, ושלמים, עופות, ומנחות, עצים, ולבונה, ומלח' has no wine, and no entry in the saved apparatus adds it. But it is a different list ('מקבלין מהן', things accepted from gentiles). It adds salt, meal offerings and peace offerings, and there the restrictive sage allows 'עולה ושלמים בלבד'. It does not witness the Bavli baraita that 'סמי מההיא' corrects. Save it as a parallel-text difference attached to the Yosei-Akiva dispute, with low confidence as support for the deletion. Do not attach it to yosi_solution as supporting evidence for the emendation.

'עוֹלָה וְכׇל (חַבְירָתַהּ) [אַבְזָרַהָא]' occurs twice, at 73b:13 (about the Shekalim mishnah) and at 73b:16 (about the anonymous baraita). Rashi 73b:13:3, Ktav Yad Rashi 73b:13:2 and Rabbeinu Gershom [8] (which comes before his [9] 'אזרח') all comment on the 73b:13 occurrence. Only Steinsaltz on 73b:16, which glosses 'כל חבירתה' as '(הנלוה לה), כנסכים', comments on the focal occurrence. Keep the gloss, but anchor the commentary evidence to 73b:13 and note that it carries over to 73b:16 because the Talmud reuses the phrase.

findings.target: F01 / reading.md 'What wider context changes' item 1
findings.reason: The antecedent at 73b:8-9 is right, and Rashi 73b:15:1 ('כדקתני מנין לרבות העופות והיין') supports it more directly than the 73b:16 comment. Two narrowings apply. First, Rashi's lemma reads 'סמי מכאן נסכי יין', not the printed 'סמי מההיא יין', and that lemma difference should be recorded. Second, Rashi ('מנין לרבות העופות והלבונה ולא תיתני היין') and Gershom ('אלא מנין לרבות העופות והלבונה') quote only the opening of the corrected list; wood is not mentioned. reading.md's 'give the corrected wording: "birds and frankincense"' should say they show the list's opening without wine, not the full corrected wording.

The apparatus has London lacking both words: 'אמ' | ד אמר א א'. ל ח'.' and 'לו | ל ח'.', with 'עקיבא | ... ל יוסי הגלילי [או']'. But Lieberman's own summary in Kifshutah gives both Erfurt and London as 'א' לו ר' יוסי הגלילי'. His two statements disagree for London, so London's framing should stay open ('said to him' versus 'says'), and both entries should be cited. The dossier's main point stands: the Bavli 73b:9 has 'רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר', with no addressee, and no addressed speech or meeting belongs in 73b:16.

The names and the local father placeholder 'Gurya' from 'רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא' are supported, flagged as possibly a fixed name. If the window is widened, the text marks no addressees. 'מֵתִיב רַב שֵׁיזְבִי ... אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָא קַשְׁיָא' and 'מֵתִיב רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא ... אָמַר רָבָא' place an answer after an objection. They do not say the answerer spoke to the objector, so no addressee and no meeting should be recorded. The target, Rav Huna's statement at 73a:16, is given by the sugya's structure and the English gloss ('To answer the challenge to Rav Huna's statement'), not by the Aramaic of 73b:3-5.

findings.target: F09, F10, F02 (referent of 'this', agreement versus authorship, deletion as emendation)
findings.reason: Mishnah Shekalim 7:5 ends 'הִתְקִינוּ בֵּית דִּין שֶׁיְּהוּ נְסָכֶיהָ בָּאִין מִשֶּׁל צִבּוּר', and Ktav Yad Rashi ('לעיל מיניה קא מיירי') and Tosafot Yom Tov ('והדר מפרש לאינך שש נכרי') confirm that 'this' is the found animal's libations. The gentile rule is another of the seven, so the court still instituted it. 'כמאן אזלא' and 'לימא' ask which sage's view a mishnah already said in Rabbi Shimon's name agrees with, so the accords_with_view_of change for c5, c6 and c10 is right. The 'סמי' deletion is framed by 'איבעית אימא' as one of two answers. Treating it as a proposed emendation, and not as Yosei changing his mind, is right. The mishnah's own before-and-after sequence ('בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה ... חָזְרוּ ... הִתְקִינוּ') is relative order only and gives no date.

quote_checks.exact_quote: מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת הָעוֹפוֹת, וְהַיַּיִן, וְהַלְּבוֹנָה, וְהָעֵצִים?
quote_checks.note: Occurs once, at 73b:8, inside the baraita that 73b:9 closes with 'דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי'. This is the right occurrence for the 'wine' that 73b:16 proposes to delete.

quote_checks.exact_quote: פְּרָט לִנְזִירוּת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
quote_checks.note: 73b:9. It is followed at once by 'רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר', a listed view with no 'said to him'.

quote_checks.exact_quote: סמי מכאן נסכי יין - ואמר מנין לרבות העופות והלבונה ולא תיתני היין
quote_checks.note: Rashi 73b:16:1. It supports the antecedent. The lemma wording ('מכאן', 'נסכי') differs from the printed 'מההיא', and the comment quotes only the opening of the corrected list.

quote_checks.exact_quote: סמי מההיא יין. אלא מנין לרבות העופות והלבונה
quote_checks.note: Rabbeinu Gershom [12]. The lemma matches the printed wording. The corrected list is quoted only in part.

quote_checks.exact_quote: עוֹלָה וְכׇל (חַבְירָתַהּ) [אַבְזָרַהָא]
quote_checks.note: The phrase occurs twice, at 73b:13 and 73b:16. F04's location, 73b:16, is one real occurrence. The commentary glosses in F04 belong to the 73b:13 occurrence.

quote_checks.exact_quote: עולה וכל חבירתה דהיינו נסכים אבל נסכים לחודייהו לא
quote_checks.note: Rashi 73b:13:3, on the mishnah occurrence, not the focal 73b:16.

quote_checks.exact_quote: פרט לנזירות, דברי ר' עקיבא [גירס' הגמרא ריה"ג]. אמר לו ר' יוסי הגלילי [גירס' הגמרא ר"ע] אפילו אתה מרבה כל היום אין כאן אלא עולה בלבד.
quote_checks.note: It confirms the swap and the direction Yosei to Akiva. The bracketed notes are Bavli cross-references of unknown date and are not an independent witness.

quote_checks.exact_quote: ואיכא נסחי דכתיב בהו דברי ר' עקיבא אמר לו ר' יוסי הגלילי מיהו האי נסחא דכתיבנא איתא במנחות
quote_checks.note: Ra'avad's own text follows Menachot, and he justifies it by Menachot. It is dependent on the Bavli and not a separate vote for the Bavli order.

quote_checks.exact_quote: לו | ל ח'.
quote_checks.note: The preceding entry, 'אמ' | ד אמר א א'. ל ח'.', shows London also lacks 'אמ''. That conflicts with Kifshutah's 'בכי"ע ובכי"ל: ... א' לו'.

quote_checks.exact_quote: עצים, ולבונה, ומלח, דברי
quote_checks.note: The Vienna list has no wine. It is a different list, of things accepted from gentiles, and it also differs by salt, meal offerings and peace offerings.

quote_checks.exact_quote: הִתְקִינוּ בֵּית דִּין שֶׁיְּהוּ נְסָכֶיהָ בָּאִין מִשֶּׁל צִבּוּר
quote_checks.note: End of Mishnah Shekalim 7:5, directly before 'אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן ... וְזֶה אֶחָד מֵהֶן' in 7:6. It supports F09.

quote_checks.exact_quote: וְאֵין מְבִיאִין עֲלֵיהֶם נְסָכִים, אֲבָל קׇרְבָּנוֹ טָעוּן נְסָכִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
quote_checks.note: The quote is exact, but it does not fully carry F11's 'same rule' claim. 'עליהם' is printed here, it is parenthesised at 3a:10, and Tosafot reports it as a variant that changes the scope. Temurah 2b:10 goes on 'אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: בְּכוּלָּן אֲנִי רוֹאֶה לְהַחְמִיר', a named dissent the dossier omits.

quote_checks.exact_quote: מיהו ברוב ספרים לא גרסי' עליהם אבל בספר רבינו גרשם כתוב עליהם
quote_checks.note: Tosafot 73b:15:1. It follows 'ובריש תמורה (דף ג.) משמע [דהא] דאין עובד כוכבים מביא נסכים מיירי בבאין עם הזבח', which is why F11 needs the reading-dependence qualifier.

quote_checks.exact_quote: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, הָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
quote_checks.note: 73b:5. It follows 'מֵתִיב רַב שֵׁיזְבִי' with no addressee marker, so this is an answer to an objection, not a conversation.

cases.question: In Sanhedrin 36a:6, who gives the explanation that Rabbi's court voted from the side, what kinship do the names carry, and what do the wider sugya, the Gittin 58b-59a parallel and the commentaries add or dispute about Rav's vote, the practice's reason and the follow-on praise of Rabbi?

findings.claim: The focal line gives one explanation under two alternative speaker names: Rabba son of Rava, 'and some say' Rabbi Hillel son of Rabbi Volas. The explanation is that the vote in Rabbi's house was different, because all their votes began from the side. The same wording, with the same pair of names, appears in the William Davidson Aramaic and in the Gittin 59a parallel (which spells the name הילל).

evidence.exact_quote: אמר רבה בריה דרבא ואיתימא רבי הלל בריה דרבי וולס שאני מניינא דבי רבי דכולהו מנינייהו מן הצד הוו מתחלי
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Rabba son of Rava said, and some say Rabbi Hillel son of Rabbi Volas: the vote of Rabbi's house is different, for all their votes would begin from the side.

evidence.exact_quote: אמר רבה בריה דרבא ואיתימא רבי הלל בריה דרבי וולס שאני מניינא דבי רבי דכולהו מנינייהו מן הצד הוו מתחלי
אמר רבה בריה דרבא ואיתימא ר' הילל בריה דר' וולס שאני מנינא דבי רבי דכולהו מנינייהו מן הצד הוו מתחילין
Rabba, son of Rava, says, and some say that it was Rabbi Hillel, son of Rabbi Valles, who says:

findings.reasoning: ואיתימא introduces a second attribution of the same words. The text reports two candidate speakers; it does not say both spoke, nor which is right. The Gittin 59a sugya is a parallel copy of the same unit, so its agreement is not an independent witness to who spoke.
findings.graph_effect: Keep c3/c4 as two branches of one attribution group. The speaker in each branch is the son, not the father. Do not treat the Gittin parallel as a second observation of the attribution.

findings.claim: Both speaker names carry a patronymic, so the passage supports two parent placeholders: Rava (father of Rabba) and Rabbi Volas (father of Rabbi Hillel). Neither father speaks or acts here. Steinsaltz glosses בריה as 'his son' in both names; Jastrow calls Volas 'an Amora, father of R. Hillel'.

evidence.exact_quote: רבה בריה דרבא
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Rabba son of Rava

evidence.exact_quote: רבי הלל בריה דרבי וולס
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Rabbi Hillel son of Rabbi Volas

evidence.exact_quote: אמר רבה בריה [בנו] של רבא:
an Amora, father of R. Hillel

findings.reasoning: A patronymic is explicit kinship evidence under the project rule. Whether the Rava named here is the well-known Amora Rava is a separate identity question. Seder HaDorot treats him that way when it discusses Rabba son of Rava (S24), but that is a later biographer's identification. Nothing in this passage checks it.
findings.graph_effect: Keep c7 (rabba child_of rava) and c8 (hillel child_of voles), each tied to its own name branch. Keep the parent placeholders local. Do not merge 'rava' with a global Rava entity on name alone.

findings.claim: The father's name is spelled in several ways. Wikisource and the William Davidson Aramaic read וולס. Jastrow reports ולס in the Munich manuscript for Sanhedrin 36a and וילס in the Kohut edition of the Arukh, and gives Yerushalmi forms אלס and חליס. Rashi on Sanhedrin 36a:7 has a bare heading 'בריה דרבי וולס' with no comment. Seder HaDorot and the Chatam Sofer read this as a spelling note: the name is וולס, not the gentile name ולוס/לוס of Gittin 11b.

evidence.exact_quote: (Ms. M. ולס, Ar. ed. Koh. וילס)
בריה דרבי וולס:
כוונת רש"י דהגירסא וולס ולא ולוס שהוא שם נכרי
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Rashi's intent: the reading is Volas and not Valos, which is a gentile name.

evidence.exact_quote: ציין רש"י וולס ולא פי' כלום ובסנהדרין כתב כך שמו
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Rashi marked 'Volas' and explained nothing; and in Sanhedrin he wrote 'so is his name'.

findings.reasoning: The manuscript readings are known here only through Jastrow's report; no manuscript image was checked. The Chatam Sofer reports a Rashi on Sanhedrin that says 'כך שמו'. The Vilna Rashi saved here has only the heading, so the wording in his copy may differ from this edition. These are spelling forms of one name in this passage, not evidence of different people.
findings.graph_effect: Record name-form variants (וולס / ולס / וילס) as attributes of the local 'voles' mention, typed as a reported manuscript reading, not a variant this dossier checked. Do not create extra persons. Yerushalmi forms (אלס, חליס) belong to identity research, not to this passage.

findings.claim: In Sanhedrin the text does not say which vote Rav means. The Gittin 58b-59a parallel puts the same report of Rav directly after 'Rabbi convened a court and they voted' on the sicarii land rule. Rashi on Sanhedrin 36a:5 and on Gittin 59a names that vote as the one Rav meant.

evidence.exact_quote: אמר רב אנא הואי במניינא דבי רבי ומינאי דידי הוו מתחלי ברישא
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Rav said: I was in the vote of Rabbi's house, and they would begin with me first.

evidence.exact_quote: רבי הושיב ב"ד ונמנו שאם שהתה בפני סיקריקון שנים עשר חודש כל הקודם ליקח זכה
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Rabbi convened a court and they voted: if [the field] remained before the sicarius twelve months, whoever buys first acquires.

evidence.exact_quote: אנא הואי במניינא דבי רבי ומינאי דידי מנו ברישא
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: I was in the vote of Rabbi's house, and they counted me first.

evidence.exact_quote: במניינא דסיקריקון אמרה רב בפ' הניזקין (גיטין דף נח:)
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Rav said it about the sicarius vote, in chapter HaNizakin (Gittin 58b).

evidence.exact_quote: באותו מנין שתקנו שכל הקודם ליקח זכה
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: In that vote where they enacted that whoever buys first acquires.

findings.reasoning: The Sanhedrin wording alone reports one vote or a habit ('הוו מתחלי', they would begin). The link to the sicarii ordinance rests on the Gittin placement and on Rashi. The two wordings also differ slightly: 'הוו מתחלי ברישא' in Sanhedrin, 'מנו ברישא' in Gittin.
findings.graph_effect: The 'voting' event (c1) may carry a candidate link to the Gittin 58b:15 court vote. Its basis is 'parallel sugya plus commentary', not 'explicit in Sanhedrin'. Rav's first-person participation stays explicit.

findings.claim: The Aramaic says only that they began with Rav, and the objection assumes he was not 'the greatest'. Saying that Rav was the youngest or most junior comes from commentary and editors, and they disagree. Rashi on Gittin gives two views: that Rav was middling, and 'I heard' that he was the smallest. Steinsaltz and the William Davidson English (in plain, editorial words) call him the youngest or junior. Yad Ramah says only that greater men than Rav were present.

evidence.exact_quote: והא אנן מתחילין מן הגדול תנן
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: But we learned: they begin from the greatest!

evidence.exact_quote: והוא היה בינוני לא מן הגדולים ולא מן הקטנים ואני שמעתי שקטן שבהם היה
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: and he was middling, neither of the greatest nor of the smallest; and I have heard that he was the smallest of them.

evidence.exact_quote: ורב הצעיר שבהם היה
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: and Rav was the youngest of them.

evidence.exact_quote: and Rav was one of the junior judges of that court
although I was the youngest member of the court
כלומר אעפ"י שהיו שם גדולים ממני
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: that is, although there were greater ones than me there.

findings.reasoning: In the William Davidson English these phrases are plain text, so they are the editors' explanation, not the Talmud's words. The Gittin phrase 'although I was the youngest' puts the claim in Rav's mouth, but it too is plain text. Rashi keeps both possibilities open.
findings.graph_effect: Do not add a text-basis claim that Rav was the youngest or most junior judge. At most, add 'Rav was not the greatest in the court' as an implication of the objection. Store the rank views as commentary, credited to Rashi (two views), Steinsaltz, the William Davidson editors and Yad Ramah.

findings.claim: The text gives no reason why Rabbi's court began from the side, and the commentaries disagree about it. Rashi on Sanhedrin and Yad Ramah say it was Rabbi's great humility. Rashi on Gittin says it was because 'do not answer against the great one' applies to all cases. Tosafot on Gittin reject that reading and say humility. Steinsaltz and the William Davidson English say Rabbi was so esteemed that no one would dare contradict him. Petach Einayim notes that Rashi's two places contradict each other. Arukh LaNer ties Rashi's two reasons to the two views of Rav's rank.

evidence.exact_quote: מן הצד הוו מתחלי - מפני ענוה יתירה שהיתה בו:
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: 'They would begin from the side': because of the extra humility that was in him.

evidence.exact_quote: מתוך ענותנותו לא היה רוצה להתחיל הימנו אלא מן הקטן שבהן
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: out of his humility he did not want [them] to begin with him, but with the smallest of them.

evidence.exact_quote: משום לא תענה על ריב וכתיב חסר בלא יו"ד ודרשינן לא תענה על רב לא תחלוק על מופלא שבבית דין
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: because of 'do not answer in a dispute (riv)', written defectively without yod, and we expound: do not answer against the great one (rav), do not disagree with the most distinguished of the court.

evidence.exact_quote: פי' בקונט' דמוקי לה לא תענה על ריב בכל דבר ואין נראה
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Rashi explained that he applies 'do not answer in a dispute' to every matter; this does not seem right.

evidence.exact_quote: אלא משום ענוה שלא להראות עצמו גדול היה עושה
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: rather, he did so out of humility, so as not to show himself great.

evidence.exact_quote: This was because Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi was held in such high esteem that once he expressed his opinion, no one would be so brazen as to contradict him.
משום שהיה רבי גדול מאוד בחכמה ובגדולה ולא היו מעיזים להמרות את פיו
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: because Rabbi was very great in wisdom and greatness, and they would not dare to defy his word.

evidence.exact_quote: ק"ק דהו"ל להקשות על רש"י דידיה אדידיה דרש"י עצמו פירש בסנהדרין דף ל"ו משום ענוה
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: It is a little difficult: they should have challenged Rashi from his own words, since Rashi himself explained in Sanhedrin 36 [that it was] because of humility.

evidence.exact_quote: ולענ"ד י"ל הא דרש"י פי' ב' פירושים דזה תליא בהשני פירושים שהביא רש"י שם בגיטין אי רב מן הבינונים היה או הקטן שבכולם
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: In my humble opinion, Rashi gave two explanations because it depends on the two views Rashi brought in Gittin: whether Rav was among the middling ones or the smallest of all.

findings.reasoning: The Talmud states the practice ('all their votes began from the side') but not its motive. Humility is a trait of Rabbi; esteem is about how others reacted to him; the verse reading is a legal rule. These are three different graph claims, each from a named commentator.
findings.graph_effect: c3/c4 should carry the practice only. Any motive (Rabbi's humility; others' deference; the verse) goes in as a commentary claim with its author, kept as disagreeing alternatives. None is a text-basis trait of Rabbi.

findings.claim: The statement in 36a:7 praises Rabbi (and Moses): from Moses until Rabbi, no one else combined Torah and greatness. It does not say that Moses and Rabbi lacked the combination. The Gemara's objections list figures who might have combined both, and Rashi and Yad Ramah say that Moses and Rabbi each did.

evidence.exact_quote: ואמר רבה בריה דרבא ואיתימא רבי הלל בריה דר' וולס מימות משה ועד רבי לא מצינו תורה וגדולה במקום אחד
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: And Rabba son of Rava said, and some say Rabbi Hillel son of Rabbi Volas: from the days of Moses until Rabbi we did not find Torah and greatness in one place.

evidence.exact_quote: ולא הא הוה יהושע הוה אלעזר
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Is that so? There was Joshua! — There was Elazar.

evidence.exact_quote: כגון משה שהיה גדול על כל ישראל במלכות ובתורה וכן רבי בנשיאות ובתורה
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: such as Moses, who was great over all Israel in rule and in Torah, and likewise Rabbi in the patriarchate and in Torah.

evidence.exact_quote: וכן רבינו הקדוש היה גדול ולא היה בדורו כמוהו לא בחכמה ולא בנשיאות
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: and likewise our holy Rabbi was great, and there was none like him in his generation, neither in wisdom nor in the patriarchate.

findings.reasoning: The first reading's label 'From Moses to Rabbi, learning and greatness were not found together' could be read as denying the combination to Moses and Rabbi. The objections only make sense if the claim is about the period between them. It is a comparison that makes Moses and Rabbi the end points. It is not an interaction.
findings.graph_effect: Relabel the 'combined' statement: 'Between Moses and Rabbi no one combined Torah and greatness (praise of Rabbi)'. Add 'about' roles for Moses and Rabbi. No meeting, no teaching, and no time overlap between them.

findings.claim: The first reading anchored Rabbi only in 36a:5. Rabbi is named again in 36a:6 ('דבי רבי') and 36a:7 ('ועד רבי'). Both refer to the same Rabbi whose court Rav describes. The identification with Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi appears only in the William Davidson English's plain (editorial) words and in Steinsaltz.

evidence.exact_quote: שאני מניינא דבי רבי
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: the vote of Rabbi's house is different

evidence.exact_quote: מימות משה ועד רבי
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: from the days of Moses until Rabbi

evidence.exact_quote: in the school of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi is different,
רבי יהודה הנשיא

findings.reasoning: Taken with 'Rabbi convened a court' in the Gittin parallel, these mentions support Rabbi as head of the court (בי רבי). 'Yehuda HaNasi' is not in the Aramaic. The same editorial work supplies both the English and the Steinsaltz Hebrew, so they do not count as two independent witnesses.
findings.graph_effect: Add mentions of רבי in s2 and s3 linked to local entity 'rabbi'. Keep 'Rabbi = Yehuda HaNasi' as an identity proposal with an editorial basis. It is conventional and probable, but historical identity is decided separately.

findings.claim: The objection is the anonymous Gemara voice ('והא אנן ... תנן', but we learned). It quotes the Mishnah rule that monetary and purity cases begin from the greatest. The Gittin parallel quotes the rule in full, including that capital cases begin from the side.

evidence.exact_quote: והא אנן מתחילין מן הגדול תנן
והאנן תנן דיני ממונות והטהרות והטומאות מתחילין מן הגדול ודיני נפשות מתחילין מן הצד
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: But we learned: monetary cases, and purities and impurities, begin from the greatest; and capital cases begin from the side.

evidence.exact_quote: דִּינֵי הַטֻּמְאוֹת וְהַטָּהֳרוֹת מַתְחִילִין מִן הַגָּדוֹל, דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת מַתְחִילִין מִן הַצָּד

findings.reasoning: 'תנן' marks a quotation of Mishnah. That is a source-citation claim. The first reading recorded the objection but not which source it cites.
findings.graph_effect: Add a source-attribution claim: the anonymous objection cites Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:1-2 (Bavli 32a). No named Tanna is involved.

findings.claim: In both 36a:6-7 and the Gittin parallel, the second teaching repeats the same pair of alternative names, joined by 'ואמר' (and said). The texts never say whether choosing Rabba for one teaching means choosing Rabba for the other. Rabbeinu Chananel and Yad Ramah paraphrase the sugya without naming the speaker; Rabbeinu Chananel writes 'והן אמרו' (and they said).

evidence.exact_quote: ואמר רבה בריה דרבא ואיתימא רבי הלל בריה דר' וולס
ואמר רבה בריה דרבא ואיתימא רבי הילל בריה דרבי וולס
ואסיקנא כל מנייניה דבי רבי מן הצד הוו מתחלי והן אמרו מימות משה ועד רבי לא מצינו תורה וגדולה במקום אחד
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: and we concluded: all the votes of Rabbi's house began from the side; and they said: from the days of Moses until Rabbi we did not find Torah and greatness in one place.

findings.reasoning: 'ואמר' with the identical pair suggests one transmitted unit carried with one attribution doubt. That is a reasonable reading, not a textual statement. A commentator's paraphrase that leaves out the names is not a textual variant against them.
findings.graph_effect: Link groups legal_speaker and praise_speaker as a repeated, probably correlated alternation, as the earlier review warned. Count them as one attribution doubt, not four independent speaker-teaching combinations. Do not use the commentators' omission of names as evidence.

findings.claim: The wider sugya, just after the focal lines, names many more people. In Sanhedrin 36a:8-13: Joshua, Elazar, Pinchas, the Elders, Saul, Samuel, David, Ira the Yairite, Solomon, Shimi ben Gera, Hezekiah, Shebna, Ezra, and Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. Then a named amora says 'I too say: from Rabbi until Rav Ashi…' and mentions Huna bar Natan. Sanhedrin names that amora as Rav Adda bar Ahava; the Gittin parallel names him as Rav Acha son of Rava.

evidence.exact_quote: אמר רב אדא בר אהבה אף אני אומר מימות רבי עד רב אשי לא מצינו תורה וגדולה במקום אחד
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Rav Adda bar Ahava said: I too say, from the days of Rabbi until Rav Ashi we did not find Torah and greatness in one place.

evidence.exact_quote: אמר רב אחא בריה דרבא אף אני אומר מימות רבי ועד רב אשי לא מצינו תורה וגדולה במקום אחד
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Rav Acha son of Rava said: I too say, from the days of Rabbi until Rav Ashi...

evidence.exact_quote: הונא בר נתן מיכף הוה כייף ליה לרב אשי
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Huna bar Natan was subordinate to Rav Ashi.

evidence.exact_quote: הא הוה אלעזר הוה פנחס והא הוה פנחס הוו זקנים
הוה אלעזר והא הוה פנחס הוו זקנים
ואסיק' אף אני אומר מימות רבי ועד רב אשי
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: and it concluded: I too say, from Rabbi until Rav Ashi

findings.reasoning: These are outside the supplied excerpt (36a:5-7), but they belong to the same unit that the focal speaker's statement opens. The two parallels name different speakers for 'אף אני אומר'. That is a cross-parallel attribution difference to keep open, not a merge of Rav Adda bar Ahava and Rav Acha son of Rava. The Gittin text also has an Elazar-to-Pinchas step that Sanhedrin 36a:8 lacks. Rabbeinu Chananel paraphrases without a name. Rav Acha son of Rava also carries a patronymic (Rava), which gives one more local parent placeholder there; it is not assumed to be the Rava of 36a:6.
findings.graph_effect: A later job should extend coverage to 36a:8-13. Record the 'אף אני אומר' attribution as a parallel-witness difference: Sanhedrin says Rav Adda bar Ahava, Gittin says Rav Acha son of Rava. Record Huna bar Natan's subordination to Rav Ashi as a stated social relation. Biblical figures are 'about' mentions in a comparison, not participants.

findings.claim: Nothing in the passage says either explainer was present at Rabbi's court. Evidence elsewhere about 'R. Hillel son of R. Volas' does not settle who he was. In Avodah Zarah 52b he speaks alone, answering a question about something Rabbi taught his son R. Shimon. Yerushalmi Kilayim 9:1 has 'רבי הלל בירבי וולס' whose garment went to 'רבי', printed in parentheses. Guggenheimer glosses that Rebbi as 'probably Rebbi (Jehudah Nesia)', not Yehuda HaNasi. Seder HaDorot gathers several name forms into one entry.

evidence.exact_quote: א"ר הילל בריה דרבי וולס לא נצרכה שיש לו בה שותפות
רִבִּי הִלֵּל בֵּירִבִּי וַולֶס הָיָה לוֹ בֶגֶד בִּשְׁלֹשִׁים רִיבּוֹא דֵינָר (וִיהֲבֵיהּ לְרִבִּי)
evidence.translation_by_this_dossier: Rebbi Hillel son of Rebbi Volas had a garment worth thirty myriad denars (and gave it to Rebbi).

evidence.exact_quote: Probably Rebbi (Jehudah Nesia) suspected the garment to contain the very expensive Egyptian byssus
ר' הלל בריה דר' וולס

findings.reasoning: A shared name does not establish identity. The explainers comment on Rav's report after the fact. Since the report is not theirs, it does not show that they attended or lived at the same time as Rabbi or Rav. The Yerushalmi's 'Rebbi' may be a later patriarch, according to Guggenheimer's note. If Rava is the well-known Amora, the two alternatives would be of very different periods, but the passage does not require resolving that.
findings.graph_effect: No presence, meeting or contemporaneity edges for Rabba son of Rava or R. Hillel son of R. Volas with Rabbi or Rav. Leave historical_compatibility of the attribution group as unknown. Any identity pack for R. Hillel b. R. Volas must weigh the Yerushalmi forms and Guggenheimer's 'Jehudah Nesia' gloss separately.
